============================================================
22. ANALYSIS OUTPUT STRUCTURE
============================================================

Use this exact structure in the final analysis:

1. Event verification
2. Data cutoff
3. Sources checked
4. Confirmed/projected starting goalies
5. Confirmed/projected lines, defensive pairings, scratches, and injuries
6. Rolling Last 5/10/15/20 team stats
7. Scoring, period, shot, xG, and possession profile
8. Goalie analysis
9. Special teams analysis
10. Schedule, rest, travel, and venue context
11. Head-to-head
12. Market-specific stats
13. Market context
14. Most likely outcome
15. Confidence level: Low / Medium / High
16. Key reasons supporting the pick
17. Key risks that could flip the pick
18. Final answer

============================================================
23. FINAL DECISION RULES
============================================================

FINAL DECISION RULES:
- Do not make a pick until starting goalies, lineups, injuries, scratches, and schedule spot are checked if available
- Confirm starting goalie, line combinations, defensive pairings, scratches, power-play roles, and injury/minute workload limits through official team reports, morning skate, and verified X/Twitter beat reporters before puck drop. Classify key players/goalies as CONFIRMED IN, CONFIRMED OUT, LIMITED/TOI RISK, PROJECTED, or UNKNOWN and adjust pace, shot volume, defensive quality, special teams, and period-specific projections.
- If starting goalies are unconfirmed, clearly state that the pick is pre-goalie/provisional
- If line combinations are unconfirmed, clearly state that the pick is pre-lineup/provisional
- If key injury/scratch information is missing, lower confidence
- Do not rely on one stat only
- Prioritise same-season and same-strength-state data over older data where possible
- Prioritise 5v5 xG%, high-danger chances, shot share, goalie quality, special teams, rest/travel, and lineup availability
- For totals, prioritise xGF/xGA, high-danger chances, goalie GSAx, special teams, shot volume, PDO, schedule fatigue, and empty-net context
- For moneyline, prioritise goalie edge, xG%/shot-share edge, special teams, injuries, rest/travel, and home-ice last-change advantage
- For puckline, prioritise goal differential, empty-net frequency, one-goal game profile, goalie edge, and third-period game state
- For first-period totals, prioritise early scoring, early shot/xG profile, starting goalie, and early penalty rate
- For player shots, prioritise line role, TOI, PP role, shot attempts, ixG, opponent shot allowance, and stat-keeper/home effect
- For player points/goals, prioritise active status, line role, PP role, individual xG, shooting regression, matchup, and goalie quality
- For player blocks, prioritise defensive pairing, PK role, opponent shot volume, and expected defensive-zone time
- For goalie saves, prioritise confirmed start, shots faced, opponent shot volume, team defence, and rest/workload
- Do not overweight H2H if goalies, lines, coaches, injuries, or team systems have changed
- Check pre-game and post-game coach/player press conference comments for tactical intent: forecheck pressure, defensive structure, line matching, goalie workload, power-play changes, shot-volume emphasis, and whether the team says it wants to play more aggressively or tighten defensively. Weight comments more when they align with morning-skate lines, scratches, goalie confirmation, travel/rest, and recent period splits; do not use them alone.
- If the evidence is mixed, say so
- If the data is weak or unavailable, lower confidence
- If key information is missing, state that the prediction is provisional
- Never call a pick "safe" or "guaranteed"
- Mark unavailable information as UNKNOWN





## AFL added learnings (2026-05-30)
- Marvel Stadium and other closed-roof AFL venues remove weather/wind/rain as variables; do not apply open-air scoring suppression. Treat conditions as neutral-to-fast and let team scoring profiles, injuries, and territory drive the total.
- AFL total-corridor cards (e.g. Over X / Under Y as a wide pair): a combined score inside the corridor cashes BOTH totals. Rank the wide Under first when both offenses are weak and the under has hit repeatedly in H2H, but do not assume the lower Over is safe if either side can be held to a very low score. Check each teams average COMBINED game total against the over line specifically (a team last in the league for combined game points can sit below the over line on its own).
- AFL favourite-line vs underdog-cushion: when the favourite is only modest and both teams are low-scoring grinders, keep the underdog cushion live rather than burying it; tight defensive H2H histories compress margins. Only rank the favourite cover high (and the cushion as bottom) when the underdog is heavily depleted on offence/defence (multiple key forwards/defenders out) so a comfortable favourite win is the cleanest path. Distinguish this from a true mismatch, where the favourite line AND a high total can both be underrated (ref: Sydney 170-Richmond 56 lesson).
- Cross-sport correlation rule (confirmed WNBA Atlanta-Portland and applied to AFL): when an underdog carries multiple key availability outs against a strong rebounding/star or in-form opponent, favourite-cover and a LOW total become correlated. Do not rank the favourite blowout as the bottom pick, and do not assume a low over is safe, because one offense can fully collapse and drag the total under both lines.
- AFL live halftime projection rule: a combined halftime total can be doubled as a first-pass full-game estimate, but it must be stress-tested against fourth-quarter comeback/fatigue scoring. Bulldogs-Collingwood sat at 81 combined at the main break (~162 projected), then finished at 190 after a 56-point fourth quarter; the low over won, the wide under lost, and the underdog cushion cashed despite the favourite winning. When a card pairs a wide Under with a mid Over, treat the Over and the underdog cushion as live swing items unless the underdog is truly outclassed or injured beyond repair.
- KBO over-first confirmation (SSG-Hanwha): when the projected band is 9-12 in a hitter-friendly park with a leaky home bullpen/strong home lineup, the Over (8) can clear by mid-game and the high Under (10) can bust early. Reinforces not defaulting to KBO unders when May run-environment and lineup/bullpen profiles point high.
- KBO settlement (SSG-Hanwha, final 13-10, total 23): the over-first / under-as-bottom read fully paid off as both bullpens leaked in a hitter-friendly Daejeon spot. Refinement on the SIDE ranking: I had Landers +1.5 above Eagles ML, but the stronger-lineup home team won outright by 3. Lesson - when the same high run-environment that drives the over also favours one team lineup, rank that team ML above the opponent cushion rather than defaulting the underdog +1.5 higher; the cushion only earns the higher slot when the favourite has real bullpen/lineup fragility, not when it is the side most likely to push the total up.

## AFL settlement learnings (2026-05-31, after Bulldogs-Collingwood 97-93)
- AFL roof/dry-deck total correction (HARD lesson, repeated): do NOT anchor a card on a low-scoring H2H average or a "league-worst scoring" tag when both lineups are healthy enough to score and conditions are benign (closed roof, or dry/sunny/light-wind open deck). Bulldogs-Collingwood produced 190 on a Marvel roof after I projected 170-184 and ranked the Under top - it lost, while the lower Over (166.5) I ranked third was the truest pick. Default to ranking the lower Over higher and treat a high Under as the safer total, not a low Under.
- AFL cushion-discipline rule (now burned TWICE - Collingwood +9.5 and the margin axis): never make the underdog/home +cushion the declared least-likely in a small/medium-line game between competitive teams. Tight AFL contests routinely deliver the cushion even when the favourite wins. Only bury a cushion when the underdog is genuinely outclassed/heavily depleted AND a comfortable favourite win is the cleanest path. When the cushion-holder is the HOME team in a near-even game, rank the cushion ABOVE the favourite line.
- Live-data integrity rule: weight user live corrections and a single reliable live source over slow aggregator feeds. In Bulldogs-Collingwood, stale ESPN/Sofascore data initially hid Collingwood's comeback (the user had to correct the live score); always re-verify a "final"-tagged feed that only shows two quarters of an AFL game - it is almost certainly a halftime/live state.
- GWS/Melbourne side correction: tight historical H2H and a good underdog ladder position should not override current form, defensive-class returns, and scoring-efficiency mismatch. GWS beat Melbourne by 49 despite losing inside 50s 62-46 because they dominated marks, uncontested possession, marks inside 50, and forward efficiency. For AFL side lines, separate territory volume from scoring quality; if the favourite can control possession and convert cleaner entries, the favourite cover can sit above the underdog cushion even when recent H2Hs were close.
- Alice Springs / Traeger Park context: dry hard desert deck with typically light winds favours open running football and scoring; territory and transition defence are decisive, which can favour a high-pressure travelling side even at the nominal home team's second home. Melbourne have a poor recent Traeger record, so "home ground" weighting must be tempered by actual venue results.

## AFL side-axis learnings (2026-05-31, after Melbourne-GWS 119-70)
- Cushion-discipline boundary (refined after back-to-back side-axis misses): the underdog +cushion is the live, do-not-bury side ONLY in near-even FORM matchups between healthy/competitive teams (e.g. Bulldogs-Collingwood, both mid-table and healthy). When the favourite is in dominant recent form AND the underdog is depleted AND H2H/ladder-form favours the favourite, the favourite BLOWOUT is a primary path - rank the favourite line ABOVE the underdog cushion. Melbourne-GWS proved this: a tight 3-game H2H (by 3/2/2) did NOT stop a 49-point GWS win because GWS were surging (166 pts the week before) and Melbourne were missing Lever.
- A tight historical H2H must NOT override current-form asymmetry. Recent close margins are a weak signal when one roster is surging and the other is decimated/just changed coach.
- Conditions are the key blowout switch: dry/benign decks (Marvel roof, sunny Traeger) ENABLE blowouts, so do not bury the strong favourite line there. Wet/windy decks (e.g. Optus in rain) COMPRESS margins, which genuinely supports the underdog cushion even against a strong favourite - this is the one setup where ranking the cushion above the favourite line is justified despite a roster mismatch. Always tie the side-axis ranking to the forecast, not just the rosters.
- When my own writeup names a specific scenario as a "risk" (e.g. "if GWS replicate their form, the cover cashes"), and that scenario is supported by current form + injuries + venue, treat it as a PRIMARY path, not a tail - rank accordingly instead of defaulting it to fourth.

## Side-axis learning (2026-05-31, after West Coast-Essendon 85-55, THIRD straight side-axis miss)
- THE STANDING WEAKNESS IS THE SIDE AXIS, NOT TOTALS. Three straight AFL cards nailed the totals corridor (190->both, 189->both, 140->both) but lost the bottom pick by burying the favourite/dominant side. Stop repeating this.
- Default rule: in a clear quality/health mismatch, rank the SUPERIOR team's cover HIGH (often #1) and the underdog cushion LOW. Do not let a stale favourable H2H, "they always keep it close" history, or margin-compressing weather demote the strong favourite cover - those factors only matter between evenly-matched, healthy teams.
- Crisis multiplier: when the underdog has multiple core players out AND coaching turmoil AND a poor record, the blowout is the PRIMARY path. Essendon (coach sacked, 4 core out, 1 win) lost by 30 in the wet despite owning the recent H2H; Melbourne (Lever out, vs a surging GWS) lost by 49 despite three straight tight H2H results.
- Cushion-discipline still applies ONLY to genuinely near-even FORM matchups of healthy teams (Bulldogs-Collingwood). Diagnose "near-even FORM" vs "mismatch" first, THEN choose whether the cushion or the favourite line ranks higher.
- Cross-sport application (basketball): a dominant league leader (e.g. Astana 28-4, 25-3 H2H, ~28-pt avg margin, elite D, home) should have its spread cover ranked at or near the top, with the underdog cushion as the declared least-likely.

## Match-context / decider learnings (2026-06-01, after Astana-Kaspiy Game 5 lost 87-89 OT)
- CLASSIFY MATCH CONTEXT FIRST, every card. Tag the game as regular-season / in-season-cup / play-in / playoff-series-game / WINNER-TAKE-ALL DECIDER before ranking. The framework changes by context.
- Winner-take-all / elimination games between closely-matched teams: (a) lean the TOTAL toward the series/season HIGH, not the average, and explicitly price OT risk - deciders produce empty-the-tank shootouts and foul-heavy late minutes (Astana-Kaspiy G5 hit 158 in regulation then 176 with OT vs a 146/121/150 prior pattern); (b) treat the SIDE as a near coin-flip and NEVER bury the underdog who already won games in the series or qualified for the final; (c) do NOT apply regular-season margin/PPG/H2H-blowout profiles to a one-game decider.
- The "back the dominant favourite cover" rule (from the AFL mismatch run) is REGULAR-SEASON QUALITY/HEALTH-MISMATCH ONLY. It does not transfer to knockouts, finals, or games where the favourite is missing a star.
- Reconcile the two recent lessons by decision tree: 1) Is it a knockout/decider? -> coin-flip side, total up, do not bury qualified underdog. 2) Else, is it a clear regular-season quality/health mismatch? -> back the superior team cover high. 3) Else (near-even healthy regular-season) -> cushion-discipline, rank by venue/form edge.
- WNBA phase-total note (Lynx-Mercury card): separate Q1 and 1H when the same matchup previously showed a controlled Q1 but second-quarter recovery. A strong defence can keep Q1 under live, while first-half over can still rank higher if team 1H averages, opponent defensive leakage, foul paths, or bench scoring point to an 85+ half. Do not package all unders together just because a star scorer is out.
- WNBA Lynx-Mercury settlement correction: the 1H Over was the right anchor, but Q1 control was wrong - the opener reached 57. In Commissioner's Cup/home-energy spots, do not assume elite defence automatically creates a slow Q1 when prior phase data, home pace, and available creators leave a fast-start path. The chat-facing ranking must match the logged ranking exactly.

## WNBA phase-total + process learnings (2026-06-01, after Lynx-Mercury 88-84, Q1 57 / 1H over)
- GRADE OF RECORD IS THE LOG. The logged Lynx-Mercury card led with 1H Over 84.5 (won) and graded 2-2 clean; a chat answer that inverted both halves to unders would have been 2-4. Always make the chat-presented ranking MATCH the logged ranking - never invert over/under direction between the answer and the log.
- What worked (REPEAT): weighting recent ACTUAL phase scores over season pace narratives. The May 12 H2H (Q1 39, half 86) and a ~86.3 combined 1H average correctly beat Minnesota's season "league-best defence" story; the 1H Over cashed. Recent same-matchup phase splits > season defence/pace ratings for phase totals.
- Collier/Juhasz OUT did NOT suppress Minnesota - they scored 35 in Q1. CONFIRMS: a star scorer's absence is not an automatic under signal; remaining starters absorb usage and pace can hold or rise.
- The clear miss was Q1 Under 42.5: opener hit 57. Do NOT assume a controlled Q1 when a home team plus in-season-cup/novelty energy can produce a track-meet start. For Q1 unders, require recent ACTUAL low Q1s from BOTH teams, not just season defence.
- Phase-total ranking sanity check: if season narrative says "under" but recent same-matchup actuals say "over," trust the recent actuals; and avoid stacking both phase options in the same direction unless recent actuals strongly agree.

=== FULL LOG RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT 2026-06-03 ===
Scope: review of the full prediction log through the latest 2026-06-03 entries. The log shows the model often finds plausible score corridors, but ranking calibration is the persistent weakness. Bottom-pick penalties are far more damaging than top-pick penalties, which means the fourth slot is too often being used for "contrary to the lean" instead of "requires the most things to go wrong."

GLOBAL WHAT WENT RIGHT:
- Best cards came from exact threshold arithmetic, not generic lean language. Examples: WNBA Portland-Golden State projected a 172 total and landed exactly 172; MLB and KBO middle-band totals often worked when the expected run cluster was named; T20 innings bands worked when powerplay, middle-overs, and death overs were separated.
- Phase separation works. Q1 under plus 1H over can both be right; powerplay under plus innings over can both be right; a high Q1 can still cool in Q2 but leave the first-half over live because the remaining requirement is small.
- Live corrections are strong when the model accepts new arithmetic. When a powerplay is 80/0 or a basketball Q1 is 56, pregame priors must be demoted immediately and the remaining-points requirement becomes the main input.
- Wide upper unders and middle-band totals work when collapse, pitcher/bowler control, defensive pressure, or one-team offensive failure is explicitly priced.
- Winner leans are better when anchored to current lineup depth, home/venue, and current form rather than old H2H alone.

GLOBAL WHAT WENT WRONG:
- Fourth-pick discipline is the biggest leak. Never put an outcome fourth if it lies inside the projected score band, if it is the direct complement of a thin top pick, or if normal variance can make it win.
- Stale anchors caused several bad cards. Multi-season H2H, old venue averages, and preview adjectives like "grind" or "defensive" must not outrank current-season scoring, last 2-3 games, current availability, and confirmed venue/conditions.
- Overcorrection after misses is a recurring error. A successful under lesson does not make the next similar game an under; a pitch-over correction does not make every venue an over. Rebuild the next card from current inputs.
- Side-axis ranking is weaker than total-axis ranking. The model often nails the scoring corridor but buries the wrong spread/cushion side. Diagnose side context separately from total context.
- Full-game and phase markets were sometimes blended. A late foul/OT/bullpen/garbage-time path can beat a full-game under even when early-phase unders were correct.
- Availability was sometimes treated one-way. A star out does not automatically mean under; usage can redistribute. Multiple defensive/frontcourt outs can make opponent overs and favourite covers more likely. Multiple offensive/creation outs can create one-team collapse and a favourite-low-total correlation.

MASTER DECISION HIERARCHY FOR FUTURE CARDS:
- First: classify context. Regular season, cup, friendly, playoff, elimination/decider, dead rubber, relegation/survival, rematch, same-series, or live state.
- Second: verify current source stack. Official schedule/venue, current lineups/starters/injury statuses, last 2-3 games, current-season scoring/pace/ratings, recent phase splits, and hourly/weather/venue state where relevant.
- Third: build the expected band. State the likely Q1/1H/full-game, powerplay/innings, inning/run, or half/goal band before ranking.
- Fourth: map every listed option to that band. If two options both win in the likely band, they should both rank high or middle. If an option only loses on a narrow threshold miss, it cannot be fourth.
- Fifth: stress-test the top and bottom picks. The top pick must survive the most obvious adverse path. The bottom pick must require multiple unlikely things or sit outside the current band. If not, rerank.
- Sixth: use live arithmetic when live. Recalculate from the actual score and exact remaining requirement; do not extrapolate labels like "regression" or "momentum" without the math.

BASKETBALL AND WNBA/NBA/NZNBL LEARNINGS:
- Treat Q1, Q2, 1H, 2H, and full-game totals as separate markets. Do not package all overs or all unders unless recent actual phase data supports the same direction in each phase.
- For Q1 unders, require recent actual low Q1 evidence from both teams or a strong tactical/lineup reason. Home/cup/novelty energy and early shooting can blow up a Q1 even when a strong defence exists.
- For 1H overs, Q2 recovery is a real path through bench scoring, fouls, opponent defensive slippage, or a favourite adjusting after first rotation.
- For 2H totals, price game state. A big lead can slow pace, but a low threshold can still clear through trailing-team urgency, bench pace, fouls, and ordinary scoring. Do not settle or log 2H add-ons without final score.
- Winner-take-all basketball deciders have fatter over and OT tails than series averages imply. Lean toward the series high, not the average, and treat the side as closer to a coin flip if both teams already won games in the series.
- NZNBL/NZ NBL: never anchor to multi-season H2H for phase totals. Use current-season pace/scoring and last 2-3 games first. The 2026 environment is high-scoring enough that stale "grind" H2H language can invert the card. Preview adjectives are low-weight unless confirmed by current phase scores.
- NZNBL live rule: if Q1 reaches the mid-50s, immediately rerank the first-half market from exact Q2 requirement. A high Q1 plus only 40-ish needed in Q2 makes the first-half over favoured unless injury/foul/bench evidence says otherwise.
- WNBA: strong defence can coexist with high totals if the opponent's defence is the weak link and both teams protect possessions well enough to create quality shots. Do not rank broad high unders first unless pace, shot quality, foul rate, and late-game paths all support it.
- Basketball side-vs-total split: a correct total read does not validate the side. Favourite cover rises when the underdog has multiple key outs or crisis context; underdog cushion rises in near-even healthy matchups and deciders.
- Quick-rematch rule (validated 2026-06-07 VBA Cantho-Hanoi): a recent same-matchup BLOWOUT does NOT guarantee a repeat margin or total. A 2-3 day rematch invites defensive adjustment by the prior loser and shooting regression by both sides. Do not anchor the projection to the blowout game; weight the slower/closer H2H points and explicitly model the tight, low-efficiency path. Same root family as the playoff "same-series totals can reverse" lesson, now confirmed for non-playoff rematches.
- Shooting-variance-league rule (VBA and similar low-3P% leagues): both offenses can shoot a game into the floor simultaneously (Cantho-Hanoi: 27% vs 4% from three -> 87-80, total 167 off a 196 prior), collapsing margin AND total together. Where league/team three-point variance is high, CAP both the favourite cover and the over, and keep the underdog cushion + unders ranked above a blowout narrative.
- Large-handicap top-pick gate: a double-digit-plus handicap (e.g. -21.5) is only a safe TOP pick when the gap is structural - talent chasm + opponent cannot score + favourite plays starters. A single prior blowout is NOT structural. Otherwise treat the large line as a cover risk, not an anchor, and rank the cushion adjacent.
- Full-total 2H-blowout tail rule, added 2026-06-25 from Chicago 101, Portland 78 (Q1 43, 1H 85, full 179): phase unders and the full total are SEPARATE axes. The Q1 Under 44.5 (43) and 1H Under 88.5 (85) both won, but the Full Under 171.5 LOST at 179 because a healthier favourite (Chicago) pulled away with a 55-point second half against a depleted opponent (Portland missing multiple guards). When a fitter favourite faces a star-thinned/depleted opponent, the full total carries a live one-sided-blowout tail even off a low first half; do NOT rank a full under above the full over on the strength of low early-phase scoring alone. Mirror of the NZNBL "high-scoring 2H can clear a low-1H game" family.
- WNBA elite-home-defense ANCHOR rule, added 2026-06-25 from Golden State 77, Atlanta Dream 66 (Q1 40, 1H 71, full 143): when a high-pace road offense (Atlanta L5 194 full avg) visits a slow, league-best home defense (Golden State 79.4 opp PPG), ANCHOR the total to the home defense's opponent-PPG number, NOT the visitor's recent scoring spike. I stacked all three overs (full 165.5, 1H 81.5, Q1 40.5) at the top and all three LOST while all three unders won; the Dream were held to 66 (9 in Q2). Reinforced because Atlanta was also missing a frontcourt piece (Brionna Jones), so role concentration could not sustain the L5 pace against elite half-court defense. This is the mirror of the Aces-Storm do-not-default-to-unders failure: the COMBINED environment governs, and here the elite defensive end was the dominant driver. Direction test: when one side owns an elite, slow, top-of-league defense and the other side's offense is missing a key scorer, lean the unders and keep over/under no wider than adjacent unless recent same-matchup phase data clearly clears the line.

CRICKET/T20/ODI LEARNINGS:
- Live pitch report, boundary size, toss, innings pressure, and current batting XI outrank venue averages and broad season form.
- Separate powerplay and innings. A 60-65 powerplay can coexist with a 220+ innings through middle/death acceleration, and a 70+ powerplay can still be followed by a capped innings if wickets and spin pressure arrive.
- Modest powerplay overs must not be buried when the surface is flat, boundaries are short, and one opener has an attacking route, even if new-ball names are strong.
- Broad high powerplay unders must not be buried either if the expected band is low/mid-60s. Put the expected middle band ahead of emotional over/under reactions.
- Current live arithmetic overrides pregame. If the side is 80/0 after 6 or 150+ before the 12th on a flat surface, innings-over probability changes immediately.
- Do not waste two of four ranked items on exact opposites at the same threshold unless the user only provided those. If exact opposites are unavoidable, state that the card is structurally 2-2 and that the value is only in ranking direction.
- ODI/long-format innings: prior collapse plus current spin/new-ball matchup can beat venue averages. But first-5 and innings totals need separate logic because a smooth first 5 can still become a sub-par innings once spin enters.

MLB/KBO/NPB BASEBALL LEARNINGS:
- Overlapping totals require exact cluster handling. Over 7 and Under 9 can both win at 8; Over 8.5 and Under 11 can both fit a 9-10 run band. Do not rank a modest over fourth when it is inside the projected cluster.
- Run cushions are not generic. A +1.5 is live in low/middle scoring games and should not be buried just because the other starter has an edge. Conversely, do not overcorrect and bury a strong favourite moneyline when ordinary win paths remain.
- MLB starter labels matter: opener/bullpen-game, return sample, pitch count, command, handedness, and bullpen exposure must be checked before side/under ranking.
- MLB quality-starter override: when one or both starters are in genuine current form, do not push a modest full-game over above safer run cushions solely because of warm weather, hitter-friendly park factors, or bullpen-game narratives. A starter who can work 6-7 efficient innings can shrink bullpen exposure enough for a 4-1/4-2/4-3 under even when the opponent offense looks strong on season averages.
- MLB homer-friendly parks and power lineups need an ace-damage path. Elite starting pitching can still allow a total to clear through homers, walks, errors, and bullpen innings.
- KBO: do not default to unders. Warm weather, hitter-friendly parks, strong lineups, and bullpen volatility can make 10-13 runs ordinary. At Daegu especially, default the total higher unless both starters are elite and in-form.
- KBO favourites: do not lay -1.5 by default. One-run wins are common even for correct winner reads. Prefer moneyline logic or the opponent +2.5/+1.5 when the run band is close.
- NPB: model lower run environment, Central League pitcher spot where applicable, draw/extra-inning rules, and both +1.5 cushions in pitching duels. Do not bury an opponent ML when the preferred side is anchored mainly to a fragile starter edge.
- Cold-offense +1.5 fade, added 2026-06-25 from San Diego 5, Atlanta 2 (Braves swept): a +1.5 run-line cushion is NOT safe when the cushioned team's offense is cold AND missing its primary bat. Atlanta (no Acuna, slumping) was given Braves +1.5 at the top largely on Perez's starter edge; the card's own #1 stress test predicted the failure and it happened — Atlanta scored 2, the "risky replacement" opposing starter (Sears) won his debut, and the Braves lost by 3. RULE: downgrade the run-line cushion of a star-thinned, slumping lineup even when it holds the nominal starter edge; the opponent's shaky replacement starter is not a reason to trust your cushion if your own offense cannot put up runs. Separate "starter edge" from "can this lineup actually score."
- Returning-ace exact-winner caution, added 2026-06-25 from Yankees 4, Tigers 2 (Skubal tied a career high with 3 HRs allowed): do not anchor an exact-winner pick to a returning/reputation ace when the opposing lineup has already shown early power and the only live run paths are over-the-fence. The live Goldschmidt HR correctly moved Yankees +1.5 to #1 (won outright) and the wind-in Comerica under held at 6, but the Detroit winner lean on Skubal failed — a sharp ace (9 K, 1 non-HR hit) still surrendered three homers because a wind-in note does not suppress pull-power. HRs beat park-suppression narratives; keep the opponent ML live when they have shown HR ceiling.

- WNBA DO-NOT-DEFAULT-TO-UNDERS, REINFORCED (2026-06-08 Aces 101-91 Storm, full directional totals failure). I stacked all three unders (full 166.5, 1H 82.5, Q1 41.5) above all three overs because Storm had the league-WORST offense (75 ppg) and I expected a blowout with garbage-time slowdown. ALL THREE OVERS WON (192 total, Q1 48, HT 93). THREE compounding errors: (1) a team's poor SEASON offense does not cap a single GAME - Storm scored 91, well above their 75 average, because a weaker team chasing in an uptempo game still scores; (2) it was a 10-point NON-BLOWOUT, so starters stayed on and there was no garbage-time suppression - do not assume "big favourite = blowout = under" when the favourite is an uptempo offense that keeps scoring; (3) the dominant total driver was the FAVOURITE'S PACE, not the underdog's weakness - an elite uptempo offense (Aces 89->101, Wilson 34, Young 29) lifts the COMBINED environment regardless of the opponent. FIX: in WNBA, anchor the total to the COMBINED pace/scoring environment and the favourite's offensive tempo FIRST; only lean under when BOTH teams are genuinely low-pace/low-efficiency or a true blowout with deep bench minutes is likely. Never stack all unders above all overs off one team's bad season offense - keep over/under adjacent (coinflip) unless the combined environment clearly points one way. A 15.5-point favourite line does NOT imply a garbage-time under.

=== PRE-RANK TOTALS-DIRECTION GATE (anti-mistake checklist, ADDED 2026-06-09 after the Aces 101-91 Storm all-unders failure) ===
PURPOSE: totals-direction is the single most recurring ranking leak in the log (overs won in uptempo/non-blowout spots e.g. Aces-Storm 192, NZNBL Q1 56, Lynx-Mercury Q1 57; unders won in genuine low-pace/blowout/bowler-friendly spots e.g. AFL 158, Mercury-Storm Q4 33). The error is almost always COMMITTING TO ONE DIRECTION OFF A SINGLE FACTOR. Before ranking ANY over/under (full, half, quarter, innings, or powerplay), run these gates IN ORDER and write the answer:

1. WRITE YOUR PROJECTED NUMBER FIRST, then compare to the line. Only lean strongly if the gap is > ~1 scoring unit (1 run-cluster / ~3-4 basketball pts / ~0.5 goals). If the projection sits ON or within ~1 unit of the line, it is a COINFLIP - rank over/under ADJACENT in the middle and do NOT stack one direction.

2. ANCHOR TO THE COMBINED ENVIRONMENT + THE FAVOURITE'S PACE/TEMPO, NOT ONE TEAM'S WEAKNESS. An elite uptempo offense lifts the combined total regardless of how bad the opponent is (Aces 89->101). A hitter park / fast pace / flat deck / weak BOTH-team defense is an OVER driver even with one weak unit. Identify the single dominant scoring driver and weight it above narrative adjectives ("grind","defensive","worst offense").

3. SEASON AVERAGE != SINGLE-GAME CEILING. A team's league-worst SEASON offense does not cap a single GAME - they can and do post well above their average (Storm 75 avg -> 91), especially chasing in a fast game. Use season figures as a centre, never a ceiling/floor.

4. BLOWOUT != UNDER unless DEEP BENCH MINUTES ARE ACTUALLY LIKELY. A big handicap line does NOT imply garbage-time suppression. Check the realistic margin: a single-digit / ~10-pt game keeps starters on and scoring high. Only apply the garbage-time-under discount when a true 20+ runaway with emptied benches is the base case.

5. DECOUPLE SIDE FROM TOTAL. Who wins and by how much is a SEPARATE axis from how many combined points/runs. A comfortable favourite win frequently coexists with an OVER (favourite scores a lot; opponent still scores). Never infer the total direction from the handicap/winner pick.

6. PHASE-SPECIFIC VOLATILITY. Q1/first-powerplay is the highest-variance phase: a feeling-out UNDER requires recent ACTUAL low Q1s/PPs from BOTH sides; home/novelty/uptempo energy blows up early phases (Lynx-Mercury Q1 57 vs 42.5; NZNBL Q1 56). Half/2H/full are more stable. So for UNDERS rank the Q1/PP under as the WEAKEST (most volatile) under; for OVERS the Q1/PP over can be the STRONGEST over. Mirror complements symmetrically around the middle.

7. SPORT-SPECIFIC OVERRIDES THAT FLIP DIRECTION:
   - WNBA/NBA: do NOT default to unders; pace + the favourite's tempo dominate. [Aces-Storm]
   - KBO/MLB: hitter parks (Daegu/Sajik), weak bullpens, and warm weather push OVER; a genuine in-form quality starter pushes UNDER. Don't assume "bullpen game = over" (a fresh long reliever can suppress). [Giants-Cubs]
   - Cricket: venue par is a GUIDE not a shield; ADJUST for attack strength (weakened pace = higher ceiling), pitch (green/flat), and the toss/innings order; live powerplay overrides the pregame under once a side is 25+ before 5 overs. [NED-USA; AUS-BAN with no Starc/Cummins/Hazlewood]
   - Soccer mismatch friendly: total leans OVER 2.5 (favourite 2-3 + late consolation); corners run UNDER. [Rules P/Q]

8. CHECK CONDITIONS AT REQUEST TIME: weather/roof, rain/DLS, lineups/injuries (a missing scorer lowers, a returning one raises), rest/back-to-back, and motivation/match-context (Commissioner's Cup / finals = real intensity, dead rubber = looser). Tie weather only to the actual game window.

9. FINAL CONSISTENCY CHECK: if you have ranked ALL unders above ALL overs (or vice versa) across multiple correlated markets, STOP and re-justify - that is the exact shape of the Aces-Storm failure. It is only correct when one direction is genuinely favoured on gates 1-8; if any market is a coinflip, its over/under must sit adjacent, not stacked.

AFL LEARNINGS:
- AFL total corridors have been better than side rankings. Keep building 130-150, 166-190, 183-202 type corridors, but do not let that corridor decide the handicap.
- Side decision tree: if near-even and healthy, respect the underdog cushion. If one side is in crisis, depleted, or clearly outclassed, rank the favourite cover high even if old H2H was close. If it is a decider/final-like spot, do not automatically import the regular-season mismatch rule.
- Weather only matters if it affects the actual match window or surface. Do not use whole-day showers when rain is after the game. Dry/roof/benign decks enable scoring surges and blowouts.
- Quarter-by-quarter control matters. A team can trail through 3QT and still cover through a dominant final quarter; a halftime total can be beaten by late comeback/fatigue scoring.

SOCCER LEARNINGS:
- For extreme mismatch friendlies or top-10 vs sub-100 profiles with recent rout form, overs can be the true safest path. Do not treat a generic under as safe just because friendlies can be experimental.
- For first-half goal overlaps, map the shared winning scores. Over 0.5 and Under 2.5 both win at 1-2 goals; Under 1.5 and Over 0.5 both win only at exactly one goal. Compare 0-0 risk against 2+ risk using current XIs and recent defensive form.
- Stale H2H halftime scores are weak when current XIs add multiple attacking/transition players or current defences are conceding heavily.
- MISMATCH-FRIENDLY TOTAL-GOALS LEANS OVER 2.5 (high priority, 3-for-3 validated 2026-06-05/08: Tajikistan 3-1 India, Netherlands 2-1 Uzbekistan, France 3-1 Northern Ireland - ALL three cleared 2.5). The mechanism is a DOUBLE driver: (a) the stronger side scores 2-3 through quality/penalties/defensive errors, and (b) the weaker side very frequently grabs a LATE CONSOLATION (India 89', Uzbekistan 90+2', NI 64'), pushing a 2-0/3-0 into 3-1/2-1. NEVER bottom-rank Combined Total Over 2.5 in a clear mismatch friendly, and do not default the total to the Under - lean Over 2.5 or at worst keep Over/Under adjacent in the middle. A friendly Under 2.5 is only justified when the weaker side has a robust clean-sheet/offensive-failure case AND the favourite is misfiring; even then keep it a modest lean (the NED Under lean lost on late goals despite a tight 1-0 first hour).
- MISMATCH-FRIENDLY CORNERS RUN LOW - DEFAULT UNDER (high priority, 3-for-3 validated: Tajikistan-India 3 total corners, NED-Uzbekistan 6, France-NI 6 - all well under 8.5/9.5). Territorial/possession dominance does NOT convert to corners in friendlies: even France's 72.5% possession + 27 shots produced only 5 corners. Deep blocks clear long and concede throw-ins/goal-kicks; lower intensity and mass substitutions kill sustained pressure. Rank Combined Corners Under 9.5 (or 8.5) ABOVE Corners Over in friendlies unless there is specific high-corner evidence. CONTRAST - competitive matches differ: in Liechtenstein 0-2 Cyprus (a meaningful qualifier) the corner total cleared 9.5 from the bottom slot, so a dominant side CAN clear corner overs when the match matters. Do not import the friendly-under corner read into a competitive/knockout fixture, and vice versa.
- MISMATCH-FRIENDLY 1H OVER 0.5 IS A RELIABLE #1 / 1H UNDER 0.5 A RELIABLE BOTTOM (validated repeatedly: every recent mismatch friendly had at least one first-half goal, all 1-0 at the break). A first-choice favourite almost always scores before half against a weak side; rank 1H Over 0.5 the strongest pick and 1H Under 0.5 the genuine least-likely bottom. This is the most consistently-correct soccer leg in the log - keep doing it.
- WEAKER-SIDE LATE-CONSOLATION PATTERN (cross-cutting): in lopsided games the trailing side scores disproportionately in the final ~15 minutes (subs, favourite easing off, tiring lines, set pieces, penalties). Price this explicitly into total-goals overs and into any "clean sheet"/winning-margin read - a 2-0 cruise frequently becomes 2-1/3-1.
- MUST-WIN vs CAN-DRAW final-group nuance, added 2026-06-25 from South Africa 1-0 South Korea: the "non-loss / double-chance above exact winner" rule applies ONLY when the projected band genuinely centres on the draw. Here I ranked "South Korea or Draw" at ~74% because a draw qualified Korea and Son was a bench lever, but South Africa (who HAD to win) out-shot and out-territoried them (10 shots/3 SOT/4 corners by halftime) and won 1-0 to reach the knockouts for the first time. RULE: when the team that only needs a draw is being out-chanced by a desperate must-win side with real creation, do NOT treat the can-draw team's non-loss as a high-70s safety — drop it toward a coin flip and let the must-win team's pressure (and a 1-0 path) carry real weight. The low-scoring shape can still be captured separately via the favourite/contender team-total Under (TT Under 1.5 won here). Motivation asymmetry can override draw-utility when the chance-creation gap favours the must-win side.

RANKING AND LOGGING RULES GOING FORWARD:
- Before answering any new card, sweep pending logs and settle only what reliable sources verify. If final score is unavailable, carry the item as pending without inventing the grade.
- Do not leave superseded partial-settlement duplicate rows once a final grade-of-record row exists. Update pending count after cleanup.
- For every card, write the likely band and the "bottom-pick failure test" before final ranking: "Can the fourth pick win by an ordinary path?" If yes, it is not fourth.
- For every top pick, write the "top-pick stress test": injury, weather, pace, bullpen, foul/OT, late surge, or one-team collapse path most likely to beat it. If that path is common in the log, reduce confidence or rerank.
- For every sport, prefer current-season and current-match information over old H2H. Old H2H is a tiebreaker, not an anchor, unless the same cores, venue, and tactical context still match.

=== VALIDATED RULES REGISTRY (consolidated 2026-06-07) ===
This registry replaces the former dated LEARNINGS UPDATE / PROCESS IMPROVEMENTS / FULL-LOG AUDIT example-blocks. Each line is one validated rule with its compact example citation. The GENERAL form of most of these lives in the MASTER DECISION HIERARCHY / sport LEARNINGS above and the DISTILLED MASTER PRINCIPLES below; this registry preserves the example-grounded provenance without the prose duplication. Live calibration counts are maintained in the universal core (top of file) and PREDICTION_RESULTS_LOG.md.

RANKING ARCHITECTURE (the dominant edge):
- Bottom-slot (#4) is the single biggest leak: across the audited log the #4 least-likely pick won ~47% while top picks won ~88%. Spend the most effort proving #4 is genuinely <~30% with the most failure paths. [FULL-LOG AUDIT 121 cards, historical snapshot - current counts top-of-file]
- Complementary-pair trap: when #4 is the Over/Under (or +X/-X) complement of a line your central estimate sits near, it is a forced ~coinflip; flag "no genuine least-likely outcome" and avoid confident fade language. [KBO Over 10.5 buried #4 won; validated on Philippines 5-1 Guam clean 2-2]
- Overs are underrated at the bottom: if expected total is within ~1 scoring unit of the line, rank over/under adjacent in the middle, never over-at-#4. Lean over more in high-variance setups (weak/unproven starters, weak defenses, fast pace, hitter parks). [NZ NBL Over 95.5; KBO Over 10.5]
- Chat-vs-log consistency is a grade-changing failure: the logged ranking is the grade of record; present the EXACT same order in chat, never invert direction. If a logged row exists, grade/use it - do not re-rank from scratch. [WNBA Tempo@Liberty 2-2 vs would-be 2-4]
- Grade by confidence: bottom-two losing is expected (half-weight, no introspection); a #1 loss or #4 win is full-weight and forces a written rule change. [CARD GRADING WEIGHT RULE]

TOTALS / ANCHORING:
- Anchor totals to CURRENT-SEASON pace/PPG + last 2-3 actual games FIRST; multi-season H2H and preview adjectives ("grind","defensive","two-way") are context only, never the anchor. [NZ NBL Auckland-Canterbury: stale 2019-25 H2H under blew up, live Q1 hit 56]
- Opponent-adjust recent scoring before using it: low scores vs strong foes understate the ceiling vs a minnow; high scores vs minnows overstate it vs a peer. [Philippines (1,1,1 vs strong sides) -> 5-1 over Guam; Morocco 8-0 mismatch overs]
- Anchor to the COMBINED scoring environment, not one team pace label: a low line vs a high expected environment = lean over; high line vs a modest matchup = lean under. [WNBA POR@GSV exact 172 call; weak-defense opponent makes half/2H overs right]
- A comfortable favorite win and an over are NOT contradictory when the opponent weakest dimension is defense. [GSV won by 18 AND total 172]

PHASE SEPARATION:
- Treat Q1, 1H, 2H, full as separate markets; do not package all overs/unders unless recent ACTUAL phase data agrees. Q1 is the feeling-out quarter (~23-25% of game) and leans slightly under even when the half leans over - "controlled Q1 then Q2 explosion" is bankable. [POR@GSV Q1 41 / half 92]
- Q1 unders require recent ACTUAL low Q1s from BOTH teams; home/cup/novelty energy and fast-tempo teams blow up Q1 even with a strong defense. [WNBA Lynx-Mercury Q1 57 vs Under 42.5 miss]
- 1H/2H overs are more stable than single-quarter bets; when both point the same way rank the half/2H leg above the Q1 leg. [POR@GSV]
- Cricket: separate powerplay/middle/death and first-5/innings; a smooth phase can still become a sub-par innings once spin enters, and a modest powerplay over is live on flat decks/short boundaries. [AUS-PAK]

SIDE / MARGIN (independent of total):
- A correct total does not validate the side. Project margin from efficiency-differential x pace vs COMPARABLE-quality opponents, not "who looks better." [WNBA 90-84 proj vs 95-77 actual; AFL handicap misses]
- Margin is bimodal and both tails get misjudged: a real favorite edge (home+matchup+form) -> project a WIDER margin and the cover can correlate with the over; near-even healthy games -> respect the underdog cushion. [AFL West Coast -12.5; North-Fremantle by 124]
- Low projected totals raise the value of the underdog +cushion (each score is a bigger share of margin); do not bury +1.5/+cushion or a small-spread dog in a 5-8 run / low-total band. [MLB Dodgers-DBacks +1.5; AFL sub-170 Port -6.5 lost by hook]
- New high-usage creator/import -> re-rate the team side/winner ceiling immediately even if old scoring still informs the total. [NZ NBL Hawks-Giants]
- Do not fade a winless-away record when the opponent is also a weak home team with a bad defense. [Hawks-Giants: Hawkes Bay allowed 97.6 PPG]

SPORT-SPECIFIC SIDE/TOTAL:
- KBO: do NOT lay -1.5 by default (one-run wins common) - prefer ML or dog +1.5/+2.5; at Daegu/hitter parks default the total UP unless BOTH starters are elite/in-form. [Samsung 8-7 NC; KBO LG@KT dog +1.5 validated]
- MLB: a quality starter is an UNDER input, not a universal dominant force - model the favorite offense and late bullpen innings separately from the ace first 6-7. A pitching-edge favorite can win by 2-3 via run prevention, so its +1.5 is safe and the OPPONENT +1.5 is the real risk. [Marlins 4-1 Nationals; Padres-Phillies; Wheeler 7IP but 6 runs scored]
- MLB starter-readiness gate: a return-from-injury/blister start cannot be a normal current-form edge without a command/readiness discount. [Cabrera 8ER/3.2IP; Giants-Cubs]
- Soccer mismatch friendlies: for top-tier vs leaky minnow with rout form, 1H Over 0.5 and full Over 2.5 can both be safest; the genuine fades are 1H Under 0.5 and Total Under 2.5. Low corner volume does NOT prove low goals, and corners themselves run LOW in friendlies (default Corners Under). Total Over 2.5 is 3-for-3 in recent mismatch friendlies via favourite 2-3 goals + weaker-side LATE CONSOLATION; never bottom-rank Over 2.5. Corner Over is the friendly trap (lost as #2 and #3). Competitive matches differ - a dominant side CAN clear corner Over there. [Morocco 8-0; Tajikistan 3-1 India (3 corners); NED 2-1 Uzbekistan (6 corners); France 3-1 NI (6 corners); Liechtenstein 0-2 Cyprus corner Over cleared in a competitive qualifier]
- World Cup group-opener mismatch caution, added 2026-06-16 from Spain 0-0 Cape Verde: do not import the friendly/clear-mismatch 1H Over 0.5 and Over 2.5 ladder automatically into a tournament opener when the underdog's best trait is defensive organization and the favourite starts with control midfielders rather than maximum wide pace. Spain started Rodri/Pedri/Fabian with Lamine Yamal, Nico Williams and Olmo on the bench, failed to score before halftime, and drew 0-0. In this setup, Under 3.5 and Under 2.5 deserve real protection until confirmed lineups or first-15 live pressure show repeated high-quality entries. Class gap plus debutant status is not enough by itself.
- AFL: build total corridors (130-150 / 166-190 / 183-202) but do not let the corridor decide the handicap; a quasi-home/interstate game can function as the favorite home edge. [North-Fremantle Bunbury]

LIVE / SETTLEMENT / SOURCES:
- Never finalize a side/run-line/handicap from a mid-inning or mid-period snapshot - late rallies flip margins; settle sides ONLY from the official final. [KBO LG@KT: mid-9th 7-4 projected 2-4, final 7-6 flipped top pick to a win]
- Live questions override the pregame model: recompute from exact remaining requirement (points/runs/goals/corners), time left, pace, foul/bonus/bench state. Do not extrapolate "momentum/regression" without the math.
- Settle completed PHASE markets from a later score that mathematically proves the threshold even without an exact milestone (scoring is monotonic). [PAK first-5 Under 26.5 from 23/1 after 6]
- Source hierarchy: use official league boxes (e.g. eng.koreabaseball.com, FIBA LiveStats, ESPN gameId pages) over aggregator live-renders, which stay stale/conflict; cross-check final/HT across 2 sources. WebFetch is often 403 (ESPNcricinfo, flashscore, sofascore, mykbostats) - capture phase splits live where possible. [KBO LG@KT aggregator conflict]
- Void/canceled fixtures are ungraded - never grade from a 0-0 placeholder or abandoned shell; tag VOID. [Equatorial Guinea-Burundi]
- Confirm fixture identity (date, local kickoff, venue, competition tier) before settling when teams have multiple fixtures in a window or parallel Rapid/main leagues. [Tajikistan-India June 5 vs 9; NZNBL Rapid vs main]

################################################################
SYNTHESIZED META-PRINCIPLES (2026-06-04)
Distilled from the full lesson corpus + 121 settled cards in the results log.
These are the HIGHER-ORDER patterns behind the individual lessons. Apply these first.
################################################################

PRINCIPLE 1 - THE #4 SLOT IS THE DOMINANT LEAK, AND THE CAUSE IS ALWAYS THE SAME: a genuinely LIVE outcome was ranked as "least likely."
Evidence: bottom-pick penalties recur across MI/LSG (PP Over), Rangers/Yankees (Over 7.5), LSG/RCB (PP Over), PBKS/DC (PP Over), Pistons/Cavs (1Q Under), TWolves/Spurs (1H Under), WNBA Sea/Tor (1Q Over), Rockies/Phillies (favorite ML), Braves/Dodgers (home +1.5). Adjusted record is LOSING (~.484) almost entirely because of this.
THE THREE THINGS I WRONGLY BURY AT #4 (memorize these):
  (a) A modest OVER when the scoring mechanism is live - cricket powerplay/innings over on a confirmed batting pitch; MLB over when starter AND bullpen are both weak; basketball Q1/1H over in a mismatch or shootout.
  (b) A favorite's WIN / no-cushion ML - a home/quality favorite's ordinary win path is rarely <30%.
  (c) The "slow-start" UNDER (Q1/1H under) when the actual game opened below the line.
RULE: the #4 pick must clear a "genuinely <30% AND most failure paths" test. If it is any of (a)/(b)/(c) above, it almost certainly does NOT belong at #4. When no option is truly <30% (overlapping totals, two +1.5 cushions), SAY SO and cap bottom confidence.

PRINCIPLE 2 - CURRENT/LIVE STATE ALWAYS BEATS HISTORICAL AVERAGE. The single most repeated correction across every sport.
Hierarchy (highest to lowest weight): live in-game arithmetic > confirmed lineups/starters/scratches + live pitch/weather report > current-season form & last 3-5 games > venue/season averages > multi-season H2H.
Manifestations: cricket live pitch report > venue average (Wankhede/Jaipur/Chepauk/Dharamshala overs); live score math overrides pregame bands (80/0 after 6 -> over; 56-pt Q1 -> 1H over); current XIs/transition forwards > stale H2H halves; NZ NBL stale-H2H blowup. NEVER anchor a total to a multi-season average.

PRINCIPLE 3 - PHASE SEPARATION IS A REAL, REPEATABLE EDGE (the top-of-card process that works). Keep it.
- Always model Q1 vs 1H vs full (and cricket PP vs innings, AFL quarters, MLB innings/bullpen-entry) SEPARATELY; never extrapolate one from another.
- Sub-rule that keeps winning: the 1H OVER usually outranks the Q1 OVER, because Q2 provides bench/foul/recovery scoring even if Q1 starts controlled (WNBA, Euro, Japan, NBA cards repeatedly).
- Sub-rule that keeps BURNING me: do NOT rank a Q1 UNDER above a Q1 OVER when the half thesis is "strong offense/mismatch" - in those, Q1 and 1H both tend to clear the over (Olympiacos 35-pt Q1, Bnei Herzliya, Magnolia, Pistons/Cavs). Q1 unders are fragile; a single ordinary 24-22 opening quarter beats a 45.5-type Q1 under.

PRINCIPLE 4 - TOTALS ARE DRIVEN BY THE DOMINANT FORCE, NOT A SECONDARY NARRATIVE.
- A QUALITY starter, strong defense, or elite rim protection is an UNDER input, not an automatic lean. It becomes the dominant force only when the opponent, venue, availability, bullpen/bench, and damage-path checks agree (Marlins/Meyer 5-run game; CSK spin control; Spurs Game-1 1H under). In hitter-friendly parks against power lineups, keep the over live.
- BOTH starters weak/short (opener/bullpen game) OR a confirmed flat/short-boundary pitch OR starter+bullpen weakness AGREE -> lean OVER, and do not bury the modest over (Twins/Nats over; cricket batting pitches).
- Do not let a single sub-narrative (one pitcher's poor form, "bullpen game," playoff "should be tight") override the dominant force. Classify openers/bulk starters correctly and model the bullpen innings explicitly.

PRINCIPLE 5 - MARGIN IS BIMODAL AND I MISJUDGE BOTH TAILS.
- A pitching-edge / talent-mismatch FAVORITE can win by 3+ via RUN/SCORE PREVENTION even with a modest offense -> its +1.5/ML is safe, the OPPONENT +1.5 is the real risk; do NOT assume "weak favorite offense = close game" (Marlins 4-1; AFL favorites).
- Conversely, DEPLETED teams or EXTREME conditions (Darwin heat/humidity, roof-closed parks, key ball-user out) score far BELOW the modeled band -> totals can fall well under (Gold Coast Darwin games landed 129-146 vs 181-198 model).
- Always tie weather to the actual match window, and price overtime (basketball) and the late-blowout scoring tail explicitly.

PRINCIPLE 6 - SIDE AND TOTAL ARE INDEPENDENT AXES; getting one right does not validate the other, and CONTEXT can flip the side while the total holds.
- Repeatedly the total was right but the side wrong, or vice-versa (Astros/Reds, Beer Sheva/Netanya, title-clinch rematches).
- Motivation/context matters: relegation/elimination urgency keeps a motivated-underdog cushion live; consolation/dead-rubber games open looser (over); a mathematically-safe favorite plays with less resistance. Price 4th-quarter/late response capacity separately from early-phase scoring.

PRINCIPLE 7 - CALIBRATION REALITY: top picks hit ~88%, bottom picks hit ~47%.
The top-of-card process (high-threshold unders, cushioned favorite/home side, half-over off strong offense, live-evidence anchoring) is SOUND - keep it. The entire edge to be gained is at the BOTTOM. Spend the most analytical effort on slot #4 and slot #3, not slot #1.

OPERATING SEQUENCE (apply every card): (1) live/current state first; (2) separate phases; (3) find the dominant force for the total; (4) project margin for BOTH tails; (5) build the ranking; (6) STRESS-TEST #4 against Principle 1 (a/b/c) before committing; (7) match the chat ranking to the logged ranking exactly.

A 2-3 day rematch invites defensive adjustment by the loser and shooting regression by both sides. === LEARNINGS UPDATE 2026-06-07 (AFL Sydney 97-101 St Kilda: mismatch-trap pregame, live override rescued) ===
RESULT: St Kilda 101 def Sydney 97 by 4 (combined 198), St Kilda led wire-to-wire. PREGAME card graded 2-4 (Swans -9.5 top LOST, St Kilda +9.5 bottom WON - both penalties); LIVE re-rank graded 2-2 with the top (St Kilda +9.5) winning and bottom (Swans -9.5) losing.
TRAP-AVERAGE RULE (new, high priority): do NOT import a favourite's "average margin vs sides ranked 11-18 / vs lower half" onto a mid-table opponent with finals-level talent. Sydney's 94-pt avg margin came vs cellar sides; St Kilda were 5-7 but well above cellar quality, so that number massively overstated the expected margin and wrongly anchored Swans -9.5 as the top pick. Opponent-class-adjust the margin stat before using it, exactly as totals must be opponent-adjusted.
RETURNING-STARS RE-RATE RULE (new): when a struggling side regains MULTIPLE elite players in the same week (St Kilda: Wanganeen-Milera back from 4 wks + Liam Ryan back from 5 wks), re-rate BOTH the side and the total upward immediately. Recent suppressed scores were recorded WITHOUT those players and understate the team - St Kilda had been held goalless in a half vs Hawthorn yet kicked 11 goals in the first half here. This is the availability-adjustment twin of the opponent-adjustment rule and applies to side AND total, not just total.
LIVE-OVERRIDE VALIDATED (keep doing): quarter-by-quarter recomputation rescued the card. The side flipped correctly (Swans -9.5 from pregame #1 to live #4) and the total flipped Over->Under after Q3 produced only 34 combined (per-qtr combined 59-75-34-30). Recompute the total every quarter from the exact remaining requirement; do not carry a halftime Over lean once the pace clamps. A clear regular-season favourite can be losing wire-to-wire - never finalise the side from the pregame mismatch narrative.

LARGE-HANDICAP TOP-PICK CAUTION (reinforced): a -21.5 type top pick is only safe when there is a structural reason the gap is sticky (talent chasm + opponent can't score + favorite plays starters). A single prior blowout is not structural. Treat double-digit-plus handicaps as cover risks, not anchors, unless the cushion-side failure paths are genuinely <12% margin.

=== LEARNINGS UPDATE 2026-06-08 (COMPREHENSIVE PENDING SWEEP: all carried rows settled/closed) ===

CONTEXT: Closed the remaining carried prediction-log rows. Settled PBA G3, NZNBL Southland-Franklin, JB Bruges-Ghent, Liechtenstein-Cyprus, and Antwerp-Akcel; corrected Liechtenstein-Cyprus from a stale 1-0 partial to Cyprus 2-0 with corner total over 9.5; closed Denmark-Ukraine as abandoned/partial after a completed 2-1 first half. Net lesson: the top/bottom leak is still alive in soccer corners and cricket innings totals, while completed-phase settlement and abandonment handling both improved.

RULE A - CHASE-CAP RULE (cricket, HIGH CONFIDENCE, fully validated). When the market is the SECOND-innings chasing side total and the line sits far above the target, the total is structurally capped: the innings ends on the winning run or after the overs expire, so realistic max is roughly target plus a few runs. JB Bruges-Ghent: Ghent chased 167, market was Over/Under 254.5, Under was a structural lock (#1 WON) and Over a near-impossibility (#4 LOST). This is not a complementary-pair coinflip. Always establish innings order and target first; then spend effort on the live leg such as powerplay/first-6 O/U.

RULE B - NEW-LEAGUE VENUE PAR IS A GUIDE, NOT A SHIELD (cricket correction). EUT20 Belgium / 12 Stars Hofstade had early first-innings totals around 159, 166, and 166, so 165.5 looked like the upper edge. Antwerp-Akcel corrected that: Antwerp made 174/9 and was already 53/1 after 4.5 overs, which mathematically settled first-6 Over 46.5 before the powerplay was done. In brand-new leagues, venue par should cap confidence, not override live batting quality, star-heavy top orders, or an explosive first five overs. Once a side is 50+ before five overs, stop defending a top-ranked innings under unless wickets and required deceleration make it structurally live.

RULE C - COMPLEMENTARY-PAIR HONESTY STILL REQUIRED. Over/Under pairs around 1H 0.5, total 2.5, corners 9.5, innings 165.5, or powerplay 46.5 often create forced near-50% bottom slots. If no outcome is genuinely below about 30%, say so and cap confidence. Antwerp 1st-innings Over 165.5 and Liechtenstein-Cyprus corner Over 9.5 both won from bottom slots; neither deserved to be treated as a confident fade.

RULE D - SOCCER GOALS AND CORNERS ARE SEPARATE AXES. Liechtenstein-Cyprus finished 0-2, so Total Goals Under 2.5 and 1H Over 0.5 were right, but the corner total still cleared 9.5 (published stat lines show either 1-9 or 1-10 corners). A stronger side can dominate width and corners against a deep block without producing a goal avalanche. Do not infer corner under from goal under; model wide entries, blocked crosses, possession tilt, and deep defensive shape separately.

RULE E - CONTROLLED-FRIENDLY UNDER NEEDS A 2-1 FIRST-HALF STRESS TEST. Denmark-Ukraine was abandoned after Eriksen collapsed, but the completed first half was already Denmark 2-1 Ukraine. That means 1H Over 0.5 and full Over 2.5 were mathematically determined before abandonment. For friendlies with two real attacks, 1H Over can be the cleanest leg, and full-game Under 2.5 should not rank second unless the 2-1/2-0 first-half path is explicitly discounted.

RULE F - ABANDONED-MATCH SETTLEMENT HYGIENE. If a match is abandoned, close the row as ABANDONED/PARTIAL rather than leaving it pending. Settle only completed or mathematically determined legs: a completed first-half goal market can be graded; a full total already over the threshold can be graded by monotonic score; corners and winner/side that depend on a normal full match should be void/ungraded unless the competition or settlement rule explicitly says otherwise. Record the stoppage state and source label, then remove the row from pending.

RULE G - FINALS SIDE: SUPERSTAR CEILING OVER ONE-GAME MOMENTUM (basketball). In a tied finals, do not pick the side only from the most recent game's momentum/cushion logic. PBA G3 ranked TNT +1.5 above Ginebra -1.5 on Game 2 momentum, but Ginebra's proven superstar ceiling (Brownlee 41) plus home crowd blew it open 35-16 in Q1 and won by 14. The finals scoring-floor read was correct; the side read missed the superstar/home response path.

RULE H - DEFENSIVE-BATTLE / SLOWER-H2H SIGNAL (basketball). NZNBL Southland-Franklin projected 195 but finished 161 in a defensive battle; three overs in the top half all lost. The slower April H2H was a truer total signal than pace-inflated recent home blowouts. When one credible direct data point sits well below recent form, do not bury the under. Side and total remain independent axes: Sharks cover/winner was still correct.

RULE I - DATA-VERIFICATION DISCIPLINE. Cross-check exact date, competition identity, and stat line before grading. This sweep caught multiple false/stale paths: a stale April NZNBL recap masqueraded as Southland-Franklin, an earlier Liechtenstein-Cyprus partial score missed the 71st-minute goal and corner stats, and search summaries conflicted across soccer pages. If two sources disagree on an exact corner count but both land on the same side of the market threshold, grade the threshold while documenting the source conflict.

RULE J - DEDUPLICATE PARALLEL-SESSION ROWS. Concurrent sessions can write two pregame cards for the same fixture. On cleanup, consolidate into one settled row, grade the fuller card, and preserve any useful read from the removed duplicate rather than double-counting the fixture.

RULE L - +1.5 RUN CUSHIONS BOTH SAFE IN A 1-RUN GAME (MLB). With two weak/short starters projected, ranking BOTH +1.5 run lines above the total was correct: Giants 2-1 meant both cushions cashed. When the projected margin is ~1 run, the two run cushions are the safest items and the total is the higher-variance axis - keep run cushions above the total in two-weak-starter games.

RULE M - DO NOT OVER-TRUST THE HOME/QUALITY FAVORITE TO WIN OUTRIGHT IN A ~1-RUN GAME (MLB winner-pick). I picked the Cubs (better season/home profile) but the Giants won 2-1 in extras on hot bats. RULE N - VERIFY HANDICAP LINE ORIENTATION BEFORE RANKING (AFL Essendon-Carlton, June 7). The listed handicap had the BOTTOM side (Essendon, 1-11) favored by 32.5 and the actual in-form favourite (Carlton, 3-0 under interim coach) getting +32.5 - backwards from reality. Always confirm which team the line actually favours against real form/standings before ranking handicap legs; here it made Carlton +32.5 a near-lock #1 and Essendon -32.5 the genuine least-likely #4. A "favourite" in the line text may be the underdog in reality.

RULE X - FINAL SCORE FIRST, PHASE SCORE SECOND (cricket/source correction from Netherlands-USA). Never settle a match winner or innings-total from a stale live row, search snippet, or partial innings display. First confirm the final/complete score and winner from an opened final source, then separately confirm phase markets from over-by-over, ball-by-ball, period, quarter, or official split data. If the match result is confirmed but the phase split is not, correct the result and leave the phase leg UNGRADED instead of inferring it from average scoring pace. This rule applies across sports: full-time score cannot prove Q1/1H/corners/first-5 unless the phase is directly shown or mathematically forced.

=== LEARNINGS UPDATE 2026-06-09 (TWO pre-WC soccer friendlies settled: NED 2-1 Uzbekistan and France 3-1 Northern Ireland; both cards 3-3, same repeatable corner error) ===

RESULTS: Netherlands 2-1 Uzbekistan (HT 1-0; 3 goals; 6 total corners, 3 each). France 3-1 Northern Ireland (HT 1-0; Olise hat-trick; 4 goals; 6 total corners, France 5 / NI 1). Both cards graded 3-3 with NO penalty - in BOTH, the #1 pick (1H Over 0.5) won, the #6 bottom pick (1H Under 0.5) lost, and the potential winner (the favourite) was correct. The extremes-and-winner process is sound; keep it.

RULE P - CORNERS RUN LOW IN INTERNATIONAL FRIENDLIES; DEFAULT TOWARD THE UNDER (high priority, validated twice same day). I ranked Combined Corners Over 9.5 at #2 (NED-Uzbekistan) and #3 (France-NI) on "dominant favourite vs deep block generates corners" logic. BOTH games produced only 6 total corners and both Overs LOST; Corners Under 9.5 won both. Why the reasoning failed: friendlies are lower-intensity, the favourite is sharpening shape not chasing a result, deep-block opponents clear long / concede throw-ins and goal-kicks rather than corners, and second-half mass substitutions break attacking rhythm. Even a 72.5%-possession, 27-shot France performance yielded only 5 corners. FIX: in international friendlies, treat Corners Over 9.5 as a LOWER-half pick by default and rank Corners Under 9.5 ABOVE Corners Over 9.5 unless there is specific evidence of a high-corner script (both teams attacking openly, competitive/elimination context, a known high-corner team, or a wing-heavy plan against a packed box in a meaningful game). Possession/shot dominance does NOT reliably convert to 10+ corners in a friendly. (Note this is the friendly-specific counterpart to competitive-match corner reads - do not import a league/knockout corner expectation into an exhibition.)

RULE Q - TOTAL-GOALS DIRECTION IS MATCHUP-SPECIFIC, NOT A BLANKET FRIENDLY UNDER. The two totals split correctly on the matchup logic: France (home, elite attack, NI's more open 3-4-3) went OVER 2.5 (4 goals) and I correctly ranked Over #2; Netherlands (neutral venue, misfiring attack, Uzbekistan's packed 5-4-1) I leaned Under #3 and it lost by a whisker (1-0 until the 87th, then two late goals + a consolation made it 3). LESSON: the France OVER flip was right - opponent shape (open 3-4-3 vs bus-parking 5-4-1), home advantage, and finishing quality justified differentiating the two totals rather than copying one lean across both cards. But beware the LATE-GOAL TAIL in friendlies: a 1-0 game can add 2+ goals in the final 10 minutes once subs/fatigue/penalties intervene, so a friendly "Under 2.5" lean off a tight first hour is fragile - keep total unders as modest leans, never confident, when a favourite is camped in the opponent half.

RULE O - IN-FORM ROAD FAVOURITE CUSHION + CAPPED COMPLEMENTARY TOTAL (KBO Hanwha-Lotte, June 7, validated). Hanwha (in-form road favourite, won the opener 9-2) beat slumping Lotte 7-2. The favourite +1.5 cushion was the correct #1 (fails only if the slumping home side wins by 2+ - least likely state), and the Over/Under 10.5 total was correctly flagged a capped near-coinflip (landed 9, Under won from the bottom slot, no serious penalty). Repeat: rank the in-form side's cushion #1 when the opponent is slumping, and pre-flag same-line totals as capped pairs rather than confident fades.

=== LEARNINGS UPDATE 2026-06-09 (shortened cricket, WNBA Aces-Storm, and Mirpur pitch/live-source correction) ===

RULE R - RAIN-SHORTENED CRICKET FORMAT OVERRIDE (JB Bruges 121/5 vs Liege Red Lions 85/7, 10-over match). Pregame damp-outfield/pitch-under logic failed once the match was reduced to 10 overs per side. In a shortened innings, the "first 10 overs" market becomes the whole innings, wickets are discounted, and batting intent becomes powerplay-style from ball one. Bruges were 74/2 after 6 and 121/5 after 10, so both phase overs won. FIX: when overs are reduced, immediately rerate all phase totals from the new innings length. A wet delay does not mean under if the reduced format creates maximum-attack intent.

RULE S - WNBA FAVOURITE CEILING CAN BREAK FULL-GAME UNDERS EVEN WHEN THE UNDERDOG OFFENCE IS WEAK (Aces 101-91 Storm). The Aces +15.5 side read and Storm -15.5 bottom read were correct, but the full-game Under 166.5 was wrong by a lot because Las Vegas carried a 100-point ceiling and Seattle still produced enough scoring to reach 192 total. Do not rank a full-game under high when the favourite can score 95-105 by itself and the underdog has any plausible 80+ path through young scorers, transition, or loose late game script.

RULE T - WNBA PHASE OVERS CAN BE BETTER THAN FULL-GAME UNDER WHEN A FAVOURITE HAS ELITE EARLY CREATION. Storm-Aces Q1 was 48 and halftime was 93, so Q1 Over 41.5 and 1H Over 82.5 both won. The separate Aces Q1 -0.5 lean lost because Seattle won Q1 25-23. FIX: do not assume the better team wins Q1 just because it is the better full-game side; Q1 side is more volatile than Q1 total. When the favourite has elite creators but can start loose defensively, phase overs can beat favourite Q1 spread plays.

RULE U - MIRPUR PITCH REPORT NUANCE: NOT SPIN-SLOW FROM BALL ONE. For Bangladesh-Australia 1st ODI research, the stronger current pitch report described Shere Bangla as Fast & Bounce / average batting / pace & bounce / average spin, while venue summaries still show Mirpur as a tougher ODI batting venue with average first innings around 227-230 and surfaces that can slow later. Correct framing: early scoring or a first-5 over can be compatible with the pitch; the under case on high innings lines comes from the full 50-over venue profile and middle-overs slowdown risk, not from assuming the new ball is dead.

RULE V - LIVE-SOURCE CONFLICT HYGIENE IN CRICKET. If a user/broadcast state conflicts with a reliable live score page, state the conflict and rank from the most current verifiable score while allowing that the broadcast may be ahead. Bangladesh-Australia had conflicting live states (user reported 56/0 after 15, CricketAddictor later showed 87/1 after 14). Do not overcommit to a total-path update without naming the source/time and recalculating from exact runs, wickets, overs, and required run rates.

RULE W - MANDATORY FIELDING/DEFENCE CHECK FOR CRICKET AND BASEBALL (high priority, user directive 2026-06-09). For every cricket and baseball card, get the latest available information on the FIELDING/DEFENSIVE ability of the actual players available to play, not only batting/bowling or hitting/pitching. This is required for pregame and live analysis.

CRICKET FIELDING GATE: after confirming XI/squad availability, check wicketkeeper quality, slip cordon/catching reliability, boundary-fielding strength, run-out/direct-hit threat, dropped-catch history, recent fielding errors, substitute-fielding impact, and whether injured/limited players are likely to hide in the field or lose mobility. Where available, use recent catches, run-outs, stumpings, dropped catches, fielding rating/impact, keeper byes/missed chances, and team fielding efficiency. Apply this to totals and side reads: weak fielding can add 10-25 runs through dropped chances, twos, overthrows, and missed run-outs; elite fielding can support unders and favourite/winner reads even when bowling is only average.

BASEBALL DEFENCE GATE: after confirming starters, catcher, bench, late scratches, and defensive alignment, check current-season and recent player/team defensive metrics before ranking sides, run lines, and totals. Prioritize Outs Above Average, Defensive Runs Saved, UZR when available, fielding percentage/errors only as a blunt signal, catcher framing/blocking/throwing, outfield arm strength, infield range, double-play ability, and whether players are out of position or playing through mobility injuries. Defence changes the run environment: poor range/errors can turn contact into crooked innings and push overs/favourite fades; elite catcher/fielding support can strengthen starter run suppression and make unders/run cushions safer.

LIVE FIELDING OVERRIDE: in cricket/baseball live cards, record any visible dropped catch, missed stumping, misfield, throwing error, passed ball/wild pitch block failure, outfield route mistake, or defensive substitution. Treat repeated fielding leakage as a live over and opponent-side input; treat sharp fielding plus efficient pitching/bowling as an under and run-suppression input. If fielding data is unavailable, explicitly say UNKNOWN and lower confidence rather than ignoring the dimension.
