RULE Y - NEAR-EQUAL FRIENDLIES ARE NOT MISMATCH FRIENDLIES. China PR vs Thailand exposed a misuse of the mismatch-friendly soccer rule. The 1H Over 0.5 rule is strongest when a clear favourite faces a weaker/leaky side. It should NOT be treated as automatic when teams are similarly ranked, recent model probabilities are near-balanced, one team uses a 5-back/5-3-2 defensive shape, weather is damp, and the stronger-side edge is modest. In that near-equal setup, 0-0 HT is a normal script, not a tail. FIX: before ranking 1H Over 0.5 first, classify the soccer card as one of: true mismatch, moderate favourite, near-equal, or defensive/wet near-equal. Only the first two can use the "1H Over first, 1H Under bottom" default. In near-equal or defensive/wet near-equal friendlies, keep 1H Over/Under closer together and let lineup shape, weather, and first-15 live state decide.

RULE Z - FRIENDLY CORNER UNDER CAN BE A PICK, BUT NOT A SETTLEMENT. Philippines-Myanmar and China-Thailand had opened final/HT scores but no opened reliable corner counts. The correct handling is to grade goals and winner, then leave the corner pair UNGRADED. Never infer Corners Under 9.5 from a 0-0 score or Corners Over/Under from a 5-1 score. Goals, possession, and territorial dominance are not corner counts. For settlement, require an opened stat source that explicitly lists corners, or leave the corner leg pending/ungraded even if the rest of the row is closed.

RULE AA - SOURCE TIMESTAMP IMPOSSIBILITY CHECK. China-Thailand had a search/opened source conflict: multiple live-score sources listed FT 0-0, while one Sina article claimed China won 2-0 but showed a visible publish time before kickoff and a generic "according to post-match reports" structure. If an article claims a final score while its visible timestamp predates kickoff, or if it conflicts with multiple current live-score pages, mark it CONFLICTING and do not let it control settlement. Re-check official federation pages, reliable live-score pages, and local-language reports; if the conflict remains, settle from the most timestamp-sane source stack and record the conflict.

RULE AB - CRICKET ABANDONED MATCHES: COMPLETED PHASES ONLY. Liege-Akcel confirms the phase-only settlement rule for rain-abandoned cricket. A completed first-six/powerplay score can be graded if the phase is complete, but full-innings totals and match winner should be void/ungraded when rain or wet outfield/run-up stops the innings before the required full market state. Directional "it was on pace under" is not enough to grade a full-innings under.

RULE AC - OPPONENT-ADJUSTED MISMATCH GOALS STILL WORK WHEN THE CLASS GAP IS REAL. Philippines-Myanmar reinforced the Philippines-Guam lesson: when both current form and opponent quality point to weak defensive resistance, the 1H Over 0.5 and full Over 2.5 can both be good even in a friendly. Philippines won 5-1 with HT 1-0, so the top 1H Over, full Over, and winner read were correct. Keep separating this from China-Thailand: Philippines-Myanmar was a clearer scoring mismatch; China-Thailand was a near-equal defensive/wet friendly.

RULE AD - FINAL-STATUS LAG CHECK FOR LIVE SCORE SOURCES. Australia-Bangladesh showed that one source can still display Live/Rain while another reputable scorecard has already settled the DLS result. If a match is rain-stopped and near completion, re-open multiple sources before leaving the winner pending. If a reputable scorecard clearly marks Match Ended/DLS with final teams, innings, player-of-match context, and a coherent result, close the row from that source while recording the lagging/conflicting source. Do not keep a row open purely because one official series page is cache-lagged.

=== SOURCE ACCESS PLAYBOOK - ACCURATE PRE-MATCH AND LIVE INFORMATION (added 2026-06-09) ===

PURPOSE: Before every card, use the most accurate current source stack available in this environment, with special attention to sources that can be opened without bot blocks. Do not rely on search snippets alone when a direct match page, API JSON, official league page, or reliable live scorecard can be opened. If a source is dynamic, blocked, stale, or conflicts with another source, state that explicitly and cross-check.

UNIVERSAL SOURCE ORDER:
1. Official league/competition match centre, official API JSON, official scorecard, official team sheet, official injury report, and official weather/venue data.
2. Structured public JSON feeds that open cleanly, especially MLB Stats API, ESPN public scoreboard/summary endpoints, NBA CDN liveData, and NHL api-web references when accessible.
3. Reliable live-score/box-score pages that expose text in the page, not just a blocked script shell: Cricbuzz, CricTracker, CricketWorld, Guardian match centres, ESPN pages/API, ABC/AFL/NRL official pages, CBS/FOX/theScore where available.
4. Team/club/federation press releases, verified beat reporters, and preview articles for availability, tactical intent, pitch/venue notes, or expected XI/lineups.
5. Historical/stat sources: AFL Tables/OzFootball/Footywire, Baseball Savant/FanGraphs/Baseball-Reference, Basketball-Reference/StatMuse/RealGM, Soccerway/WorldFootball/FBref where accessible, Hockey-Reference/Natural Stat Trick, Rugby League Project, Ultimate Rugby, Tennis Abstract, official ranking/stat pages.
6. Weather/conditions: official meteorological source when possible (BOM, Met Office, NOAA/NWS, Environment Canada, local national service), then Timeanddate/WillyWeather/Weather.com/local forecasts. Always tie weather to the match window, not the whole day.

BOT-ACCESS / STALENESS RULES:
- If ESPNcricinfo, Flashscore, SofaScore, some official pages, or app-style match centres are blocked/dynamic/stale, do not force them. Use opened text scorecards, official APIs, Cricbuzz/CricketWorld/CricTracker, Guardian/ABC/CBS/FOX/ESPN APIs, or direct league pages instead.
- Search result snippets are orientation only. They can identify a source or alert to a score, but do not settle or rank from the snippet alone unless every direct page is blocked and the uncertainty is stated.
- If two live sources conflict, name the conflict, prefer the most official/opened live feed, and keep the user-reported broadcast state as potentially ahead. Recalculate from exact score/time/overs only after choosing the state.
- For settlement, require a final/FT/Full Time/Completed source with period/quarter/inning/over detail where the market depends on phases. Do not settle from competition labels or incomplete tables.

CRICKET SOURCE STACK:
- First use official board/ICC/tournament scorecards when they open; then Cricbuzz live scores/scorecard/commentary, CricketWorld match live pages, CricTracker live scores/scorecards, CricketAddictor, CREX, Sportzwiki, MyKhel, and cricsheet for historical ball-by-ball only.
- For pre-match: confirm toss, innings order, XI, substitute/impact rules, venue, pitch report, ground dimensions/boundaries if available, weather, DLS/shortened-overs risk, and whether the line is a full-innings or phase line.
- For live: Cricbuzz is a high-priority accessible text source because it exposes live score, venue, toss, overs, and links to scorecard/commentary. CricketWorld is useful for pitch/weather/venue metadata. CricTracker often exposes scorecard and phase state.
- Avoid treating generic fantasy pitch reports as definitive. Use them as pitch inputs only after checking current live behaviour, official toss/conditions, and venue averages.

BASEBALL SOURCE STACK:
- MLB: MLB Stats API is the first structured source for schedule, gamePk, line score, box score, live feed/play-by-play, venue, probable/actual starters, and game status. MLB.com pages, MLB Gameday, Baseball Savant/Statcast, FanGraphs, Baseball-Reference, team pages, ESPN/CBS/FOX/theScore are secondary/cross-check sources.
- KBO/NPB/other baseball: official league sites first where accessible; then Naver/Yahoo Japan/local reliable pages, MyKBO, Baseball-Reference minors/international where available, ESPN/CBS/FOX only if covering the league.
- Always collect actual starters, catcher, batting order, handedness/platoon, bullpen rest, defensive fielding metrics (Rule W), park factor, roof/weather, umpire if available, and current injury/scratch state.
- MLB Stats API and ESPN scoreboard JSON are usually accessible without bot blocks and should be preferred to dynamic pages for live state.

BASKETBALL SOURCE STACK:
- NBA: official NBA game pages and CDN liveData scoreboard/boxscore JSON when current; ESPN public scoreboard/summary API; NBA/WNBA official stats pages if accessible; Basketball-Reference, StatMuse, RealGM, team injury pages, beat reporters, CBS/FOX/theScore as cross-checks.
- WNBA: WNBA official game pages/box scores first, then ESPN public WNBA scoreboard/summary API, CBS/FOX/theScore game pages, official/team injury reports, Athlon/Rotowire/team PR for late availability. WNBA stats pages may time out; if so, use official game page plus ESPN/CBS/FOX.
- FIBA/domestic: FIBA LiveStats and official competition pages first; Proballers/RealGM/Eurobasket/FIBA box scores and league official pages next. For small leagues, verify date/competition identity carefully.
- For live phase markets, require quarter/half splits from a live box score or play-by-play; do not infer Q1/1H from final score unless mathematically forced.

SOCCER SOURCE STACK:
- Official federation/competition match centre first (FIFA, UEFA, confederations, league/federation pages). Then ESPN public soccer scoreboard where the competition is covered; Guardian match centres/results for accessible goals, lineups, possession/shots/corners; BBC/Sky/L'Equipe/Goal/Sports Mole for team news and match context; Soccerway/WorldFootball/FBref/FotMob/SofaScore only when the page is accessible and current.
- For corners, use a source that explicitly lists corners/statistics. If only goals are exposed, do not infer corner outcome from goals/possession.
- For friendlies, get confirmed/expected lineups and substitution context; corner volume and late-goal tails differ from competitive matches.

AFL SOURCE STACK:
- AFL.com.au official match centre, AFL app-accessible summaries, official club team announcements, ABC score centre/live blog, ESPN AU/AFL pages, WatchAFL match centre where accessible, Zero Hanger match pages, Footywire, AFL Tables, OzFootball, BOM/WillyWeather/Timeanddate for weather.
- Confirm final 23s, late changes, substitute, injuries, venue roof/open-air status, hourly match-window weather, quarter scores, inside 50s, clearances, hitouts, marks inside 50, disposal/turnover profile, and scoring-shot conversion.
- If AFL.com.au is dynamic, use ABC/ESPN/ZeroHanger/OzFootball/AFL Tables as text-accessible cross-checks.

NRL / RUGBY LEAGUE SOURCE STACK:
- NRL.com official Match Centre, official Team Lists/Casualty Ward, live blogs, match reports, and player stats first. Then ESPN, Fox Sports Australia, ABC, Rugby League Project, Livesport where accessible, club reports, and verified reporters.
- Confirm final 17/18, late interchange changes, HIA/injury risk, weather, venue surface, travel/rest, recent metres, line breaks, tackle breaks, errors, penalties, goal-kicking, and fatigue.

RUGBY UNION SOURCE STACK:
- Official competition/union pages first (World Rugby, Six Nations, SANZAAR, Premiership/URC/Top 14, national federations). Then ESPN Scrum, Ultimate Rugby, BBC/Sky/Guardian, RugbyPass, team sheets, and local weather.
- Confirm starting XV/bench, late withdrawals, goal-kicker, set-piece strength, discipline/card profile, weather/wind, and field condition.

NFL / COLLEGE FOOTBALL SOURCE STACK:
- NFL.com official Game Center, official injury reports, team PR, inactives, Next Gen Stats, ESPN public scoreboard/summary API, CBS/FOX/Pro-Football-Reference/Stathead where available.
- For college football, use official conference/team pages, ESPN, NCAA pages, Sports-Reference CFB, local beat reporters, and official depth charts/injury reporting where available.
- Confirm QB, offensive line, defensive front/secondary injuries, weather/wind, turf/grass, pace, red-zone, explosive plays, turnovers/pressure, and special teams.

NHL SOURCE STACK:
- NHL.com GameCenter and official NHL API-web endpoints when accessible; ESPN public NHL scoreboard/summary API; official team pages/beat reporters for starting goalies and scratches; Natural Stat Trick, Hockey-Reference, MoneyPuck, Evolving-Hockey where available.
- The public NHL API is commonly referenced as api-web.nhle.com for schedule/gamecenter/play-by-play/boxscore, but test endpoint access each time and fall back to NHL.com/ESPN if blocked.
- Confirm starting goalie, line combinations, defensive pairings, scratches, travel/rest, back-to-back goalie workload, special teams, shot/xG profile, and period splits.

TENNIS SOURCE STACK:
- ATP/WTA/ITF/Grand Slam official live scores and draw pages first; then Flashscore/SofaScore only if accessible, Tennis Abstract for historical form and surfaces, Ultimate Tennis Statistics, official tournament pages, weather for outdoor matches.
- Confirm surface, indoor/outdoor, retirement/injury history, recent workload, hold/break stats, serve/return splits, H2H only after surface/form adjustment.

GOLF / MOTORSPORT / OTHER SPORTS:
- Golf: PGA/DP World/LPGA official leaderboards, tournament pages, ShotLink when available, weather/wind, course fit, tee times/wave bias, injury/WD news.
- Motorsport/F1: FIA/F1 official timing/classification, team updates, qualifying/grid, weather, tyre allocation, penalties, practice long-run pace, reliability.
- For any niche league, identify the official competition page and one independent accessible cross-check before ranking. If only one source is reachable, lower confidence and say source coverage is thin.

FINAL SOURCE DISCIPLINE:
- Always note which source controlled the key decision: official lineup/toss, live score, pitch report, injury report, weather, or phase split.
- In no-odds requests, do not use betting odds, market movement, or bookmaker previews except to identify fixture time/venue if no other source exists; never let odds drive ranking.
- Prefer reproducible, opened URLs and structured data over memory. If information is UNKNOWN, mark it UNKNOWN rather than filling the gap with assumptions.

PRESS CONFERENCE / COACH COMMENT EVIDENCE GATE:
- Before a pre-match card, search for official or credentialed pre-match press conference material when it could change tactics, availability, workload, rotation, pitch/venue read, weather preparation, motivation, or role allocation. Priority order: official team/league transcript or video, official team article, credentialed beat report quoting the coach/player directly, then reputable local media. Do not use generic hype, unsourced quote graphics, or fan reposts as controlling evidence.
- After settlement, search for post-match coach/player comments when the result exposed a modelling miss or a new pattern. Use those comments to explain WHY the result happened: tactical adjustment, defensive coverage, substitution plan, fatigue, player limitation, pitch behaviour, fielding/defensive errors, shot quality, weather, or game-state management.
- Treat press comments as context, not proof by themselves. A coach saying "we wanted tempo" is useful only if the lineup, phase splits, shot map, possession data, or live state supports it. A coach saying a player was limited or unavailable can control the availability model only when official/credentialed and timestamped.
- Log the quote source, speaker, timestamp, and whether it is pre-match or post-match. Convert the timestamp to Australia/Sydney when timing affects the data cutoff. If no press conference/report is accessible, write PRESS COMMENTS: not found/opened and do not invent intent.
- Apply this before sport-specific rules: universal availability, source freshness, and final-score/phase verification still control; press comments then refine the sport model. Cricket comments may alter pitch/batting order/overs workload; basketball comments may alter rotation/pace/defensive coverage; soccer comments may alter formation/press/substitution intent; AFL/NRL comments may alter role, injury, weather, or interchange assumptions.

=== AUTOMATIC FAILURE REVIEW TRIGGERS (added 2026-06-09) ===

MANDATORY COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW TRIGGER: automatically run a comprehensive review whenever the original ranking fails at the top of the card. For a 4-option card, if BOTH original top-2 picks lose, immediately review what went wrong before the next card or live update. For an 8-option card, if ALL original top-4 picks lose, immediately review what went wrong. This review is mandatory even if later live updates improved the read.

REVIEW SCOPE: re-check final score and phase splits; compare original ranking to final result; inspect newest reliable sources; identify missed inputs across form, pitch/venue/field conditions, weather, player availability, fielding/defence, pace/tempo, matchup, coaching/tactical context, and live-source conflicts. Name the specific bad assumption, the source that corrects it, and the concrete rule change. If the top failure was caused by a late lineup/toss/format/weather change, document that trigger separately from pure model error.

CRICKET APPLICATION - BANGLADESH/AUSTRALIA MIRPUR CORRECTION: do not use old Mirpur averages as a hard ceiling when current Bangladesh batting form, actual XI, toss, and live pitch behaviour show a better scoring surface. In Bangladesh-Australia 1st ODI, Bangladesh were 62 in the mandatory powerplay, 106/2 by 16.3, and 265/7 by 48.3; this made low 251.5 unders wrong and proved Bangladesh's current top/middle order form was underweighted. Mirpur can be "average batting / fast & bounce" early and still slow later; model both halves instead of treating the venue as a blanket under.

CRICKET OPPONENT-QUALITY / FIELDING CORRECTION: when a major side fields an inexperienced or non-first-choice attack, do not price it as full-strength just because of the badge. For Australia in the Bangladesh ODI, the attack included Bartlett, Ellis, Liam Scott, Green, Short, Renshaw and Zampa, with part-time overs and several younger/less-set ODI roles. Before ranking innings unders, compare the available bowling/fielding unit to the normal first-choice unit and ask whether weak fielding, inexperience, part-time overs, or missed boundary prevention can add 20+ runs.

LIVE TOTAL CORRECTION: when the live innings has wickets in hand and is already ahead of a threshold's required rate, demote historical venue unders quickly. At 87/1 after 14, Bangladesh needed only 4.58 rpo to clear 251.5 and 5.31 rpo to clear 277.5; Over 251.5 should have been favoured immediately, while 277.5/287.5 unders should have been framed as thin, not comfortable. Use exact live arithmetic first, then venue/pitch as a modifier.

BASKETBALL LOWER-HOUSE TOTALS CORRECTION - NETANYA/NES ZIONA 2026-06-10: a correct survival/form side read can coexist with a wrong under stack. Nes Ziona won 91-84, but the Q1 was 53, halftime 96, and final total 175, beating the Q1/1H/full overs. When two teams average around 81 ppg each and the same-venue H2H already showed a 186 total with Q1 49 and halftime 95, do not rank full/Q1/1H unders together near the top solely from recent lower-house tension or modest defensive preference. Keep the overs closer unless current lineups, pace, or press evidence clearly suppress creation.

BASKETBALL DOMESTIC FINAL GAME 2 BLOWOUT CORRECTION - LKL JUVENTUS/ZALGIRIS 2026-06-10: Zalgiris beat Juventus 100-69 with Q1 37, halftime 83, and final total 169. All original top-four picks lost because the model over-weighted home adjustment, season scoring, and underdog cushion, while under-weighting the immediate Game 1 blowout/phase pattern and Zalgiris' defensive control. In domestic finals where Game 1 is a favorite blowout with low Q1/1H phases and coach/player comments point to physicality or a blocked opponent start, do not bury the favorite spread or full-game under in Game 2 just because the venue changes. Treat the repeat-blowout low-phase path as a main script.

BASKETBALL LOWER-HOUSE SIDE/TOTAL DIVERGENCE - RAANANA/GALIL 2026-06-10: Raanana beat Galil 81-64 with Q1 36, halftime 77, and final total 145. The correct winner still hid a major side-margin and total miss: Galil +4.5 failed and the bottom-ranked Raanana -4.5 won easily. In lower-house survival games, a prior close H2H or underdog table cushion is not enough to protect the dog if current home creation, urgency, and opponent scoring fragility support a low-total favorite cover. Model "favorite cover + under" as a normal correlated path when the underdog offense can collapse.

=== DEEP RESEARCH REPORT INTEGRATION - ADDED 2026-06-10 FROM C:\Users\danie\Downloads\deep-research-report.md ===

PURPOSE: The report is a multi-sport governance and performance-system review, not a single-game prediction note. Integrate it as a higher-level operating layer over all sport-specific modules. The durable upgrade is: official rules/source mapping first, minimum effective KPIs second, welfare/availability/load gates third, then sport-specific prediction modelling, live reassessment, and settlement.

RULE-SOURCE REGISTRY GATE:
- Before any serious card or retrospective, identify the governing/rules authority and competition-specific data source for that sport/league. Examples: IFAB for soccer laws, FIBA/NBA/WNBA for basketball rule/stat context, MCC/ICC for cricket laws/playing conditions, MLB/WBSC for baseball, IIHF/NHL for hockey, IRL/NRL for rugby league, World Rugby for rugby union, ITF for tennis, and R&A/USGA plus official tour leaderboards for golf.
- If a competition has its own rule variations, phase format, overtime/extra-time treatment, concussion substitution, reduced-overs rule, lineup rule, or settlement convention, record that before ranking. A prediction model using the wrong rule set is invalid even if the statistical read is strong.
- Dynamic official pages should be treated as current-state sources, not permanent truth. Record last-opened time, source status, and whether the page is final, live, stale, blocked, or script-only.

MINIMUM EFFECTIVE KPI PRINCIPLE:
- Do not bury the analysis under every available stat. Choose the smallest KPI set that explains the market being ranked, then add only variables that can actually change the decision.
- Universal KPI groups: availability status, injury/welfare burden, current form adjusted for opponent strength, phase performance, venue/conditions, decision-quality calibration, and source completeness.
- Forecasting KPI set for this workspace: top-pick hit rate, bottom-pick failure rate, Brier/log-loss style calibration where probabilities are stated, percentage of rows settled from official/primary sources, percentage of phase legs with verified splits, and error rate in the lowest-confidence or "least likely" slot. The bottom-slot error rate must be reviewed as a separate KPI, not hidden inside raw W-L.

ATHLETE WELFARE / LOAD / AVAILABILITY AS PRIMARY INPUTS:
- Availability is broader than "injury list." Treat concussion/HIA status, load management, minutes/pitch-count/overs caps, travel fatigue, dense schedule, youth overuse rules, return-to-play status, and heat/hydration risk as first-order inputs where relevant.
- If a welfare or load protocol could limit participation, minutes, bowling overs, pitch count, snaps, shifts, substitutions, or late-game effectiveness, cap confidence until the role is verified from official team sheet, gamebook, box score, coach quote, or live participation.
- For youth/development or lower-level competitions, never import elite professional workload assumptions. Age, sex category, competition level, budget, medical support, and pathway stage change the reliability of public data and the expected player-management pattern.

SPORT KPI QUICK GATES FROM THE REPORT:
- AFL: inside-50 differential, clearance differential, contested possession, intercept/turnover-to-score rate, marks inside 50, scoring-shot efficiency, concussion/late-change status.
- Baseball: OBP/SLG or OPS, K-BB, quality of contact, starter times-through-order, bullpen leverage, defence/run prevention, pitch-count/rest compliance.
- Cricket: run rate by phase, wickets in hand, dot-ball rate, boundary rate, bowling economy by phase, dropped chances/fielding, pitch/weather, workload for fast bowlers.
- Basketball: eFG%, TS%, turnover rate, offensive rebound rate, free-throw rate, lineup net rating, pace, shot profile, Q1/1H/full splits, minutes/load.
- Soccer: xG/xGA, shot quality allowed, final-third entries, field tilt, pressing/PPDA, set-piece xG, transition shots allowed, best-XI minutes continuity, explicit corner source when corners are a market.
- American football: EPA/play, success rate, pressure rate, explosive-play rate, red-zone TD rate, third-down conversion, missed tackles, QB/offensive-line availability, contact-load/weather.
- Hockey: xG share, shot/slot chance share, controlled exits/entries, PP/PK quality, adjusted save percentage, goalie confirmation, rest/travel, scratches.
- Rugby league: completion rate, ruck speed, post-contact metres, line breaks, tackle efficiency, errors, kick-return outcomes, spine availability, HIA/collision load.
- Rugby union: gain-line success, line-break rate, territory/kicking retention, penalties, tackle breaks conceded, lineout/scrum, red-zone conversion, head-injury/tackle-height compliance.
- Tennis: first-serve in, first-serve points won, second-serve points won, return points won, hold/break rate, surface-adjusted serve/return profile, travel/workload and retirement risk.
- Golf: strokes gained by category, GIR, scrambling, proximity, driving dispersion, wind/course-fit splits, official leaderboard/tee-time/weather wave.

PREGAME-LIVE-POST LOOP:
- Pregame: verify rule set, fixture identity, source freshness, market orientation, availability/load, minimum KPI set, phase/venue context, and confidence cap.
- Live: override pregame with exact score/time/phase arithmetic, confirmed participation, current pace, foul/penalty/bonus state, wickets/outs/goalie/pitcher state, weather interruptions, and official live source conflict handling.
- Post-settlement: confirm final score first, then phase splits/stat markets second, then update the log and add only durable lessons. If a top-cluster or bottom-slot failure occurs, classify whether the miss was rule/source, availability/load, KPI selection, phase modelling, market orientation, live arithmetic, or variance.

QUARTERLY CALIBRATION / MAINTENANCE HABIT:
- Periodically audit the sports doc and prediction log as a system, not just one game at a time. Track: unresolved pending rows, stale sources, duplicate rows, bottom-pick wins, top-pick losses, phase-leg ungraded rate, official-source coverage, and repeated sport-specific failure modes.
- If a lesson is already covered by a universal rule, reinforce it briefly instead of duplicating it. New additions should either add a new gate, sharpen a confidence cap, identify a sport-specific KPI, or correct a repeated error pattern.

============================================================
2026-06-10 COMPREHENSIVE ACCURACY UPGRADE - GAME-STATE/TIMEZONE RESOLUTION, SOURCE FRESHNESS, MASTER SOURCE DIRECTORY, EVIDENCE-CITED REASONING, AND TOP/BOTTOM PENALTY ELIMINATION
============================================================

WHY THIS UPGRADE (calibration snapshot at 2026-06-10):
- ~150 settled/closed cards. Top picks win ~82.7% (26 top-pick penalties). The declared "least likely" bottom pick wins ~46.7% (70 bottom-pick penalties) - statistically indistinguishable from a coinflip, i.e. ZERO demonstrated skill in the bottom slot. The adjusted record (~349-388) is losing almost entirely because of bottom-slot penalties plus a smaller top-slot leak.
- June 2026 failures show the rules EXIST but are not being APPLIED at ranking time (Juventus-Zalgiris all top-4 lost; Raanana-Galil top lost + bottom won; Bangladesh-Australia top-2 lost + bottom won; Liege-Akcel top lost + bottom won; Antwerp-Akcel top lost + bottom won; Netanya-Nes Ziona under-stack lost). The root causes repeat: (1) stale anchors (venue par, multi-season H2H, season averages) overriding current evidence; (2) totals-direction stacking; (3) no written probability before ranking; (4) game-state/timezone confusion; (5) decisive facts taken from memory or snippets instead of opened, timestamped sources.
- Therefore this upgrade is PROCESS ENFORCEMENT, not more lessons: mandatory written gates whose outputs must appear in every card. A rule that produces no written output in the card did not happen.

------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 1. MANDATORY PRE-CARD GATE SEQUENCE (run for EVERY ranked card; write the answer to each gate in the card)
------------------------------------------------------------
GATE 0 - PENDING SWEEP: settle/carry pending log rows first (existing rule).
GATE 1 - FIXTURE IDENTITY AND FORMAT: confirm teams, competition + tier (main league vs Rapid League vs cup), venue, official LOCAL start date/time, overs-per-side / quarters / period format, and HANDICAP LINE ORIENTATION against real form (Rule N). A first-N-overs line near a plausible full-innings value means CHECK FOR T10/REDUCED OVERS before modelling.
GATE 2 - GAME-STATE/TIMEZONE RESOLUTION: run Section 2 below. Output one word: PREGAME / LIVE / LIKELY COMPLETE, plus the AEST-converted start time. Never write "this game has not happened yet" without this conversion.
GATE 3 - SOURCE FRESHNESS: pull current sources per Section 4 directory; timestamp every decisive fact per Section 3; mark each as OPENED / SNIPPET / ASSUMED. No #1 pick may rest on ASSUMED or SNIPPET-only facts. For slate counts, schedule completeness, or "fixture missing" claims, use a direct shell fetch and count programmatically - summarized fetches truncate large JSONs (Sections 10/12).
GATE 4 - AVAILABILITY PACKET: both teams, by PLAYER PROFILE (existing injury/exclusion module): confirmed in/out/starter/bench/limited/projected/unknown, netted availability verdict, latest-cutoff re-check if within 60 minutes of start. If official websites are blocked/thin or the fact is late-breaking, run Section 9 social verification and label the result, walking the Section 10 access chain (X is logged-out blocked; Reddit unavailable; Bluesky public API is the working structured social rung).
GATE 5 - CONDITIONS: venue traits (park/pitch/boundaries/altitude/roof), weather inside the match window in VENUE LOCAL time (memory: weather-game-window-rule), motivation/match context (final, decider, dead rubber, relegation, cup).
GATE 6 - RECENCY STACK + OPPONENT ADJUSTMENT: current-season pace/scoring and last 2-3 actual games FIRST, opponent-adjusted; venue par / season averages / multi-season H2H are context, never the anchor; write the one-line recency verdict (CURRENT OVERRIDES / HISTORICAL HOLDS / MIXED / UNKNOWN-CAPPED).
GATE 7 - WRITE THE PROJECTION FIRST: for every market on the card, write the projected number/band BEFORE ranking. Compare to each line: projection within ~1 scoring unit of a line = COINFLIP flag (over/under must sit adjacent, never one at #4 by default).
GATE 8 - DECOUPLE SIDE FROM TOTAL: margin model (efficiency edge, comparable-opponent margins, home/away, availability, late-game control) is a separate axis from the total. Explicitly consider both correlation cases: favourite-cover+over (opponent weak on defense) and favourite-cover+under (opponent offense collapses).
GATE 9 - PROBABILITY TABLE + SLOT TESTS: per Section 6 - independent probability next to every option, top-slot stress test, bottom-slot <=30% + named failure paths, swap test, structural anchors placed correctly. On leak-flagged sports (MLB, Cricket, AFL, KBO, NBA-phase per Section 11.2) also write the SPORT-LEAK CHECK line and apply the sport gates: T20 powerplay/innings overs cannot sit at #4 without structural evidence (11.3), KBO #4 is structural-only with card-wide confidence cap, NBA Q1/1H complement pairs are coinflip-class at the extremes.
GATE 10 - CONSISTENCY AND OUTPUT: chat ranking MUST equal logged ranking; complementary pairs pre-flagged as capped; confidence caps written; cite source + timestamp for the #1 and #4 decisive facts (Section 5).
SHORTCUT RULE: if time-constrained, GATES 1, 2, 7 and 9 are NEVER skippable; they prevent the four penalty classes that dominate the log (wrong fixture/format, wrong game-state, coinflip buried at #4, unstressed #1).

------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 2. TIMEZONE AND GAME-STATE RESOLUTION PROTOCOL (fixes the "game hasn't happened yet" confusion)
------------------------------------------------------------
CONTEXT: the user's requests arrive in Australia/Sydney time. June-September is AEST (UTC+10); October-April is AEDT (UTC+11). Treat the request timestamp as AEST/AEDT accordingly unless the user states otherwise. The request time IS the data cutoff for pregame analysis.

PROCEDURE (run at GATE 2, every card):
1. Record the request timestamp in AEST.
2. Find the fixture's OFFICIAL local start time AND the venue's timezone from a current source (league schedule page, match centre).
3. Convert the official start to AEST. Conversion table for common zones (June = northern summer / southern winter):
   - US Eastern: EDT = UTC-4 -> AEST = ET + 14h (a 7:00pm ET start = 9:00am AEST NEXT calendar day).
   - US Central: CDT = UTC-5 -> +15h. US Mountain: MDT = UTC-6 -> +16h. US Pacific: PDT = UTC-7 -> +17h.
   - UK: BST = UTC+1 -> +9h. Central Europe: CEST = UTC+2 -> +8h. Eastern Europe/Israel: EEST/IDT = UTC+3 -> +7h.
   - India: IST = UTC+5:30 fixed -> +4.5h. Pakistan: PKT = UTC+5 -> +5h. Bangladesh: BST(Dhaka) = UTC+6 -> +4h.
   - Korea: KST = UTC+9 fixed -> +1h. Japan: JST = UTC+9 fixed -> +1h. China: CST = UTC+8 -> +2h.
   - New Zealand: NZST = UTC+12 (winter) -> -2h (an NZ 7pm tip = 5pm AEST same day).
   - South Africa: SAST = UTC+2 -> +8h. UAE: GST = UTC+4 -> +6h.
   - In southern summer (Oct-Apr) re-derive: AEDT = UTC+11 and northern zones leave DST (US ET becomes UTC-5 -> +16h; UK GMT -> +11h; CET -> +10h).
4. Classify the game state:
   - PREGAME: AEST start > request time. Use ONLY information available at or before the request cutoff; later facts are for settlement only.
   - LIVE: AEST start <= request < start + expected duration. Expected durations: soccer ~2h; NBA/WNBA/Euro basketball ~2.25-2.5h; NHL ~2.5h; AFL/NRL ~2.5-3h; MLB/KBO/NPB ~3-3.5h; T20 ~3.5-4h; ODI ~7.5-8.5h; Test = multi-day. LIVE means: pull the live score/state FIRST and re-rank from exact arithmetic; pregame narratives are void.
   - LIKELY COMPLETE: request >= start + duration. Search for the FINAL result before writing anything; the card is settlement/retrospective, not prediction.
5. THE LOCAL-DATE TRAP (the recurring error this protocol kills): a fixture's official local calendar date is often ONE DAY EARLIER than the AEST request date. A request on June 10 AEST about a US game "dated June 9" is usually about a game that finished THIS MORNING AEST - it HAS happened. Conversely an evening AEST request can precede that night's US/European games. NEVER conclude "not played yet" or "schedule conflict" from the date label alone; ALWAYS compare converted datetimes. If a team has two fixtures in the window (doubleheaders, friendlies, Rapid/main league), match the EXACT local kickoff and venue before proceeding (Tajikistan-India lesson).
6. WORKED EXAMPLES:
   - Request 2026-06-10 13:00 AEST; NBA game "June 9, 8:40pm ET" -> +14h = June 10, 10:40am AEST -> request is 13:00 -> LIKELY COMPLETE -> fetch final.
   - Request 2026-06-10 19:00 AEST; KBO game "June 10, 6:30pm KST" -> +1h = 7:30pm AEST -> PREGAME (30 min out) -> final lineup check now mandatory (GATE 4 last-cutoff rule).
   - Request 2026-06-10 09:00 AEST; IPL game "June 10, 7:30pm IST" -> +4.5h = June 11 12:00am AEST -> PREGAME, toss ~15 hours away -> XI is PROJECTED ONLY; card is provisional.
7. OUTPUT FORMAT (mandatory line in every card): "GAME-STATE: [PREGAME/LIVE/LIKELY COMPLETE] - local start [X], AEST start [Y], request [Z]."

------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 3. DATA FRESHNESS AND ANTI-STALENESS PROTOCOL (no decisions from stale, outdated or old information)
------------------------------------------------------------
EVERY DECISIVE FACT CARRIES THREE TAGS: [source] [timestamp or recency] [access level: OPENED page/API, SNIPPET from search results, or ASSUMED from memory]. A fact that cannot be timestamped is treated as stale until confirmed.

MAXIMUM AGE BY DATA TYPE (older = stale = re-verify before use):
- Lineups / XIs / inactives / scratches / starting goalie or pitcher: only as old as the sport's official release window (Section 4); anything earlier is PROJECTED. Re-check at the latest possible cutoff when the request is within 60 minutes of start.
- Injury/availability status: <24h old, and re-verified same-day for day-of-game statuses ("questionable"/"GTD" must be resolved by the final report or marked UNKNOWN).
- Weather: nowcast/hourly forecast pulled same-day, for the 30-60 min window before/during/after start in VENUE LOCAL time; a morning forecast does not describe an evening window.
- Pitch reports (cricket): same-day, ideally the live broadcast/toss report; previous-match pitch reports are context only.
- Team form/stats: must include the most recent completed game; if a source's "last 5" predates the team's latest game, it is stale.
- Live scores: only from pages/APIs showing current period/over state; a page stuck at Q2 or showing a pre-match shell is NOT live (Dubai-Partizan lesson).
- News/press: check the article's publish timestamp; apply RULE AA (timestamp impossibility - an article "reporting" a result with a publish time before kickoff is invalid).
- Betting lines (if permitted): real-time only; any line not checked at request time is omitted.

SEARCH-FOR-FRESHNESS TECHNIQUE (how to actually source current information):
1. Include the exact date and year in queries ("Team A vs Team B June 10 2026 lineup/final score") - undated queries surface old seasons and stale previews.
2. Prefer structured JSON APIs or official date-stamped pages over rendered pages, but still run the freshness gate: MLB Stats API, exact-date ESPN site APIs, NHL api-web, official injury PDFs/pages, and official date-path score pages are useful only when the returned date/timestamp matches the target event. Do not trust an official brand or HTTP 200 by itself; official endpoints can still serve stale cached bodies.
3. Open the page; do not settle or rank from a search snippet. Snippets can be cached/stale (the Sina pre-kickoff "result", the NED-USA 158/8 stale row, the stuck Dubai-Partizan shell). SNIPPET-only facts cap confidence and cannot carry #1.
4. Cross-check finals across TWO independent opened sources before settlement; for phase markets require explicit period/over/quarter splits (RULE X: final score first, phase score second).
5. Known fetch-blocked or render-thin sites (commonly 403/dynamic shell/login/CAPTCHA/stale shell): ESPNcricinfo direct, NRL.com automation paths, Flashscore, SofaScore, mykbostats live renders, some official app-style match centres, and X/Twitter logged-out pages. Route around them by switching sources, not by forcing access: Cricbuzz/CricTracker/CricketWorld/CREX/ICC/boards (cricket), official league pages + exact-date ESPN APIs (US sports), Guardian/ABC/club pages/TotalCorner (soccer/corners), KBO Korean official pages, NPB BIS, official Winner League/LKL/league pages (basketball), ZeroTackle/club/Fox/Legz late mail (NRL).
6. If two current sources conflict, name the conflict in the card, prefer the most-official opened feed, and record which source controlled (RULE AD source-lag, RULE V live-conflict hygiene).
7. Convert every source timestamp to AEST when timing affects the cutoff decision.

League paths verified/useful include baseball/mlb, basketball/nba, basketball/wnba, football/nfl, hockey/nhl, soccer/{comp e.g. eng.1, uefa.champions, fifa.friendly}, and australian-football/afl. Exact-date queries (?dates=YYYYMMDD) are mandatory when supported because default day.date may be US-local or stale relative to AEST. ESPN rugby-league/NRL endpoints failed in 2026-06-10 testing; do not depend on ESPN for NRL. Includes status, line scores, odds (ignore in research-only), and sometimes injuries/team objects. TRUNCATION WARNING (Section 10): summarized fetch tools cut these large scoreboard JSONs (a 15-game slate rendered as 6) - for slate counts/completeness fetch the JSON via direct shell (Invoke-RestMethod/curl) and count programmatically.
- StatMuse (statmuse.com) - natural-language stat lookups for US sports (required first stat stop for NBA/WNBA/MLB/NFL/NHL). FULL ACCESS PROTOCOL:

  STATMUSE ACCESS PROTOCOL (verified working 2026-06-10):
  - URL PATTERN: https://www.statmuse.com/{league}/ask/{question-with-hyphens} - write the question in plain English, lowercase, spaces replaced with hyphens, no punctuation. Verified league paths: nba, wnba, mlb. Additional paths (nfl, nhl, pga, cfb, fc for soccer) follow the same pattern - verify on first use each session. Example: statmuse.com/mlb/ask/yankees-record-last-10-games.
  - The page is server-rendered and fetch-friendly: it returns a one-sentence ANSWER at the top (e.g. "The New York Yankees have a record of 6-4 in their last 10 games") plus a game-by-game or stat table underneath. Read BOTH - the table is the evidence; the sentence alone can hide a misparse.
  - HIGH-VALUE QUERY TEMPLATES for the card workflow (slot into GATE 6 recency stack and GATE 7 projection):
    * Team form: "{team} record last 10 games" (returns game-by-game results with scores - doubles as a last-N scores source).
    * Scoring environment: "{team} points per game this season" / "{team} runs per game last 10 games" / "{team} opponent points per game this season" (defense).
    * PHASE SPLITS (critical for Q1/1H markets): "{team} 1st quarter points per game this season" / "{team} 1st quarter points per game last 5 games" / "{team} first half points per game this season". Quarter-level data confirmed back to 2006 (WNBA) and supported for NBA; combine both teams' phase averages for the combined-environment anchor.
    * Head-to-head: "{team A} record vs {team B} this season" (returns each meeting with date and score - use for same-season H2H only; remember multi-season H2H is context, never the anchor).
    * Players/props: "{player} points per game last 10 games", "{player} era and whip this season", "{pitcher} last 5 starts", "{player} home runs vs {team} this season".
    * Splits: "{team} home record this season", "{team} points per game on the road last 10 games".
  - FRESHNESS BEHAVIOR: StatMuse is a stats/context layer, not a live authority. It can update when games go FINAL, but 2026-06-10 deep-research checks found stale/mis-timed StatMuse outputs in some MLB/NHL/NFL-style queries (e.g. last-10 table not reaching the latest completed game; "tonight" resolving to an old slate; occasional 403). FRESHNESS CHECK: read the most recent date row in the returned table and confirm it matches the team's latest completed game from the official schedule; if the latest game is missing, the cache is behind - re-fetch, use official/stat-site alternatives, or mark StatMuse as context only.
  - MISPARSE GUARD: StatMuse sometimes answers a near-miss interpretation (career instead of season, wrong timeframe, wrong player with similar name). Always check the answer sentence restates the intended team/timeframe/stat; if not, rephrase with explicit stat name and window (e.g. add "this season" / "last 10 games").
  - LIMITATIONS / COMPLIANCE: stats ONLY - no decisive injuries, no lineups/inactives, no live scores, no schedules of unplayed games; no coverage of KBO/NPB/cricket/AFL/NRL/Euro-domestic basketball (use the league-specific stacks in this directory). StatMuse public pages are not a high-frequency scraping API; if automated production use is required, use an approved/licensed API path. Any odds/betting content on the page is ignored in research-only mode.
  - FALLBACKS if a StatMuse query fails or misparses: Basketball-Reference / Baseball-Reference / Pro-Football-Reference / Hockey-Reference (deep splits), ESPN site API team/event endpoints (current state), NBA.com/stats and FanGraphs (advanced), team game logs on official league sites.

------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 5. EVIDENCE-CITED REASONING REQUIREMENT (reasoning must trace to fresh, sourced facts)
------------------------------------------------------------
- For AT MINIMUM the #1 and #4 picks (ideally all), the card must state: the decisive fact -> its source -> its timestamp/recency -> access level. Example: "#1 anchored on: Bangladesh 62/0 mandatory powerplay [Cricbuzz live, opened 21:45 AEST, LIVE]"; "#4 fade because: Judge confirmed OUT pregame [NBA injury report 5:30pm ET PDF, OPENED]".
- Access-level discipline: OPENED current page/API > OPENED dated article > SNIPPET > ASSUMED (memory/general knowledge). ASSUMED facts cannot support a #1 pick or a #4 fade; SNIPPET facts cap confidence and must be marked.
- If the decisive fact for any slot is UNKNOWN (lineup not out, pitch report unavailable, corner source missing), say UNKNOWN explicitly, cap confidence, and do not let that slot be the anchor.
- Recency beats authority when they conflict ON CURRENT STATE (a live official page lagging behind a reputable final scorecard - RULE AD); authority beats recency on RULES/settlement conventions.
- This requirement exists because penalty post-mortems repeatedly trace to a decisive "fact" that was stale (venue par, old H2H, day-old availability) or assumed (format, line orientation, weather). Citing forces the check.

------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 6. TOP/BOTTOM PENALTY ELIMINATION PROTOCOL (the core ranking upgrade)
------------------------------------------------------------
TARGETS: top-pick hit rate >= 80% sustained (currently ~82.7% - protect it), bottom-pick win rate <= 30% (currently ~46.7% - this is the entire adjusted-record deficit). Review these as KPIs on every sweep.

6.1 WRITTEN PROBABILITY TABLE (mandatory, GATE 9): write an independent probability next to EVERY option before final ranking (overlapping options need not sum to 100, but each must be justified by a named mechanism, not vibes). No table = no card.
6.2 SLOT REQUIREMENTS:
- Slot #1 requires >=60% genuine probability AND a named mechanism AND a fresh (Section 3) decisive fact. If nothing clears 60%, say "no true anchor on this card" and cap confidence card-wide.
- Slot #4 (or #8) requires <=30% probability AND the most independent failure paths, written out. If the best candidate is 30-40%, label "FORCED BOTTOM SLOT - no genuine least-likely outcome" and cap confidence (complementary-pair honesty).
6.3 THE SWAP TEST: if P(#3) and P(#4) are within ~10 points, they are interchangeable - flag forced bottom. If P(#4) > 35%, STOP and re-rank; something on the card is more wrong than the bottom slot.
6.4 SEPARATION TEST: require >=20 points between P(#1) and P(#4). Less than that = the card has no real edge; present it as low-edge and cap language accordingly.
6.5 LEGITIMATE #4 CANDIDATES (the only things that belong there):
   (a) STRUCTURAL near-impossibilities: chasing-side total far above the target (chase-cap rule), a handicap whose orientation is backwards vs reality (Rule N), a side needing a 16+ swing from the league's worst team (Storm -15.5 class), markets requiring an event the format forbids.
   (b) Outcomes requiring 3+ INDEPENDENT failures to land (e.g. elite home favourite losing by 2+ when healthy, in form, AND opponent depleted).
   (c) True tail phases: 1H Under 0.5 in a verified MISMATCH (not near-equal) fixture; a quarter/PP total 2+ scoring units outside both teams' current phase range.
   (d) The far side of a line your projection clears by >1.5 scoring units WITH a fresh mechanism (not venue par alone).
6.6 THE FORBIDDEN-#4 LIST (the 70 penalties, condensed - if the candidate matches ANY of these, it is NOT the bottom pick):
   - A modest over INSIDE the projected band (the single most repeated penalty).
   - Either +1.5/+2.5 run/point cushion when the projected game is close or low-scoring.
   - A home/quality favourite's plain win (ML) with ordinary win paths.
   - A Q1/1H/phase under when the projection straddles the line or the opener is structurally slow.
   - The complement of ANY line your projection sits within ~1 scoring unit of (coinflip burial).
   - The favourite cover against a CRISIS opponent (multiple core outs + coaching turmoil + losing streak) - that cover is live, not a fade.
   - The repeat-blowout path in a series where Game 1 was a blowout with low phases (Juventus-Zalgiris class).
   - The over/up-side in a winner-take-all decider between matched teams (deciders lean UP toward the series high + OT risk).
   - A motivated relegation/survival side's cushion in a late-season game against a safe opponent.
6.7 TOP-SLOT STRESS TEST (the 26 penalties): before locking #1, write its single most likely KILL PATH and estimate that path's probability. If >25-30%, downgrade or re-rank. Mandatory checks:
   (a) ANCHOR CLASS - is #1 built on current-season/last-3 evidence (acceptable) or on venue par / multi-season H2H / season averages / preview adjectives (NOT acceptable as anchor - June log: Mirpur 251.5, Hofstade 165.5, Auckland-Canterbury 171 H2H all burned this)?
   (b) AVAILABILITY DEPENDENCE - does #1 lean on an unconfirmed status? (Judge class scratch risk.)
   (c) FORMAT/LINE SANITY - reduced overs? backwards handicap? first-10 line that is really a full innings?
   (d) GAME-STATE - PREGAME confirmed via Section 2? (Do not pregame-rank a live/finished game.)
   (e) COINFLIP HONESTY - if the model projection sits ON the line (Stats Insider 178 vs 179.5 class), #1 cannot be that total; pick a structural item instead.
6.8 STRUCTURAL-ANCHOR PRIORITY: when the card contains a structural near-lock (6.5a), it MUST occupy #1 (and its mirror the #4/#8 slot where applicable). Do not spend a structural lock mid-card.
6.9 EIGHT-OPTION CARDS: treat as two stacked 4-cards. Extremes (#1/#8) take the structural/most-separated items. NEVER stack all three unders (or overs) in the top half off one factor - June 9-10 evidence punished this four times (Aces-Storm, Netanya-Nes Ziona, Juventus-Zalgiris totals, Raanana-Galil). Apply the PRE-RANK TOTALS-DIRECTION GATE to every totals pair, and run the mandatory review trigger if all top-4 lose.
6.10 CONFIDENCE-WEIGHTED GRADING (existing rules preserved): bottom-two losses = expected, half-weight, no introspection. #1 loss and/or #4 win = full-weight failure -> serious retrospective with ONE concrete rule change; both-top-two losses -> comprehensive review trigger. TOP-HALF SWEEP EXEMPTION (2026-06-12): if every pick in the top half wins (#1-#2 on 4-option cards; #1-#4 on 8-option cards), record any bottom-pick win as a normal item result but do not add the extra bottom-pick penalty. One-goal totals near-misses stay penalty-exempt per the 2026-06-09 caveat (bottom-pick loss exception preserved).
6.11 CALIBRATION LOOP: every settlement sweep, recount rolling top hit rate and bottom win rate over the last 20 cards. If bottom > 35% rolling, tighten the swap test to 15 points and require structural-class (#6.5a/b) candidates only at #4 until the rate drops back under 30%.

------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 7. BLINDSPOT FIXES - 2026-06-10 SECOND-PASS AUDIT (structural gaps the existing rules did not cover)
------------------------------------------------------------
7.1 EXTREME-SLOT PAIR ASSIGNMENT RULE (double-penalty prevention - HIGHEST PRIORITY NEW RULE).
- THE BLINDSPOT: when #1 and #4 are the two sides of the SAME line (e.g. #1 Innings Under 251.5 / #4 Innings Over 251.5), ONE wrong directional call triggers BOTH the top-pick penalty AND the bottom-pick penalty simultaneously. Four cards in the June 5-10 window were double-penalized through exactly this construction: Bangladesh-Australia (Under/Over 251.5 at #1/#4), Antwerp-Akcel (165.5), Liege-Akcel (first-6 42.5), JB Bruges-Liege (first-10 104.5). Expected penalties for same-pair-at-extremes = 2 x P(direction wrong); for split construction = P(top market wrong) + P(bottom market wrong) but never two penalties from ONE mistake.
- THE RULE: on a card containing two (or more) complementary pairs, assign #1 and #4 to the pair with the STRONGEST directional confidence; the weaker/coinflip pair sits at #2/#3. Same-pair-at-extremes is permitted ONLY when the direction is structural-class (Section 6.5a: chase-cap, backwards line, format-forced) with P(wrong) under ~15% - then it is optimal. If NO pair clears ~65% directional confidence, say "no extreme-worthy pair on this card", put the least-coinflip pair at the extremes anyway, and cap confidence in writing.
- COROLLARY: a single directional thesis must never be allowed to cost two penalties unless it is the single most defensible read on the card.
7.2 FREQUENCY-COUNT PROBABILITY REQUIREMENT (probabilities must be counted, not narrated).
- THE BLINDSPOT: Section 6 demands a probability table, but nothing forced the numbers to come from data. Penalty post-mortems show estimates were narrative-derived ("strong defense, lean under ~70%").
- THE RULE: for every option, COUNT the hit rate of that exact market over the recency stack before adjusting: "Q1 over 43.5 hit in 6 of this team's last 10 (and 5 of opponent's last 10) -> ~55-60% prior" then adjust for availability/venue/pace with stated reasons. StatMuse phase/last-N queries (Section 4 protocol) make this countable for US sports; league pages and logged phase splits cover the rest. An option with no countable base goes to the table as UNKNOWN-prior with capped confidence - it cannot occupy #1 or #4.
7.3 GRADEABILITY PRE-CHECK (do not stake extreme slots on unverifiable legs).
- THE BLINDSPOT: corner legs and minor-league phase legs repeatedly finished UNGRADED (Philippines-Myanmar, China-Thailand corners; NED-USA first-5) - they consume slots, cannot be learned from, and skew card construction.
- THE RULE: before ranking, check that a settlement source EXISTS for each leg (corners: TotalCorner/explicit-stat pages cover major comps but often NOT friendlies/minor leagues; cricket phase: needs over-by-over or live capture). Flag LOW-GRADEABILITY legs in the card and keep them OUT of #1 and #4 - put gradeable legs at the extremes. If the user's four options force an ungradeable leg to an extreme, say so pregame.
7.4 SETTLEMENT-CONVENTION CHECK (rank the market that will actually be graded).
- THE BLINDSPOT: no gate verified market conventions; phantom edges arise from misread settlement rules.
- THE RULE: before ranking, state the convention for each market: basketball totals/spreads INCLUDE OT; soccer markets are 90-minutes-plus-stoppage only (no ET) unless stated; NHL totals include OT/SO result goal; whole-number lines can PUSH (state the push number); cricket totals follow the reduced/DLS state if overs change (Rule R); abandoned-match handling per Rules F/AB. One line in the card: "CONVENTIONS: OT included / 90' only / push at X / DLS-sensitive."
7.5 SOCCER THREE-WAY AND WINNER-LEAN DISCIPLINE (the draw is a first-class outcome).
- THE BLINDSPOT: winner leans were two-way even in near-equal soccer; China-Thailand (0-0) punished a "Thailand narrowly" lean where the DRAW was the modal outcome. Winner leans across sports also repeatedly missed without consequence-tracking.
- THE RULE: every soccer winner lean must state THREE probabilities (home/draw/away); in near-equal or defensive/wet matchups the draw is often 28-35% and can be the largest single outcome - say so rather than forcing a side. ALL sports: a winner lean under ~55% must be labelled "lean only, near-coinflip"; do not write "narrowly" as a hedge - write the number.
7.6 LINE-AS-EVIDENCE GATE (the offered line is information, not just a target).
- THE BLINDSPOT: lines that contradicted my anchor were treated as wrong instead of informative (NZ NBL 95.5 vs stale 171-H2H; first-10 104.5 encoding a T10 format; Essendon-Carlton backwards orientation caught only by Rule N).
- THE RULE: when the offered line sits MORE THAN ~1.5 scoring units from the GATE 7 projection, write one sentence answering "what does the line-setter know that my anchor does not?" (format, lineup news, venue change, market info). Only fade the line after that sentence names and dismisses the candidate explanations with current sources. A big line-vs-projection gap is a FORMAT/NEWS ALARM first and an edge second.
7.7 LOG-FIRST, COPY-VERBATIM RULE (mechanical fix for chat-vs-log inversions).
- THE BLINDSPOT: three documented cards had the chat answer INVERT the logged ranking (would have flipped 2-2 into 2-4 or vice versa). The cause is re-deriving the ranking while writing the chat answer.
- THE RULE: finalize the ranking ONCE - write the log row first, then copy the ranking VERBATIM into the chat response. Never re-type from memory, never "improve" the order while presenting. If a late fact arrives mid-write, update the LOG first, then re-copy.
7.8 STATMUSE SEASON-SCOPE GUARD (playoffs vs regular season).
- THE BLINDSPOT: "this season" StatMuse queries typically resolve to the REGULAR season; during playoffs/finals the relevant sample is playoff games (different pace, rotations, intensity).
- THE RULE: in any postseason card, query BOTH ("...this season" AND "...in the 2026 playoffs" / "last 5 games"), check the returned table rows are the intended games, and anchor on the playoff/most-recent sample per the recency stack. Never mix regular-season phase averages into a finals phase model without saying so.
7.9 VOID/ABANDONMENT PRE-FLAG (generalized from the KBO rain rule).
- THE RULE: when weather/curfew/light/political risk gives >10-15% chance the match does not reach a normal full state, write a VOID-RISK line pregame naming which legs survive partial completion (completed-phase legs) and which die (full-match legs). Prefer survivable legs for the extreme slots in high void-risk cards - synergy with 7.3 gradeability.
7.10 ACCESS-FLUCTUATION RULE (single fetch failure is not "unavailable").
- THE BLINDSPOT: sources flip between open and blocked day to day (2026-06-10: Cricbuzz and NDTV blocked despite opening the previous day; WNBA.com timing out while ESPN twin page opened instantly).
- THE RULE: before writing UNKNOWN for a decisive fact, walk the fallback chain: alternate domain -> structured API -> reader proxy (Section 8) -> dated search snippets (orientation only). Record which rung worked. Declare UNKNOWN only after the chain is exhausted, and retry blocked primaries next session rather than writing them off permanently.
7.11 AFL LIVE-TOTAL PHASE STABILITY RULE (added 2026-06-12 from Adelaide 121, Western Bulldogs 64).
- THE BLINDSPOT: a low early live scoreboard before Q1 stabilized led to burying Over 169.5, but Adelaide's pressure/territory dominance turned into a 56-point first quarter and a 185 total. Both Under 189.5 and Over 169.5 cashed, making the overlapping band the real edge rather than a one-sided under.
- THE RULE: in AFL live cards, do not use a low early scoreboard snapshot alone to put a moderate over in the bottom slot. Wait for Q1 confirmation or keep overlapping total bands adjacent unless live territory, scoring shots, conversion, weather, and team-quality data all clearly suppress the scoring tail.

SECTION 8. LIVE ACCESS TEST MATRIX AND BOT-BLOCK WORKAROUND PLAYBOOK (late 2026-06-10 direct probes + deep-research reconciliation)
------------------------------------------------------------
CORE ACCESS RULES (late 2026-06-10 reconciliation from live probes + deep-research reports):
- HTTP 200 is NOT enough. Classify every fetch as PASS_FRESH, PASS_CONTEXT_ONLY, STALE, BLOCKED, INVALID, or PASS_TRUNCATED (Section 10: the page opened fresh but a summarized fetch cut the body - counts and completeness claims from it are invalid) after checking date, source timestamp, expected body/schema, and block markers (captcha/login/Cloudflare/Access Denied/empty JS shell).
- Exact-date or date-path access is mandatory when available. Generic scoreboards often return source-local "today" rather than AEST today (ESPN MLB/NHL/WNBA examples); capture source-local date/time first, then convert to AEST.
- Official-first does not mean official-blind. Official NBA injury PDFs were current while some NBA CDN scoreboard-style data can be stale; NHL api-web opened in later testing after earlier 403; KBO English pages can redirect to error while Korean official pages open.
- Do not fight blocks. If a site presents CAPTCHA/auth/403/dynamic shell, switch to the next approved source rung instead of re-hammering or bypassing.

VERIFIED OPEN / STRONG WHEN FRESH (re-tested 2026-06-10 from this environment):
- ESPN scoreboards opened for NBA, WNBA, MLB, NHL, AFL, NFL, and soccer competitions tested; exact-date calls opened for the tested sports where used, even when the date had no events. Use ?dates=YYYYMMDD where supported. ESPN rugby-league/NRL endpoints failed.
- MLB Stats API opened for date 06/10/2026 and returned 15 games; use as MLB machine-primary when same-day health check passes, backed by MLB official starting lineups/probables/injury pages.
- Official NBA injury-report landing page opened and discovered current dated PDF; ak-static.cms.nba.com injury PDF opened. WNBA official injury report opened; RotoWire WNBA injury report opened as fallback.
- NHL api-web schedule endpoint opened in later testing; use when fresh, with ESPN NHL as cross-check and game-specific/beat confirmation for goalies.
- AFL injury list opened; AFL/club pages remain primary for teams/late changes.
- Cricbuzz live scores opened and exposed scorecard text; ICC fixtures opened. ESPNcricinfo direct remained 403 but r.jina.ai/https://www.espncricinfo.com/live-cricket-score opened.
- Guardian football and ESPN soccer API opened; TotalCorner schedule opened and remains the explicit-corner source.
- ZeroTackle team lists and injuries opened for NRL. Use club/league-media/late-mail confirmation because NRL.com automation is blocked.
- KBO Korean official schedule opened; English KBO pages may error. NPB BIS English games page opened; use BIS English as first English NPB path.
- Winner League and LKL official pages opened; FIBA LiveStats root 404 is expected because LiveStats is game-specific.
- Open-Meteo opened with hourly Australia/Sydney output; use exact venue coordinates and match-window hours.
- StatMuse opened for sample US-sports stat queries, but deep checks found stale/mis-timed outputs in some query types; use as stats context only after table-date validation.

BLOCKED / THIN / TERTIARY ONLY (late 2026-06-10):

Use official X API if automating, official/team page mirrors when available, or search snippets only as discovery. LATE-DAY RETEST: x.com and publish.x.com/oembed returned HTTP 402 hard blocks and syndication.twitter.com was empty/429 - Section 10 supersedes this bullet with the full chain.
- NRL.com draw/team-list/news pages returned CAPTCHA/auth-style barriers; ESPN NRL/rugby-league endpoints failed. Use official club sources, ZeroTackle, Legz, Fox/ABC/major AU media, and credentialed late-mail reporters.
- ESPNcricinfo direct returned 403; use Cricbuzz/ICC/boards first, then r.jina.ai only for public no-login ESPNcricinfo pages when it opens.
- NDTV cricket live scores returned 403 in later testing; keep Sky/CREX/Cricbuzz/CricTracker match-specific pages as alternates.
- Sofascore returned 403 in this environment and Flashscore showed dynamic/login-heavy markers; reports found they can sometimes render usable content. Treat both as tertiary, session-tested cross-checks only, never source of record.
- Footlive connection closed unexpectedly in this environment; Guardian/official/ESPN soccer/TotalCorner are preferred.
- Nitter-style mirrors were unreliable (nitter.net empty; xcancel 403). Do not build process around them.

PROXY / CACHE / MONITORING RULES:
- r.jina.ai is a LAST-RESORT reader for public, no-login pages when direct fetch is blocked. It may cache-miss or fail and does not work on every site. Never use it for login-walled/private/paywalled material, and never let proxied content settle a decisive fact without a second source when a primary exists.
- Wayback Machine can orient on blocked pages, but snapshots can be hours/days old. NEVER settle from an archive timestamp older than the event end or use it for late lineup/injury facts.
- For health checks, log URL, HTTP status, content type, fetched_at, parsed source date, parsed source timestamp, event IDs, and a response/content hash. Alert if a normally fresh source returns stale date, empty shell, schema change, or block marker twice in a row.
- At first use of a critical source each session, treat the first response as an access test; on failure walk the 7.10 fallback chain instead of re-hammering the same URL.
- When multiple primaries fail in one session, or quarterly, re-run this matrix and update this section with the date-stamped results. Access statements in Section 4 carry their test date; newer test results override older claims.

SECTION 9. X/TWITTER, REDDIT, AND SOCIAL-SIGNAL VERIFICATION GATE (late-news layer, not source-of-record by default)
------------------------------------------------------------
PURPOSE: Use social sources for facts websites miss or publish late: lineup graphics, late scratches, warmup observations, starting goalies, final 17s/23s, toss and Playing XI, pitch reports, club travel/availability notes, coach comments, import clearances, weather/delay reports, and local-language beat updates.

ACCESS REALITY (tested 2026-06-10):
- Direct x.com profile and search fetches returned large JavaScript shells with "Something went wrong" markers; raw logged-out X access is not a dependable extraction route.
- r.jina.ai can open some public X profile pages, but X search through r.jina.ai was mostly empty/unhelpful. Nitter-style mirrors were unavailable or blocked. Search-engine snippets can discover leads but are SNIPPET only.
- For automated production, use official X API routes and rate limits if credentials/permission exist. Without API access, social checks are manual/browser/search-index discovery and must be labelled accordingly.
- LATE 2026-06-10 RETEST (stricter results override the above): x.com and publish.x.com/oembed returned HTTP 402 hard blocks; syndication.twitter.com returned an empty body via reader and HTTP 429 via direct shell - there is currently NO logged-out X extraction route at all. r.jina.ai opened X profile post TEXT but WITHOUT per-post timestamps: it can confirm a post exists and its wording, never its freshness - grade such facts SNIPPET-equivalent unless the post text itself states the date. Reddit was blocked on EVERY route (www/old/api .json, r.jina.ai proxy, search index, direct shell with browser UA) - treat Reddit as UNAVAILABLE for automation and write "SOCIAL CHECK: reddit unavailable" rather than implying it was checked. The Bluesky public API is a VERIFIED OPEN structured social rung - full playbook in Section 10.

SOURCE TIERS:
- X-OFFICIAL / Tier A: league, team, team PR, league-media, federation, official competition, official club/federation lineup graphics, or organization-affiliated accounts. These can confirm low-ambiguity facts when the post is opened/current and the account identity is linked or obvious.
- X-BEAT / Tier B: credentialed beat reporter or recognized national/local reporter directly reporting a coach/team statement, warmup observation, lineup card, goalie confirmation, late mail, toss/XI, or injury status. Prefer two independent beat/official confirmations for decisive facts.
- X-AGG / Tier C: aggregator accounts reposting other reporting. Use only to discover the original source.
- X-RUMOR / Tier D: fan accounts, blue-check-only accounts, Reddit/forum posts, Discord-style chatter, anonymous tips. Discovery only; cannot anchor #1 or #4 and cannot settle a fact.

VERIFICATION RULES:
- Blue check is not verification. Organizational affiliation, official account linkage, reporter credential/employer history, and original sourcing matter more.
- Social facts must include: account/handle, account tier, post timestamp, fetched/opened timestamp, exact claim, and whether the post is original reporting, official statement, repost, or interpretation.
- A social claim can be OPENED only when the actual post/account page or official API result was opened in the current run. Search-engine snippets are SNIPPET; memory of a reporter's post is ASSUMED.
- For injuries, scratches, minutes/snap/TOI limits, starting goalie/pitcher, cricket XI, soccer XI, AFL/NRL final teams, or import/eligibility clearance: require official confirmation OR two independent high-trust confirmations before it can support #1/#4. If only one beat post exists, label UNKNOWN or PROVISIONAL and cap confidence.
- For NRL and smaller domestic leagues where official websites are blocked/thin, social can be more important but not looser: official club posts, club sites, team-list graphics, broadcaster late mail, and credentialed reporters form the cross-check chain.
- Reddit is radar only. Use it to find links, local reports, or venue chatter, then verify from the original source. Never use Reddit/fan comments as source of record. ACCESS NOTE (late 2026-06-10): every automated Reddit route was blocked in this environment (see Section 10); until a route reopens, Reddit checks are manual-only - state "reddit unavailable" instead of claiming radar coverage.
- Do not use social to infer medical clearance from a training photo, travel photo, warmup appearance, or player self-post. Classify active/available/starting/normal role separately.

SPORT-SPECIFIC SOCIAL USE:
- NBA/WNBA: official injury reports control; use team PR and beat reporters for late scratches, minutes limits, starters, and role changes close to tip.
- MLB: official lineup/probable pages control; use team PR/beat reporters for late scratches, opener/bulk changes, catcher/order changes, weather/roof, and bullpen availability.
- NHL: official game center plus team/warmup reporters for starting goalies, scratches, line combinations, and power-play roles; DailyFaceoff is projection until confirmed.
- NFL: official injury/inactive reports control; use team PR/beat reporters for warmup limitations, snap-count expectations, and late inactive context.
- AFL: AFL/club pages control; use club X and verified reporters for late outs, substitute, managed players, and warmup withdrawals.
- NRL: club posts, team-list graphics, broadcaster late mail, ZeroTackle/Fox/Legz, and verified reporters are mandatory because NRL.com automation is brittle.
- Cricket: official board/ICC/Cricbuzz scorecard controls; use team/board X and credentialed cricket reporters for toss, XI, pitch report, weather delay, replacement, and captain comments.
- Soccer: official competition/club lineup graphics and team sheets control; use club/federation X and credentialed reporters for warmup withdrawals, formation/rotation, and local-language team news.
- KBO/NPB: official league/club pages control; use club accounts and local reporters for game-day lineup, starter changes, injury exits, and roster moves.
- Domestic basketball: official league/game center controls; use club/league accounts and local reporters for import clearance, roster absences, coach comments, and final team sheets.

OUTPUT RULE:
- Every card with a social-dependent fact must show one line: "SOCIAL CHECK: [none found / official opened / beat opened / snippets only / unavailable], controlling account/source, timestamp, and confidence effect." If social access is blocked or unverified and the fact matters, cap confidence and keep it out of #1/#4.
