[3]: https://ojs.srce.hr/index.php/kinesiology/article/view/29293/16971 "29293_Silvino.indd"
[4]: https://www.statsperform.com/resource/expected-goals-xg-the-football-metric-changing-analysis-betting-and-fan-engagement/ "Expected Goals (xG): The Football Metric Changing Analysis, Betting, and Fan Engagement "
[5]: https://www.hudl.com/blog/possession-value-models-explained "What is Expected Threat (xT)? Possession Value models explained"
[6]: https://github.com/metrica-sports/sample-data "GitHub - metrica-sports/sample-data: Metrica Sports sample tracking and event data · GitHub"
[7]: https://www.theifab.com/ "International Football Association Board | Laws of the Game | IFAB"
[8]: https://www.fifpro.org/articles/2021/07/extreme-weather-in-football "Extreme Weather in Football"
[9]: https://opensportssciencesjournal.com/VOLUME/10/PAGE/52/FULLTEXT/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Fatigue and Recovery in Soccer: Evidence and Challenges"
[10]: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1802.07127 "Actions Speak Louder than Goals: Valuing Player Actions in Soccer"
[11]: https://blogarchive.statsbomb.com/news/introducing-on-ball-value-obv/ "Introducing On-Ball Value (OBV) • Statsbomb Blog Archive"


For cricket, build the app around **format-specific context + ball-by-ball data + player role profiles + pitch/weather/toss conditions + matchup modelling**. Cricket is more context-dependent than soccer because the value of a player’s action changes massively by **format, innings, phase, ground size, pitch, ball age, dew, wickets in hand, required run rate and matchup**.

Cricsheet’s public ball-by-ball structure is a good reference model: it stores match metadata such as city, competition, dates, gender, match type, teams, toss winner/decision and umpires, then innings and delivery-level data with batter, bowler, non-striker, runs, wickets and extras. ([cricsheet.org][1])

## 1. Core cricket data structure

### A. Match metadata

| Category       | Necessary fields                                                                                             |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Competition    | Test, ODI, T20I, franchise T20, domestic, World Cup, bilateral series, knockout, league stage                |
| Format         | overs per innings, balls per over, innings count, follow-on rules, Super Over rules, DLS availability        |
| Match          | match ID, date, start time, timezone, day/night flag, pink/red/white ball                                    |
| Teams          | home/away/neutral, captain, coach, playing XI, squad, substitutes, impact/replacement rules                  |
| Toss           | toss winner, decision, bat/bowl choice, whether decision matched venue trend                                 |
| Match state    | innings, score, wickets, overs, target, required run rate, DLS par, resources remaining                      |
| Series context | dead rubber, decider, must-win, qualification scenario, net run rate pressure                                |
| Rules          | powerplay structure, fielding restrictions, short-ball limits, bouncer rules, over-rate penalties, DRS rules |

The ICC’s playing conditions define DLS as the Duckworth/Lewis/Stern method for setting targets in interrupted matches, and the ICC describes DLS as the method used to recalculate totals when time is lost due to weather interruptions. 

## 2. Ball-by-ball event data

This should be the heart of your app. Every model should be able to trace back to individual deliveries.

| Field             | Examples                                                             |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| match_id          | unique match                                                         |
| innings_number    | 1, 2, 3, 4                                                           |
| over_ball         | 12.4                                                                 |
| legal_ball_number | legal delivery count                                                 |
| batter_id         | striker                                                              |
| non_striker_id    | non-striker                                                          |
| bowler_id         | bowler                                                               |
| wicketkeeper_id   | keeper                                                               |
| fielding_team_id  | bowling side                                                         |
| batting_team_id   | batting side                                                         |
| runs_batter       | runs off bat                                                         |
| runs_extras       | extras                                                               |
| runs_total        | total delivery runs                                                  |
| extras_type       | wide, no-ball, bye, leg-bye, penalty                                 |
| wicket            | true/false                                                           |
| dismissal_type    | bowled, caught, lbw, run out, stumped, hit wicket                    |
| fielder_id        | catcher/run-out/stumping involvement                                 |
| shot_type         | drive, cut, pull, sweep, reverse sweep, ramp                         |
| bowling_type      | pace, seam, swing, off-spin, leg-spin, left-arm orthodox, wrist spin |
| line_length       | line, length, yorker, bouncer, short, good length, full              |
| ball_speed        | release speed                                                        |
| swing/seam/spin   | movement metrics if available                                        |
| pitch_x/pitch_y   | where ball pitched                                                   |
| impact_x/impact_y | impact point                                                         |
| wagon_x/wagon_y   | shot destination                                                     |
| boundary_flag     | four/six                                                             |
| dot_ball          | true/false                                                           |
| phase             | powerplay, middle, death; or session for Tests                       |
| pressure_state    | required run rate, wickets left, balls left                          |
| DLS_state         | par score, resources remaining                                       |
| data_source       | manual/API/tracking/video                                            |
| confidence        | verified/estimated/uncertain                                         |

Cricsheet’s delivery data includes batter, bowler, non-striker, runs, wickets, extras and replacement events, which makes it a strong open-source benchmark for your app’s delivery schema. ([cricsheet.org][1])

## 3. Format-specific modelling

Cricket analysis must split heavily by format.

| Format             | What matters most                                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| T20                | phase hitting, matchup advantage, death bowling, powerplay wickets, boundary %, dot-ball %, bowling plans           |
| ODI                | top-order stability, middle-over control, spin matchup, death overs, DLS/weather, chasing profile                   |
| Test               | pitch deterioration, session-by-session control, bowling workload, new-ball spells, reverse swing, spin on days 4–5 |
| The Hundred/T10    | extreme strike-rate pressure, immediate boundary ability, bowling over/set allocation                               |
| Women’s cricket    | same structure, but model separately because scoring distributions, venues and player pools differ                  |
| Domestic/franchise | overseas-player availability, travel, short turnarounds, local venue familiarity                                    |

A big mistake would be using the same “batting average + bowling average” model across T20, ODI and Test cricket. CricViz’s own modern player metrics split batting into Power, Attack and Timing, and bowling into Threat, Control and Variation, because basic strike rate/economy do not properly account for batter quality, grounds, phase or match situation. ([CricViz][2])

## 4. Player-level stats

### A. Player profile

| Area             | Stats/fields                                                                          |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Identity         | player ID, name, age, nationality, domestic team, international team                  |
| Role             | batter, bowler, all-rounder, wicketkeeper, finisher, anchor, powerplay bowler         |
| Batting hand     | right/left                                                                            |
| Bowling arm      | right/left                                                                            |
| Bowling style    | fast, fast-medium, medium, off-spin, leg-spin, left-arm orthodox, left-arm wrist-spin |
| Fielding role    | keeper, slip, ring fielder, boundary rider, specialist catcher                        |
| Fitness          | injury status, return date, workload restriction, recent bowling load                 |
| Selection status | confirmed XI, squad only, likely substitute, overseas availability                    |
| Experience       | caps, matches by format, pressure-match experience                                    |
| Form window      | last 5, last 10, last 20 innings/matches, rolling career trend                        |

### B. Batter stats

| Category             | Necessary stats                                                                                    |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Traditional          | runs, average, strike rate, balls faced, innings, not outs                                         |
| Recent form          | last 5/10/20 innings, runs, strike rate, dismissals, starts converted                              |
| Phase split          | powerplay SR, middle-over SR, death-over SR                                                        |
| Innings split        | batting first vs chasing, home/away/neutral, day/night                                             |
| Match situation      | performance after early wicket, high required run rate, low chase, high chase                      |
| Boundary profile     | 4s, 6s, boundary %, balls per boundary                                                             |
| Dot-ball profile     | dot-ball %, rotation %, singles %, twos %, pressure-release ability                                |
| Dismissals           | bowled, lbw, caught behind, caught in deep, stumped, run out                                       |
| Bowling matchup      | vs pace, spin, left-arm pace, right-arm pace, off-spin, leg-spin, left-arm orthodox                |
| Line/length weakness | short ball, yorker, wide line, full swing, good length, bodyline                                   |
| Venue split          | average/SR by venue, boundary size suitability                                                     |
| Pitch split          | flat, green, turning, slow, two-paced, bouncy                                                      |
| Ball age split       | new ball, middle overs, old ball                                                                   |
| Pressure             | knockout record, chase record, final-over record, death hitting                                    |
| Advanced             | expected runs, runs above expected, false-shot %, control %, attacking-shot %, timing/power rating |

### C. Bowler stats

| Category          | Necessary stats                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Traditional       | wickets, bowling average, economy, strike rate, overs                                |
| Recent form       | last 5/10/20 matches, wickets, economy, phase usage                                  |
| Phase split       | powerplay economy/wickets, middle-over control, death economy/wickets                |
| Delivery type     | yorker %, bouncer %, slower ball %, cutter %, googly %, carrom ball %, wide yorker   |
| Line/length       | good-length %, full %, short %, wide line %, stump line %                            |
| Wicket type       | bowled, lbw, caught behind, caught deep, stumped                                     |
| Control           | wides, no-balls, boundary balls, dot-ball %, false-shot induced                      |
| Matchup           | vs RHB/LHB, vs anchors, vs finishers, vs aggressive openers                          |
| Pitch suitability | green pitch, dry turner, slow surface, hard/bouncy deck                              |
| Ball movement     | swing, seam, spin, drift, dip, bounce, release speed                                 |
| Workload          | overs last 7/14/30 days, back-to-back matches, injury risk                           |
| Death skill       | yorker accuracy, slower-ball success, death economy, death wickets                   |
| Advanced          | expected wickets, expected economy, wickets above expected, threat/control/variation |

### D. Wicketkeeper stats

| Area              | Stats                                                |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Keeping           | catches, drops, stumpings, byes conceded             |
| Standing position | up to stumps vs back                                 |
| Spin keeping      | stumpings per chance, missed chances to spin         |
| Pace keeping      | diving catches, leg-side takes, wobble-ball handling |
| Batting           | batting role, strike rate, finishing ability         |
| DRS               | keeper-influenced reviews, successful review calls   |

### E. Fielding stats

| Area              | Stats                                                              |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Catching          | catches, drops, catch difficulty if available                      |
| Ground fielding   | runs saved, misfields, boundary saves                              |
| Throwing          | direct hits, run-out assists, arm strength                         |
| Position          | slip, point, cover, long-on, deep square, keeper                   |
| Pressure fielding | death-over fielding, wet-ball fielding, big-match drops            |
| Advanced          | expected catches, catches above expected, runs saved above average |

## 5. Team-level stats

### A. Team batting

| Area               | Stats                                                                     |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Runs               | average score, median score, score distribution                           |
| Phase scoring      | powerplay RR, middle RR, death RR                                         |
| Wickets            | wickets lost by phase, collapse rate, recovery rate                       |
| Boundary profile   | 4s/6s per innings, boundary %, balls per boundary                         |
| Dot pressure       | dot-ball %, strike rotation, middle-over stagnation                       |
| Chasing            | chase success %, chasing 160/180/200+ in T20, chasing 250/300/350+ in ODI |
| Batting first      | average first-innings score, defendable score profile                     |
| Matchups           | performance vs pace/spin/left-arm/wrist-spin                              |
| Depth              | batting to No. 7/8/9, all-rounder depth                                   |
| Left-right balance | left/right combination availability                                       |
| Recent form        | last 5/10/20 team batting outputs                                         |
| Advanced           | runs above expected, projected score, win probability added               |

### B. Team bowling

| Area           | Stats                                                          |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Economy        | overall and phase economy                                      |
| Wickets        | wickets per phase, strike rate, early-wicket rate              |
| Powerplay      | wickets, economy, swing/seam usage                             |
| Middle overs   | spin control, squeeze rate, dot-ball %                         |
| Death overs    | economy, wickets, yorker success, boundary prevention          |
| Extras         | wides, no-balls, byes, penalty runs                            |
| Matchups       | bowling attack vs opposition batting handedness                |
| Attack balance | pace/spin mix, left/right arm variety, wrist-spin availability |
| Control        | dot-ball %, boundary balls, missed lengths                     |
| Advanced       | expected wickets, expected economy, wickets above expected     |

### C. Team fielding and discipline

| Area            | Stats                                                   |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Catches         | catches, drops, catch efficiency                        |
| Run outs        | direct hits, run-out chances converted                  |
| Ground fielding | runs saved/conceded, misfields                          |
| Over rates      | slow over-rate warnings, penalty risk                   |
| Reviews         | DRS success %, poor reviews, reviews lost early         |
| Discipline      | no-balls, wides, front-foot issues, short-ball warnings |

## 6. Squad, selection and availability

This is one of the most important parts for a prediction app.

| Area               | Necessary fields                                               |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Confirmed XI       | official XI, batting order expectation, bowling roles          |
| Squad strength     | full squad, missing players, replacements                      |
| Injuries           | injured player, body part, severity, return timeline           |
| Workload           | fast-bowler overs, recent travel, back-to-back games           |
| Rest/rotation      | rested stars, managed workload, upcoming finals/series         |
| Role coverage      | backup opener, backup keeper, death bowler, spin option        |
| Overseas players   | franchise availability, international duty, visa/travel issues |
| Balance            | number of batters, bowlers, all-rounders, spinners, pacers     |
| Tactical selection | extra spinner, extra seamer, batting depth, bowling depth      |

## 7. Match officials

Cricket officials are especially important because they affect wides, no-balls, LBWs, light, pitch/ground safety, DRS flow and over-rate enforcement.

The MCC Laws state that two umpires are appointed to control the match impartially, and before the toss they consult captains on balls, hours of play, intervals, the match clock, boundaries, covers and special playing conditions. They also decide if ground, weather or light makes play dangerous or unreasonable. ([Lord's Cricket Ground][3])

| Official feature        | Stats to capture                                          |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| On-field umpires        | names, experience, home/neutral status, format history    |
| Third umpire            | DRS decisions, overturn rate, review speed                |
| Match referee           | over-rate penalties, code-of-conduct history              |
| Wide/no-ball tendency   | wides called per match, no-balls called, short-ball calls |
| LBW profile             | on-field out/not-out LBW rate, overturn rate              |
| DRS profile             | successful reviews, umpire’s-call frequency               |
| Light/weather decisions | bad-light stoppages, wet-ground decisions                 |
| Discipline              | player warnings, penalty runs, conduct reports            |
| Over-rate enforcement   | slow-over penalties, captain sanctions                    |
| Consistency             | strict vs lenient interpretations                         |

## 8. Venue and ground stats

| Category        | Necessary fields                                               |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ground          | venue ID, city, country, altitude, boundary dimensions         |
| Surface         | pitch type: green, dry, hard, slow, two-paced, cracked, dusty  |
| Soil            | clay/sand profile if available                                 |
| Square          | used pitch/new pitch, pitch number, previous matches on square |
| Boundary        | straight boundary, square boundary, longest/shortest side      |
| Scoring history | average first-innings score, median score, winning score range |
| Wicket history  | average wickets per innings, pace wickets vs spin wickets      |
| Chase history   | chasing win %, bat-first win %, toss-decision success          |
| Dew history     | evening dew probability, wet-ball risk                         |
| Weather pattern | humidity, rain risk, wind, heat                                |
| Ball behaviour  | swing early, seam movement, spin later, reverse swing, bounce  |
| Venue bias      | favours pace, spin, power hitters, anchors, chasing sides      |
| Home advantage  | home team win %, travel disadvantage for away side             |

Venue and toss should be explicit model variables. A study on ODI pre-match covariates specifically investigated venue, toss outcome, toss decision and match type as influences on winning chances, while other cricket prediction work commonly includes toss and venue as key pre-match features. ([PMC][4])

## 9. Pitch and ball conditions

| Pitch/ball feature | What to record                                 |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Grass cover        | green, shaved, dry, patchy                     |
| Hardness           | hard, soft, crumbly                            |
| Moisture           | damp, dry, sweating under covers               |
| Cracks             | none, light, widening, uneven bounce risk      |
| Bounce             | low, true, steep, variable                     |
| Pace               | fast, medium, slow, sticky                     |
| Seam               | seam movement level                            |
| Swing              | conventional swing likelihood                  |
| Reverse swing      | old-ball reverse-swing likelihood              |
| Spin               | turn, grip, bounce, rough patches              |
| Ball type          | red, white, pink                               |
| Ball brand         | Kookaburra, Dukes, SG                          |
| Ball age           | new, 10-over, 40-over, 80-over                 |
| Ball change        | new ball taken, replacement ball, damaged ball |
| Outfield           | fast/slow, wet/dry, thick/thin grass           |

## 10. Time of day, weather and conditions

For cricket, weather should be stored at **match start, every 5 overs in white-ball cricket, every session in Tests, and whenever conditions change**.

| Weather/condition | Stats to capture                                           |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Temperature       | air temp, feels-like temp                                  |
| Humidity          | relative humidity, dew point                               |
| Cloud cover       | cloud %, overcast periods                                  |
| Rain              | probability, intensity, radar, stoppage risk               |
| Wind              | speed, gusts, direction across pitch                       |
| Dew               | dew point, grass moisture, evening wet-ball risk           |
| Light             | natural light, floodlights, bad-light risk                 |
| Heat stress       | WBGT if available                                          |
| Pitch moisture    | covers used, sweating, damp patches                        |
| Outfield moisture | wet grass, slow outfield, slipping risk                    |
| Air quality       | smoke, haze, dust                                          |
| DLS impact        | overs lost, revised target, par score, resources remaining |

Weather is not just a postponement issue in cricket; a 2025 ODI weather-impact study specifically combined cricket and weather data and noted the need to account for changes within innings, while another study notes that day-night ODIs can experience dew that makes it harder for spinners to grip the ball. ([Sage Journals][5])

## 11. Toss, innings and match-state modelling

This is much more important in cricket than in most sports.

| Feature           | Why it matters                                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Toss winner       | controls first strategic choice                         |
| Toss decision     | bat/bowl decision reveals pitch/weather expectation     |
| Batting first     | scoreboard pressure, pitch freshness, defendable totals |
| Bowling first     | chasing advantage, dew advantage, early movement        |
| Innings number    | especially important in Tests                           |
| Required run rate | chase pressure                                          |
| Wickets in hand   | resources remaining                                     |
| Balls remaining   | risk/reward calculation                                 |
| DLS par           | weather-affected match state                            |
| Net run rate      | tournament incentives                                   |
| Follow-on         | Test-match tactical decision                            |
| Declaration       | Test-match tactical decision                            |
| New ball due      | Test innings transition                                 |
| Powerplay status  | fielding restriction context                            |

Research on 44,224 matches found that winning the toss increased win probability by about 2.8% overall, but the advantage varied substantially by playing conditions and was larger in some day/night situations. ([arXiv][6])

## 12. Advanced player matchup features

This is where your app can become strong.

| Matchup                | Features                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Batter vs bowler       | historical balls, runs, wickets, strike rate, dot %, boundary %        |
| Batter vs bowling type | vs left-arm pace, wrist spin, off-spin, short ball, yorker             |
| Bowler vs batting hand | RHB/LHB economy, wickets, line strategy                                |
| Venue matchup          | batter’s scoring zones vs boundary dimensions                          |
| Phase matchup          | batter death SR vs bowler death economy                                |
| Fielding matchup       | batter’s aerial zones vs strong boundary fielders                      |
| Pressure matchup       | finisher vs death specialist                                           |
| Spin matchup           | left-hand batter vs off-spin, right-hand batter vs leg-spin            |
| Pace matchup           | short-ball weakness vs express pace                                    |
| Conditions matchup     | swing bowler under cloud, spinner with dry pitch, seamer with new ball |

CricViz’s WinViz is a useful model-design reference: it projects match outcome from the current situation, can be calibrated by team strength and ground history, and is informed by a large T20 results base. ([CricViz][7])

## 13. Tracking, video and computer-vision data

This is an elite layer, but it is where higher-quality apps separate themselves.

| Tracking/video feature | Stats                                                |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Ball tracking          | release speed, swing, seam, spin, bounce, trajectory |
| Pitch map              | line/length, pitching point, impact point            |
| Wagon wheel            | shot direction and distance                          |
| Beehive                | ball passing location near batter                    |
| Shot tracking          | bat contact point, launch angle, shot power          |
| Field placement        | fielder coordinates, ring/deep configuration         |
| Keeper position        | up/back, lateral movement                            |
| Bowler biomechanics    | release height, release angle, run-up speed          |
| Batter movement        | trigger movement, crease position, footwork          |
| Catch difficulty       | distance, reaction time, hang time                   |
| Injury review          | incident tagging and video archive                   |

Hawk-Eye says its data services include player and ball tracking, play-by-play feeds, data-science features such as shot-type classification and shot-phase detection, and analyst systems that combine video review with data. ([Hawk-Eye Innovations][8])

## 14. Derived advanced metrics

| Metric type          | Examples                                                                   |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Batting impact       | runs above expected, strike-rate above expected, phase-adjusted impact     |
| Bowling impact       | wickets above expected, economy above/below expected, threat/control score |
| Win probability      | pre-match, live, over-by-over, ball-by-ball                                |
| Expected runs        | expected score from current state                                          |
| Expected wickets     | wicket probability per ball                                                |
| Expected boundary    | boundary probability per ball                                              |
| Dot-ball value       | dot-ball pressure adjusted by phase                                        |
| Phase value          | powerplay value, middle-over value, death value                            |
| Resource value       | wickets/balls remaining, DLS resources                                     |
| Pressure index       | required run rate + wickets left + batter quality + balls left             |
| Matchup score        | batter-vs-bowler advantage                                                 |
| Pitch-adjusted score | score adjusted for venue and surface difficulty                            |
| Fielding value       | catches above expected, runs saved                                         |
| Selection value      | playing XI strength vs optimal XI                                          |
| Toss value           | estimated advantage from toss decision at venue                            |
| Weather adjustment   | dew/rain/cloud/wind impact                                                 |

## 16. Priority tiers

### MVP cricket app

Build these first:

* Ball-by-ball data.
* Match metadata: venue, format, toss, teams, umpires.
* Playing XI and squad availability.
* Batter stats by phase and bowling type.
* Bowler stats by phase and batter hand.
* Team powerplay/middle/death stats.
* Venue scoring and chasing history.
* Pitch report and weather/dew flags.
* DLS state for interrupted matches.
* Recent form: last 5/10/20 matches.
* Toss decision and innings order.

### Pro version

Add:

* Batter-vs-bowler matchup engine.
* Phase-adjusted player ratings.
* Expected runs and expected wickets.
* Win probability model.
* Catch/drop fielding model.
* Bowling plan optimiser.
* Batting-order optimiser.
* DRS and umpire tendency database.
* Weather-adjusted projections.
* Venue/pitch-adjusted scores.

### Elite version

Add:

* Ball tracking.
* Pitch maps.
* Wagon wheels.
* Field-placement tracking.
* Video tagging.
* Biomechanics.
* Real-time win probability.
* Live DLS modelling.
* Shot-quality model.
* Injury and workload risk model.
* Automated tactical recommendations.

## 17. Best prediction feature groups

For cricket prediction, I’d weight features roughly like this:

| Feature group                            |                                     Importance |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------: |
| Playing XI and role balance              |                                      Very high |
| Format-specific batting/bowling strength |                                      Very high |
| Pitch and venue conditions               |                                      Very high |
| Toss and innings order                   |                                      Very high |
| Weather, rain, dew and DLS risk          |                                           High |
| Batter-vs-bowler matchups                |                                           High |
| Phase performance                        |                                           High |
| Team recent form                         |                                    Medium-high |
| Bowling workload/injury risk             |                                    Medium-high |
| Fielding quality                         |                                         Medium |
| Officials/DRS tendencies                 |                                         Medium |
| Head-to-head                             |                                     Low-medium |
| Public narratives                        | Low unless tied to real selection/fitness news |

## 18. Practical build recommendation

For cricket, structure your app like this:

**Match metadata → ball-by-ball log → player phase profiles → venue/pitch/weather layer → matchup engine → live/projection model → explainable output.**

For your app pages, I’d build:

1. **Match preview page** — XI, pitch, weather, toss, venue history, phase strengths.
2. **Player profile page** — batting/bowling by phase, matchup, conditions, recent form.
3. **Team profile page** — powerplay/middle/death, chasing/defending, pace/spin balance.
4. **Venue page** — average scores, toss trends, chase trends, pitch type, dew/rain patterns.
5. **Live match page** — win probability, projected score, DLS par, pressure index.
6. **Matchup page** — batter-vs-bowler, bowling-type weaknesses, death-over battles.
7. **Model explainability page** — why one side is favoured and which assumptions matter most.

For cricket, the most important rule is: **never analyse a match without separating it by format, phase, toss/innings state, pitch, weather, and role-specific player matchups.**

[4]: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10805135/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "The role of selected pre-match covariates on the outcome of ..."
[5]: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/17479541251319477?utm_source=chatgpt.com "A comprehensive study of weather impact on ODI cricket"
[6]: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.08753?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Fairly Random: The Impact of Winning the Toss on the Probability of Winning"
[7]: https://cricviz.com/winviz/ "WinViz"
[8]: https://www.hawkeyeinnovations.com/data "Hawk-Eye | Data"


For AFL, build the app around **contest + territory + turnover + stoppage + scoring-chain data**. AFL is different from soccer/cricket because possession is messy, the field is huge and variable, player roles are fluid, and a team can dominate the ball but lose because of poor inside-50 quality, conversion, defensive transition, or ground-size mismatch.

The AFL’s own stats glossary defines core metrics such as inside 50s, hit-outs, hit-outs to advantage, groundball gets, hardball gets, score assists, smothers, spoils, tackles and rebound 50s, so those should be treated as first-class data fields, not optional add-ons. ([afl.com.au][1]) Champion Data’s AFL data model is also a strong design reference because its stats are dimensioned by **period, logical zone, physical zone, and whether the stat occurred pre- or post-clearance**. ([AFL Data Platform][2])

## 1. Core AFL app data structure

### A. Match metadata

| Category                | Necessary fields                                                                             |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Competition             | AFL, AFLW, VFL, SANFL, WAFL, local comp, finals, preseason                                   |
| Match                   | match ID, round, date, local start time, timezone, venue, home/away/neutral                  |
| Season context          | ladder position, percentage, finals race, top-four race, spoon/rebuild context               |
| Game type               | home-and-away, elimination final, qualifying final, semi, preliminary, grand final           |
| Rules                   | interchange rules, sub/removal rules, score review/ARC availability, current interpretations |
| Team sheet              | selected 23, emergencies, late outs, substitute/removal status if applicable                 |
| Conditions              | roof open/closed, weather, ground surface, wind, rain, temperature, humidity                 |
| Context                 | travel, short break, six-day/five-day break, interstate trip, derby, milestone game          |
| Market-independent news | injuries, illness, coach comments, training reports, selection hints, tribunal outcomes      |

For 2026 specifically, AFL rule/context data should be versioned by season because the AFL announced new interpretations including faster ruck restarts when a nominated ruck is absent or too far away, and broader 2026 law/interpretation updates. ([afl.com.au][3])

## 2. Ball/event-level data

This should be your central table. AFL analysis becomes much stronger when every stat is linked to **where, when, under what pressure, and what happened next**.

| Field           | Examples                                                             |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| event_id        | unique event                                                         |
| match_id        | fixture ID                                                           |
| quarter         | Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, extra time if applicable                             |
| game_clock      | time in quarter                                                      |
| player_id       | actor                                                                |
| team_id         | actor’s team                                                         |
| opponent_id     | opponent team                                                        |
| event_type      | kick, handball, mark, tackle, spoil, hit-out, clearance, shot        |
| event_subtype   | contested mark, intercept mark, centre clearance, stoppage clearance |
| start_x/start_y | event location                                                       |
| end_x/end_y     | disposal target or ball end location                                 |
| zone            | D50, defensive midfield, centre, attacking midfield, F50             |
| pressure_level  | no pressure, implied, physical, closing, tackle pressure             |
| outcome         | retained, turnover, score, stoppage, out of bounds                   |
| chain_id        | possession chain                                                     |
| source          | clearance, kick-in, intercept, turnover, stoppage, centre bounce     |
| score_chain     | true/false                                                           |
| metres_gained   | disposal/carry metres gained                                         |
| expected_score  | xScore from shot or chain                                            |
| data_confidence | verified/estimated/manual/video-derived                              |

Champion Data’s glossary includes advanced fields such as expected goals from shot location/pressure/sidedness, disposal turnovers, inside-50 entry returns, metres gained by disposal/kick/handball, points above expected, contested/uncontested possession percentage, and pressure acts that force turnovers and generate scores. ([AFL Data Platform][2])

## 3. Player-level stats

### A. Player identity and role

| Area                 | Necessary fields                                                        |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Identity             | player ID, age, height, weight, club, jumper number                     |
| Role                 | key defender, intercept defender, small defender, rebounding half-back  |
| Midfield role        | inside mid, outside mid, wing, tagger, high half-forward, utility       |
| Forward role         | key forward, second tall, small forward, pressure forward, resting ruck |
| Ruck role            | primary ruck, second ruck, ruck-forward, ruck-defender                  |
| Footedness           | left/right/preferred side, opposite-foot usage                          |
| Selection status     | locked best 22/23, fringe, debutant, returning player, managed          |
| Contract/list status | senior list, rookie, mid-season draftee, trade recruit                  |
| Matchup type         | lockdown role, attacking role, loose behind ball, tag target            |

### B. Availability, health and workload

| Area            | Stats/fields                                                            |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Injury status   | injured body part, severity, date injured, expected return              |
| Fitness         | full training, modified training, test, managed, rested                 |
| Concussion      | HIA/removal, concussion protocol, return-to-play timeline               |
| Match load      | minutes played, time on ground %, rotations, bench time                 |
| Recent workload | last 3/5/10 games, minutes, travel, short breaks                        |
| Position load   | midfield CBAs, ruck contests, defensive one-on-ones, sprint volume      |
| Medical flags   | hamstring, calf, ankle, knee, shoulder, concussion history              |
| Selection risk  | late out risk, managed veteran, young player workload, travel emergency |

The AFL states that elite AFL/AFLW players who suffer concussion are under a mandatory minimum 12-day return-to-play protocol and will miss at least one match under standard fixturing. ([afl.com.au][4]) For 2026, the AFL also introduced an ARC Mandatory Permanent Removal Process, where an independent ARC doctor can mandate permanent removal if concussion signs are evident. ([afl.com.au][5])

### C. Possession and ball-winning

| Category         | Stats                                                                           |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Basic possession | disposals, kicks, handballs, marks                                              |
| Contested work   | contested possessions, groundball gets, hardball gets, looseball gets           |
| Outside work     | uncontested possessions, receives, marks on lead, uncontested marks             |
| Clearance work   | centre clearances, stoppage clearances, total clearances                        |
| First possession | first possession from stoppage, sharked hit-outs                                |
| Ball security    | clangers, turnovers, disposal turnovers, fumbles                                |
| Role-adjusted    | possessions by zone, possessions under pressure, possessions pre/post-clearance |

### D. Disposal and ball use

| Category         | Stats                                                                 |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Disposal quality | disposal efficiency, kick efficiency, handball efficiency             |
| Kicking profile  | short kicks, long kicks, kicks inside 50, kicks backwards             |
| Territory        | metres gained, metres gained per disposal, assisted metres gained     |
| Ball retention   | retained kicks, retained handballs, turnovers by zone                 |
| Risk profile     | corridor kicks, switch kicks, boundary-line kicks, aggressive kicks   |
| Under pressure   | disposal efficiency under pressure, turnover under pressure           |
| Damage           | score involvements, score assists, goal assists, expected score added |

### E. Scoring and forward craft

| Category            | Stats                                                          |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Scoring             | goals, behinds, score involvements, score assists              |
| Shot profile        | shots, set shots, snaps, running shots, ground shots           |
| Accuracy            | goal accuracy, expected score, points above expected           |
| Forward entries     | inside-50 targets, marks inside 50, contests inside 50         |
| Ground-level threat | forward-half groundballs, crumbs, front-and-centre possessions |
| Pressure            | forward-half tackles, pressure acts, forced turnovers          |
| Matchup             | vs tall defender, vs small defender, vs intercept defender     |
| Clutch              | last-quarter goals, close-game shots, set shots after siren    |

Expected score/xScore matters because pure goal accuracy can be noisy; Champion Data’s expected-goal metric uses shot location, pressure and sidedness, and points above expected compares actual scoring to expected scoring. ([AFL Data Platform][2])

### F. Defensive stats

| Category      | Stats                                                                    |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Tackling      | tackles, tackles inside 50, missed tackles, tackle efficiency            |
| Pressure      | pressure acts, implied pressure, closing pressure, forced turnovers      |
| Spoiling      | spoils, effective spoils, one-percenters                                 |
| Intercepting  | intercept possessions, intercept marks, intercept scores launched        |
| One-on-ones   | defensive one-on-one contests, loss %, neutralised contests              |
| Rebounding    | rebound 50s, kick-ins, D50 exits, retained exits                         |
| Shutdown role | opponent disposals, opponent goals, opponent score involvements          |
| Team defence  | defensive transition, goals conceded from turnover, D50 stoppage defence |

### G. Ruck stats

| Category         | Stats                                                       |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ruck contests    | ruck contests attended, ruck contest win %                  |
| Hit-outs         | hit-outs, hit-outs to advantage, hit-outs sharked           |
| Clearance link   | clearance rate from own hit-outs, CBA-to-clearance rate     |
| Around-ground    | marks, contested marks, intercept marks, score involvements |
| Forward impact   | goals, marks inside 50, ruck-forward contests               |
| Defensive impact | behind-the-ball marking, D50 contests                       |
| Workload         | ruck minutes, time on ground, second-ruck support           |

The AFL glossary defines a hit-out as a controlled knock from a ruck contest, a hit-out to advantage as one reaching an intended teammate, and a hit-out shark as clear possession won from the opposition ruck’s hit-out. ([afl.com.au][1])

### H. Physical/GPS tracking

| Category       | Stats                                                         |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Running        | total distance, high-speed distance, sprint distance          |
| Intensity      | max speed, accelerations, decelerations                       |
| Repeat efforts | repeat sprints, repeat contests, pressure chains              |
| Fatigue        | quarter-by-quarter running drop-off, late-game sprint decline |
| Positioning    | heat map, average position, wing width, defensive depth       |
| Rotation       | bench rotations, time on ground %, stint length               |
| Role load      | midfield load, ruck load, key-position contest load           |

## 4. Team-level stats

### A. Scoring and attacking profile

| Category          | Stats                                                               |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Score             | points for, goals, behinds, scoring shots                           |
| Expected score    | xScore for, points above expected                                   |
| Scoring sources   | from turnover, from stoppage, from centre bounce, from kick-in      |
| Inside 50         | inside 50s, inside-50 efficiency, marks inside 50                   |
| Forward-half game | time in forward half, forward-half intercepts, forward-half tackles |
| Shot quality      | shots from dangerous zones, set-shot quality, snap-shot quality     |
| Conversion        | goals per inside 50, scores per inside 50, goal accuracy            |
| Forward method    | long to contest, lead-up, corridor entries, repeat entries          |

### B. Defensive profile

| Category          | Stats                                                             |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Score conceded    | points against, goals against, scoring shots conceded             |
| xScore against    | expected score conceded, points saved/conceded above expected     |
| Inside 50 defence | inside 50s conceded, marks inside 50 conceded                     |
| Turnover defence  | scores conceded from turnover                                     |
| Stoppage defence  | scores conceded from stoppage, centre-bounce scores conceded      |
| Intercepting      | intercept possessions, intercept marks, intercept scores launched |
| D50 exits         | rebound 50s, retained exits, D50 turnover rate                    |
| Pressure          | pressure rating, tackles, forced turnovers, forward-half pressure |

### C. Contest and stoppage

| Category          | Stats                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Contest           | contested possession differential, groundball differential                                   |
| Clearances        | total clearance differential, centre clearance differential, stoppage clearance differential |
| Ruck              | hit-outs, hit-outs to advantage, ruck contest win %                                          |
| Clearance quality | scores from clearance, inside 50s from clearance                                             |
| Post-clearance    | post-clearance contested ball, post-clearance possession retention                           |
| Spread            | uncontested possession differential, mark differential                                       |
| Territory         | inside-50 differential, metres gained differential                                           |

### D. Ball movement and transition

| Category           | Stats                                                   |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Speed              | ball movement speed, chain duration, metres per chain   |
| Direction          | corridor usage, boundary usage, switch usage            |
| Retention          | disposal efficiency, kick retention, handball retention |
| Risk               | turnover rate, clangers, aggressive kick turnover rate  |
| Transition attack  | scores from defensive half, coast-to-coast chains       |
| Transition defence | scores conceded from defensive-half turnovers           |
| Kick-ins           | play-on %, long/short kick-ins, retained kick-in chains |
| Rebound            | rebound 50 conversion to inside 50, D50-to-score rate   |

### E. Pressure and turnover game

| Category             | Stats                                                   |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pressure acts        | total pressure acts, pressure by zone                   |
| Forced turnovers     | turnovers forced, forced turnovers in forward half      |
| Scores from pressure | points from pressure acts, goals from forced turnovers  |
| Tackling             | tackles, tackles inside 50, missed tackles              |
| Smothers/spoils      | one-percenters, smothers, spoils                        |
| Defensive intensity  | pressure rating by quarter, late-game pressure drop-off |

## 5. Match officials and umpiring

AFL umpiring is important because free kicks, 50m penalties, holding-the-ball interpretations, high contact and dangerous-tackle interpretations can shift territory and scoring chances.

| Official area          | Stats to capture                                                        |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Field umpires          | names, experience, home-state context, recent games                     |
| Boundary umpires       | boundary throw-in style, out-of-bounds consistency                      |
| Goal umpires           | score review involvement, close-call history                            |
| ARC/score review       | reviews, overturns, score-review duration                               |
| Free-kick profile      | free kicks per match, free-kick differential, team-specific history     |
| Interpretation profile | holding the ball, high contact, insufficient intent, ruck infringements |
| 50m penalties          | 50m penalties per match, dissent/stand/encroachment calls               |
| Advantage              | advantage paid, advantage called back                                   |
| Dangerous tackles      | dangerous-tackle reports, high-contact reports                          |
| Reportable offences    | match review/tribunal referrals                                         |
| Game flow              | stoppage frequency, ball-up speed, time-on tendency                     |

The AFL Laws page says the laws are designed to ensure fair play, reduce injury risk where reasonably achievable in a body-contact sport, protect the player making the ball their primary objective, and encourage continuous, free-flowing football. ([afl.com.au][6]) For app design, that means rule interpretations should be stored as season-specific context rather than treated as static.

## 6. Venue and ground data

AFL ground dimensions matter a lot because unlike many sports, grounds are not all identical. The WA Government’s sports-dimensions guide gives open-age Australian rules playing-surface guidance of **135m–185m long and 110m–155m wide**, with 165m x 135m described as a preferred senior oval size. ([Creative Industries, Tourism and Sport][7])

| Venue category   | Necessary fields                                                      |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Venue ID         | ground name, city, state, timezone                                    |
| Dimensions       | length, width, total area, wing width, pocket depth                   |
| Shape            | wide oval, narrow oval, long ground, compact ground                   |
| Surface          | grass type, hardness, drainage, wear, recent resurfacing              |
| Roof             | open, closed, retractable, indoor-like conditions                     |
| Wind             | exposed/open, swirling, protected, end-to-end wind                    |
| Crowd            | capacity, expected attendance, hostile/home crowd                     |
| Travel           | interstate travel, time-zone travel, flight distance                  |
| Home advantage   | home win %, venue familiarity, tenant/non-tenant split                |
| Scoring profile  | average total points, goal accuracy, behind rate                      |
| Tactical profile | suits corridor teams, wide-switch teams, contested teams, speed teams |

Examples: AFL venue data lists the MCG at **160m x 141m** with capacity 100,024, Marvel Stadium at **159.5m x 128.8m** with a retractable roof, and Optus Stadium at **165m x 130m**. ([afl.com.au][8])

## 7. Time of day, weather and conditions

| Condition   | Stats/fields                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Time slot   | afternoon, twilight, night, short turnaround slot       |
| Temperature | kickoff temp, quarter-by-quarter temp, feels-like temp  |
| Rain        | pre-game rain, live rain, heavy showers, slippery ball  |
| Wind        | speed, gusts, direction, end-to-end wind, crosswind     |
| Humidity    | humidity, dew point, ball slipperiness                  |
| Surface     | dry, greasy, soft, heavy, chopped up, fast deck         |
| Roof        | Marvel roof open/closed, roof shadow, indoor conditions |
| Sun/glare   | low sun, one-end glare, marking visibility              |
| Heat        | heat stress, bench rotations, fatigue risk              |
| Cold        | handball/kicking skill impact, muscle injury risk       |
| Ground wear | previous matches, centre-square wear, goal-square wear  |

In AFL prediction, weather should not just be a “rain yes/no” field. It should feed into expected total points, disposal efficiency, contested-ball weighting, marking quality, groundball volume, and goalkicking accuracy.

## 8. Match context

| Context                      | Why it matters                                                                  |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rest days                    | short breaks reduce running/pressure repeatability                              |
| Travel                       | WA/QLD/SA/VIC travel changes preparation                                        |
| Consecutive interstate games | fatigue and routine disruption                                                  |
| Ladder stakes                | finals/top-four/relegation-style pressure via draft position narratives         |
| Rivalry                      | Showdown, Derby, Anzac Day, King’s Birthday, Dreamtime                          |
| Finals                       | pressure, selection risk, tactical conservatism                                 |
| Milestones                   | player 100/200/300, coach milestone, tribute game                               |
| Selection stability          | unchanged team vs mass changes                                                  |
| Coaching pressure            | coach under scrutiny, caretaker coach, new coach bounce                         |
| Injury cluster               | missing tall defenders, missing ruck, thin midfield, no small forwards          |
| Tribunal                     | suspended key player, appeal pending                                            |
| Form type                    | wins/losses, but also xScore, inside 50s, contested ball, turnover differential |

## 9. Advanced AFL metrics to calculate

| Metric type          | Examples                                                             |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Expected score       | xScore for/against, points above expected                            |
| Shot quality         | expected score per shot, set-shot quality, general-play shot quality |
| Chain value          | expected score added per chain, scoring chain value                  |
| Territory            | inside-50 differential, time in forward half, field position         |
| Contest              | contested possession differential, groundball differential           |
| Clearance value      | scores from centre clearance, scores from stoppage clearance         |
| Turnover value       | scores from turnover, turnovers leading to shots                     |
| Pressure value       | points generated from pressure acts, forced-turnover score %         |
| Ball movement        | metres gained retained, corridor-chain success, switch-chain success |
| Defensive transition | opponent score rate after your turnover                              |
| Inside-50 quality    | score per inside 50, mark per inside 50, groundball win after entry  |
| Ruck value           | hit-out-to-advantage to clearance to score chain                     |
| Player impact        | role-adjusted rating, scoreboard impact, expected score involvement  |
| Fatigue index        | short break + travel + time on ground + high-speed load              |
| Weather adjustment   | rain/wind/roof impact on scoring and disposal quality                |
| Venue fit            | ground-size/style fit by team and player role                        |

## 11. MVP AFL app stats

Build these first:

* Team sheet, late outs, injuries, concussion/HIA status.
* Venue dimensions, roof status, weather and surface condition.
* Scores, scoring shots, goal accuracy.
* Expected score for/against.
* Inside 50s and inside-50 efficiency.
* Contested possessions, groundball gets, clearances.
* Centre clearances vs stoppage clearances.
* Turnovers and scores from turnovers.
* Intercepts and scores launched from intercepts.
* Pressure acts, tackles and tackles inside 50.
* Marks inside 50 and intercept marks.
* Rebound 50s and D50 exits.
* Ruck contests, hit-outs and hit-outs to advantage.
* Rest days, travel, ladder context and recent form.

## 12. Pro version

Add:

* Full possession-chain model.
* Score-chain source model: turnover, stoppage, kick-in, intercept.
* Player role-adjusted ratings.
* Forward-entry quality model.
* Defensive one-on-one matchup model.
* Pressure-to-score model.
* Venue-style suitability model.
* Weather-adjusted scoring projection.
* Umpire/free-kick profile model.
* Quarter-by-quarter fatigue and momentum model.
* Interchange/rotation efficiency model.

## 13. Elite version

Add:

* GPS/tracking data.
* Player spacing and team shape.
* Defensive-zone structure.
* Off-ball running lanes.
* Real-time win probability.
* Live xScore and chain value.
* Kick target probability.
* Marking contest probability.
* Injury/fatigue risk model.
* Automated video tagging.
* Recruitment/list-management projection layer.

## 14. Prediction feature weighting

For AFL match prediction, I’d weight features roughly like this:

| Feature group                          |  Importance |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------: |
| Team selection and availability        |   Very high |
| Expected score for/against             |   Very high |
| Contest and clearance profile          |   Very high |
| Turnover game                          |   Very high |
| Inside-50 quality                      |   Very high |
| Venue and ground-size fit              |        High |
| Weather and roof conditions            |        High |
| Defensive transition                   |        High |
| Ruck/midfield matchup                  |        High |
| Forward-line vs defensive-line matchup |        High |
| Rest, travel and fatigue               | Medium-high |
| Goalkicking accuracy trend             |      Medium |
| Umpire/free-kick profile               |      Medium |
| Recent win-loss form                   |      Medium |
| Head-to-head                           |  Low-medium |

The biggest modelling mistake in AFL would be relying only on **disposals, wins/losses and ladder position**. A strong AFL app should care much more about **where the ball is won, how it enters forward 50, whether the team scores from turnover or stoppage, how well it defends transition, and whether the venue/weather suits the team’s style**.

## 15. Practical AFL app pages

For the first AFL version, I’d build these dashboards:

1. **Match preview page** — team sheets, injuries, venue, weather, rest, travel, xScore, contest, turnover and inside-50 profile.
2. **Team profile page** — attack, defence, contest, stoppage, turnover, pressure, venue splits.
3. **Player profile page** — role, form, availability, scoring impact, pressure, disposal quality, matchups.
4. **Venue page** — ground dimensions, scoring history, weather/roof profile, home advantage.
5. **Matchup page** — ruck/midfield, tall forwards vs tall defenders, small forwards vs small defenders, intercept game.
6. **Live match page** — momentum, xScore, territory, pressure, clearance value, win probability.
7. **Model explainability page** — why the model rates one team or total higher, and which assumptions matter most.

For AFL, the core principle is: **analyse the game as territory plus contest plus scoring-chain quality, not just possession volume.**
