## 9. Pre-game feature confidence scoring

Use this type of confidence system:

| Confidence | Example                                               |
| ---------: | ----------------------------------------------------- |
|       1.00 | official final team sheet / confirmed starting lineup |
|       0.95 | official injury report                                |
|       0.90 | official league/team source                           |
|       0.80 | reliable beat reporter                                |
|       0.70 | consistent multiple reputable reports                 |
|       0.55 | projected lineup from model/site                      |
|       0.35 | rumour/social media only                              |

A player should never be simply “in” or “out” unless confirmed. Use:

* confirmed in;
* confirmed out;
* doubtful;
* questionable/test;
* probable;
* projected starter;
* projected bench;
* unknown.

## 10. Pre-game-only master checklist

This is the checklist I’d use before every prediction:

| Step | Question                                                                  |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | What is the exact match, venue, date and competition?                     |
| 2    | What is the prediction cutoff time?                                       |
| 3    | Are lineups/team sheets confirmed or projected?                           |
| 4    | Who is missing, limited, suspended, rested or returning?                  |
| 5    | What is each team’s last 5/10/15/20 form, adjusted for opponent strength? |
| 6    | What is each team’s season baseline?                                      |
| 7    | What are the home/away or venue splits?                                   |
| 8    | Does the venue/pitch/ground/park suit one side?                           |
| 9    | What is the forecast weather at match time?                               |
| 10   | Who are the officials, and do they affect scoring/discipline?             |
| 11   | Is there a rest/travel/fatigue edge?                                      |
| 12   | What are the key tactical or role matchups?                               |
| 13   | Is the match context normal or unusual?                                   |
| 14   | Which data is confirmed vs projected?                                     |
| 15   | What would change the prediction before start time?                       |

## 12. Model output should include uncertainty

Your app should not just say “Team A wins.” It should output:

| Output          | Example                                  |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| prediction      | Team A slight edge                       |
| probability     | 58%                                      |
| confidence      | medium                                   |
| key reasons     | lineup, venue, recent xG/xScore, matchup |
| risks           | weather, late out, uncertain lineup      |
| data quality    | confirmed lineups / projected lineups    |
| cutoff          | T-1 hour                                 |
| what changes it | player X out, toss lost, rain worsens    |

Probability calibration matters because a model’s predicted probabilities are not automatically reliable; scikit-learn’s calibration documentation notes that classifiers can produce poor probability estimates and may need calibration. ([Scikit-learn][8])

## 13. Final pre-game principle

Build the app around this:

**Pre-game snapshot → confirmed/projected status → source confidence → sport-specific matchup features → probability → confidence → post-game review.**

For your use case, every prediction should clearly say:

**“This is based only on information available before the game at [cutoff time].”**

[1]: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11267?utm_source=chatgpt.com "A prior-free blind detection of information leakage from model predictions"
[2]: https://open-meteo.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Open-Meteo.com: 🌤️ Free Open-Source Weather API"
[3]: https://github.com/statsbomb/open-data?utm_source=chatgpt.com "statsbomb/open-data: Free football data from StatsBomb"
[4]: https://cricsheet.org/format/csv_ashwin/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Introduction to the \"Ashwin\" CSV format"
[5]: https://docs.api.afl.championdata.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "AFL Data Platform: Documentation Hub - Champion Data"
[6]: https://www.afl.com.au/venues/65?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Optus Stadium - AFL.com.au"
[7]: https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/leaderboard/statcast-park-factors?batSide=&condition=All&parks=mlb&rolling=2&stat=index_wOBA&type=year&year=2026&utm_source=chatgpt.com "Statcast Park Factors | baseballsavant.com - MLB.com"
[8]: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com "1.16. Probability calibration"


Yes — there are **obscure but very useful pre-game factors** you should include. These will make your sports research app much stronger than a basic “last 5 form + injuries + venue” app.

The key idea is: **don’t just compare teams by form. Compare them by how similar the upcoming game is to the conditions that produced that form.**

## 1. Data timing and leakage flags

This is the most important “hidden” feature. Every stat should have a timestamp saying when it was knowable.

| Field               | Example                                           |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `known_at_time`     | 13 June 2026, 6:30pm AEST                         |
| `prediction_cutoff` | T-24h, T-3h, T-1h, post-lineup                    |
| `feature_status`    | confirmed, projected, rumour, unavailable         |
| `leakage_risk`      | low, medium, high                                 |
| `source_tier`       | official, data provider, journalist, social media |

This matters because a pre-game model must not accidentally use information that only became available during or after the match. IBM describes data leakage as using information during training that would not be available at prediction time, which can make models look strong in testing but fail in real use. ([dotData][1])

## 2. “Similar conditions” form

Instead of only:

```text
Team last 5
Team last 10
Team last 15
Team last 20
```

also calculate:

```text
Team last 5 under similar conditions
Team last 10 under similar venue type
Team last 10 against similar opponent style
Team last 10 with similar rest/travel
Team last 10 with similar lineup strength
Team last 10 in similar weather
```

This is one of the best hidden edges.

| Sport    | Similar-condition split examples                                                     |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Soccer   | vs low block, high press, strong set-piece teams, artificial turf, away after travel |
| Cricket  | vs spin-heavy attacks, on slow pitches, under dew, batting first, chasing            |
| AFL      | wide ground, narrow ground, roof closed, wet weather, short break, interstate        |
| Baseball | vs lefty starters, high-velo pitchers, bullpen games, hitter parks, wind blowing out |

## 3. Rest-time mismatch

Don’t just record rest days. Record **rest differential**.

| Feature                      | Example                              |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| team rest days               | 6                                    |
| opponent rest days           | 8                                    |
| rest differential            | -2                                   |
| travel + rest combo          | away team, 5-day break, interstate   |
| short-break history          | performance on 5-day/6-day breaks    |
| opponent short-break history | how opponent performs with same rest |

Travel and jet lag should be tracked properly because athlete travel fatigue and jet lag can increase subjective burden and may influence performance, illness and injury risk. ([PMC][2])

## 4. Sleep and circadian rhythm proxies

You probably won’t have actual sleep data, but you can build proxies.

| Pre-game proxy            | Why it matters                     |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| time-zone change          | body clock disruption              |
| eastward/westward travel  | direction of travel can matter     |
| local kickoff time        | morning, afternoon, night          |
| body-clock kickoff time   | game time in team’s usual timezone |
| day game after night game | baseball especially                |
| late flight / early start | likely recovery issue              |
| consecutive travel games  | fatigue accumulation               |

Sleep is not a soft factor. Reviews show sleep disruption can negatively affect athletic performance, recovery and injury risk. ([PMC][3]) Time of day also matters: a 2025 review found neuromuscular performance in team-sport athletes is generally higher in the late afternoon or early evening than in the morning. ([PMC][4])

## 5. Crowd and home-ground intensity

Home advantage is not just “home = yes/no”.

| Field               | Better version                    |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| home/away           | home, away, neutral, semi-neutral |
| expected crowd      | attendance estimate               |
| crowd density       | attendance ÷ capacity             |
| rivalry intensity   | derby, final, grudge match        |
| travel support      | away crowd strength               |
| no/low crowd        | crowd-reduced home advantage      |
| hostile environment | subjective but useful if sourced  |

A systematic review on football found that absence of crowds tended to reduce home advantage, although the effect varied by country, and crowd absence may also influence referee behaviour. ([PMC][5])

## 6. Official/referee/umpire pressure profile

You already had officials, but go deeper.

| Obscure official feature                | Sports                |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| home-team call tendency                 | soccer, AFL, baseball |
| high-pressure decision tendency         | all                   |
| late-game strictness                    | AFL, soccer, baseball |
| penalty/free-kick/strike-zone inflation | soccer, AFL, baseball |
| review overturn frequency               | VAR, DRS, ARC, replay |
| pace/stoppage control                   | cricket, AFL, soccer  |
| card/free-kick/strike-zone volatility   | soccer, AFL, baseball |
| official familiarity with teams         | all                   |

Home advantage research repeatedly links crowd, officiating and home performance. A 2022 systematic review on football home advantage found spectator absence was often connected with changes in referee influence and team performance. ([PMC][6])

## 7. Weather interaction stats

Don’t just store weather. Store how each team/player performs **in that weather type**.

| Weather factor | Hidden stat                                      |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| wind           | team scoring/accuracy in strong wind             |
| rain           | handling errors, turnovers, low scoring          |
| humidity/dew   | cricket grip, baseball carry, fatigue            |
| heat           | late-game fade, rotations, pace drop             |
| cold           | skill error rate, injury risk                    |
| altitude       | endurance and ball-flight effects                |
| roof           | indoor/outdoor split                             |
| cloud cover    | cricket swing, baseball visibility, soccer tempo |

Weather and altitude have measurable effects on physical and technical performance in professional team sports, so your app should treat them as performance modifiers rather than just background notes. ([PMC][7]) Heat can reduce high-intensity activity in football contexts, and that logic is relevant to running-heavy sports such as soccer and AFL. ([Gatorade Sports Science Institute][8])

## 8. Venue familiarity index

This is different from home advantage.

| Field                      | Example                             |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| player games at venue      | 12                                  |
| team games at venue        | 30                                  |
| coach record at venue      | 8–4                                 |
| recent venue exposure      | played there in last 30 days        |
| surface familiarity        | turf, grass, hard deck, slow pitch  |
| dimensions fit             | wide/narrow/long/small ground       |
| sightline familiarity      | cricket/baseball batting visibility |
| travel-to-venue complexity | direct flight vs long transfer      |

This matters especially for AFL, cricket and baseball because grounds/pitches/parks are not standardised in the same way.

## 9. Lineup continuity and chemistry

A team can be “full strength” but still unstable.

| Feature                          | Meaning                     |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| same starting group last game    | continuity                  |
| same starting group last 3 games | stability                   |
| same defensive unit              | soccer/AFL/baseball defence |
| same midfield group              | soccer/AFL                  |
| same batting order               | cricket/baseball            |
| same catcher-pitcher pair        | baseball                    |
| same bowler-keeper pair          | cricket                     |
| same ruck-midfield group         | AFL                         |
| new signing/debutant count       | chemistry risk              |
| role change count                | tactical instability        |

Suggested metric:

```text
Lineup Continuity Score =
% of current starters who started last match
+ % who started 3 of last 5
+ % playing same role/position
```

## 10. Role-change index

This is very important and often missed.

| Sport    | Examples                                                                              |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Soccer   | winger used as wing-back, midfielder at centre-back, striker returning from wide role |
| Cricket  | opener moved to No. 4, finisher promoted, bowler moved from middle overs to death     |
| AFL      | defender moved forward, mid moved to half-forward, ruck sharing changed               |
| Baseball | leadoff hitter moved down, closer unavailable, starter used as opener/bulk arm        |

Create:

```text
Role Stability Score
Position Change Flag
Usage Change Flag
Role Difficulty Change
```

A player’s recent form is much less useful if their role has changed.

## 11. Replacement quality, not just absence

Injuries matter, but the real question is: **who replaces them?**

| Field                     | Example                 |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| missing player value      | +2.1 rating             |
| replacement player value  | -0.4 rating             |
| net replacement drop-off  | -2.5                    |
| role coverage             | strong/weak             |
| position scarcity         | high/medium/low         |
| replacement match fitness | full/limited            |
| replacement role fit      | natural/out of position |

Example:

```text
Absence Impact = Missing Player Role Value - Replacement Role Value
```

This is much better than a simple “Player X out” flag.

## 12. Matchup-specific weak points

Your app should identify not just “Team A is better”, but **where**.

| Sport    | Hidden matchup examples                                                       |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Soccer   | weak left-back vs elite right winger, poor set-piece defence vs tall opponent |
| Cricket  | batter weak vs left-arm orthodox, team poor against wrist spin                |
| AFL      | weak key defender vs tall forward, poor groundball team vs pressure side      |
| Baseball | lineup poor vs sliders/sweepers, starter weak third time through order        |

Output:

```text
Primary mismatch
Secondary mismatch
Mismatch confidence
Mismatch affected players
```

## 13. Tactical surprise probability

Before a game, estimate how likely a team is to do something different.

| Feature                 | Example                            |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| new coach               | high tactical uncertainty          |
| recent losing streak    | higher chance of change            |
| opponent-specific setup | likely defensive adjustment        |
| finals/knockout         | conservative or surprise selection |
| returning star          | structure change                   |
| coach comments          | hinted role/formation change       |
| training reports        | new combination trialled           |

This prevents your app from assuming the last 5 games will repeat exactly.

## 14. Training availability and session participation

This is not always public, but when available, it is valuable.

| Training info             | Meaning             |
| ------------------------- | ------------------- |
| full training             | likely fit          |
| modified training         | possible limitation |
| no contact                | injury concern      |
| left session early        | high concern        |
| trained with reserves     | selection risk      |
| trained in different role | tactical clue       |
| absent from captain’s run | possible late out   |

This should be stored as **news-derived structured data**, not just a note.

## 15. Soft-tissue recurrence risk

Don’t just record injury status. Record injury type.

| Injury type      | Risk meaning                         |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| hamstring        | recurrence/minutes risk              |
| calf             | older-player recurrence risk         |
| groin/adductor   | movement and kicking risk            |
| ankle            | agility/cutting risk                 |
| shoulder         | contact/throwing/tackling risk       |
| back/side strain | cricket/baseball bowling risk        |
| concussion       | protocol and performance uncertainty |

Use:

```text
Return From Injury Flag
Days Since Return
Games Since Return
Minutes/Overs/Pitches Since Return
Reinjury Risk Category
```

## 16. “Played injured” or “limited output” flag

A player can be selected but not fully effective.

| Field                             | Example            |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| carrying injury                   | yes/no             |
| minutes cap                       | likely/possible    |
| managed role                      | yes/no             |
| reduced training load             | yes/no             |
| recent early substitution/removal | yes/no             |
| output drop since injury          | percentage decline |

This is huge in pre-game analysis because public team sheets often say “available”, but performance may still be reduced.

## 17. Motivation and incentive precision

Don’t just say “must win”. Make it structured.

| Incentive                              | Examples                         |
| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| must win to qualify                    | high                             |
| draw is enough                         | lower risk-taking                |
| dead rubber                            | rotation risk                    |
| percentage/goal difference/NRR matters | scoring margin incentive         |
| rivalry/milestone                      | intensity lift                   |
| finals next week                       | resting risk                     |
| relegation/survival/title pressure     | tactical conservatism or urgency |

For cricket, NRR pressure can change batting tempo. For AFL, percentage can influence late-game aggression. For soccer, aggregate/goal-difference context can change risk-taking.

## 18. Market movement as an information signal

Even if you ignore odds for decision-making, line movement can reveal information.

| Field                   | Use                             |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| opening line            | early consensus                 |
| current line            | updated consensus               |
| movement direction      | injury/weather/team-news signal |
| movement timing         | when information hit market     |
| disagreement with model | possible edge or missing factor |
| market volatility       | uncertainty signal              |

Use this carefully. It should be a **benchmark and information-detection tool**, not your only model input. Calibration matters more than raw accuracy in probabilistic sports decisions; one sports-betting model-selection paper found calibration-based model selection outperformed accuracy-based selection in its NBA experiments. ([arXiv][9])

## 19. Public overreaction index

Useful if your app will compare model probabilities with public narratives.

| Overreaction trigger    | Example              |
| ----------------------- | -------------------- |
| huge last-game win      | public overrating    |
| ugly last-game loss     | public underrating   |
| star player media hype  | over-adjustment risk |
| rivalry narrative       | emotional market     |
| coach under pressure    | noise vs signal      |
| viral clip/injury scare | sentiment spike      |

Store:

```text
Narrative Strength
Confirmed Evidence
Likely Overreaction
```

## 20. Stability of the stat itself

Some stats are stable quickly; others are noisy.

| More stable sooner     | Noisier                    |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------- |
| strikeout rate         | batting average            |
| xG/xScore trend        | goals/accuracy             |
| inside-50 differential | goalkicking conversion     |
| dot-ball %             | wickets                    |
| pressure rate          | goals from limited chances |
| pitch velocity         | ERA                        |

Baseball is a good example: FanGraphs’ sample-size guide shows that baseball stats stabilise at different rates, so your app should not trust all last-5 or last-10 trends equally. ([dotData][1])

## 21. Volatility and ceiling/floor

Average form is not enough.

| Metric                   | Meaning                           |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| median output            | typical performance               |
| standard deviation       | volatility                        |
| coefficient of variation | volatility relative to average    |
| floor                    | likely bad-case output            |
| ceiling                  | likely best-case output           |
| blowout-adjusted average | removes junk-time distortion      |
| consistency index        | how repeatable the team/player is |

Example:

```text
Team A average = 90, but range 55–130
Team B average = 90, but range 82–98
```

Same average, completely different prediction profile.

## 22. Garbage-time adjusted form

Pre-game form should discount stats from dead periods.

| Sport    | Garbage-time examples                                  |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Soccer   | late shots while 3-0 down                              |
| Cricket  | impossible chase, dead rubber overs                    |
| AFL      | junk-time goals/disposals in a blowout                 |
| Baseball | position player pitching, low-leverage bullpen innings |

Store:

```text
competitive_minutes_only
high_leverage_only
blowout_adjusted_stat
garbage_time_percentage
```

## 23. Pressure and clutch context

Do not overrate “clutch”, but track pressure situations.

| Sport    | Pressure split                                               |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Soccer   | goals/chances when tied or down one                          |
| Cricket  | death overs, chase under high required rate                  |
| AFL      | fourth quarter, margin under 12 points                       |
| Baseball | high-leverage plate appearances, runners in scoring position |

Important: treat this as descriptive unless the sample is large. Many “clutch” stats are noisy.

## 24. Tactical weather fit

This is a deeper version of weather.

| Team style                | Bad weather effect                |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| soccer possession team    | wet pitch may increase turnovers  |
| soccer crossing team      | wind hurts crossing quality       |
| cricket spin team         | dew reduces grip                  |
| cricket swing attack      | cloud/humidity can help           |
| AFL marking team          | rain hurts aerial control         |
| AFL pressure team         | wet ground may help contest style |
| baseball power team       | wind in suppresses HRs            |
| baseball fly-ball pitcher | wind out increases HR risk        |

Create:

```text
Weather Style Fit Score
```

## 25. Venue-style fit

Same idea, but for ground/park/pitch.

| Sport    | Venue-style fit                           |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Soccer   | small pitch helps compact defensive teams |
| Cricket  | slow pitch helps spin-heavy teams         |
| AFL      | wide ground helps switch/wing teams       |
| Baseball | short porch helps pull-power hitters      |

Create:

```text
Venue Style Fit Score =
team style strength × venue condition suitability
```

## 26. Opponent fatigue exploitation

Sometimes it is not your team’s fatigue — it is whether you can exploit the opponent’s fatigue.

| Example                                      | Why it matters        |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| fast soccer wingers vs tired fullbacks       | late attacking edge   |
| AFL pressure team vs short-break opponent    | turnover edge         |
| cricket death hitters vs tired death bowlers | late innings edge     |
| baseball patient lineup vs tired bullpen     | walk/run scoring edge |

## 27. Bench/substitution impact

Pre-game models often underrate the bench.

| Sport    | Bench impact                                                    |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Soccer   | attacking substitutes, defensive close-out options              |
| Cricket  | impact player/sub rules where applicable, all-rounder balance   |
| AFL      | interchange depth, 23rd player quality, late-game running depth |
| Baseball | bench bats, platoon pinch hitters, bullpen depth                |

Store:

```text
Starting Strength
Bench Strength
Late-Game Strength
Replacement Flexibility
```

## 28. Coach/manager decision profile

Some coaches change the prediction environment.

| Field                     | Examples                      |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| rotation tendency         | rests players often           |
| conservative/aggressive   | protects lead or chases score |
| substitution timing       | early vs late                 |
| tactical flexibility      | formation/role changes        |
| bullpen hook              | baseball                      |
| ruck/midfield mix         | AFL                           |
| batting order flexibility | cricket                       |
| set-piece emphasis        | soccer                        |

A team with a conservative coach might be better for unders/low-scoring outcomes when leading, even if the raw attack is strong.

## 29. Psychological disruption flags

Use carefully, but don’t ignore confirmed disruptions.

| Disruption                | Examples                              |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| coach sacked/resigned     | tactical/emotional change             |
| captain injured/suspended | leadership change                     |
| player contract dispute   | selection/motivation issue            |
| travel chaos              | preparation disruption                |
| illness outbreak          | fitness uncertainty                   |
| public controversy        | mental distraction                    |
| funeral/family emergency  | player availability/emotional context |

Only include these when they come from reliable sources.

## 30. Data-source disagreement

This is obscure but important.

If multiple sources disagree, store that.

| Field             | Example            |
| ----------------- | ------------------ |
| source A lineup   | Player X starting  |
| source B lineup   | Player X bench     |
| conflict level    | high               |
| confidence        | reduced            |
| prediction impact | lineup uncertainty |

This prevents false certainty.

## 31. “What would change the prediction?” field

Every pre-game analysis should include trigger conditions.

Examples:

| Trigger                    | Effect                              |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| star player late out       | downgrade attack/clearance/batting  |
| weather worsens            | lower scoring projection            |
| roof closes                | increase skill/scoring consistency  |
| toss won and bowls first   | cricket model shift                 |
| starting pitcher scratched | baseball model reset                |
| ruck late out              | AFL clearance model reset           |
| referee/umpire changed     | discipline/strike-zone model update |

This makes the app explainable and practical.

## 32. Best obscure-stat master table

Use this as your app’s “deep layer” checklist:

| Layer        | Obscure stat/info                                       |  Importance |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------: |
| Timing       | prediction cutoff, known-at timestamp, leakage risk     |   Very high |
| Similarity   | similar opponent/venue/weather/rest form                |   Very high |
| Availability | replacement quality, not just injury                    |   Very high |
| Role         | role change, role stability, position fit               |   Very high |
| Venue        | venue-style fit, familiarity, dimensions/surface        |        High |
| Weather      | weather-style interaction, not just forecast            |        High |
| Travel       | body-clock kickoff, east/west travel, rest differential |        High |
| Crowd        | crowd density, hostility, rivalry, neutralisation       | Medium-high |
| Officials    | bias/tendency, review behaviour, strictness             | Medium-high |
| Lineup       | continuity, chemistry, projected vs confirmed           | Medium-high |
| Coaching     | tactical surprise, rotation tendency, game-state style  |      Medium |
| Market       | movement timing, overreaction, disagreement             |      Medium |
| Psychology   | disruption flags, leadership absence                    |  Low-medium |
| Data         | source disagreement, confidence score, revision history |   Very high |
| Modelling    | volatility, sample stability, regression-to-mean        |   Very high |

## Final rule

For your app, add this layer above the normal stats:

```text
Normal pre-game stats
+ rolling 5/10/15/20 trends
+ season/year/historical averages
+ opponent adjustment
+ similar-condition form
+ lineup/replacement adjustment
+ venue/weather/style fit
+ rest/travel/body-clock adjustment
+ source confidence
+ leakage protection
= high-quality pre-game prediction feature
```

The strongest obscure feature overall is probably:

**“How has this team/player performed in the last 5/10/20 games under conditions most similar to today’s match?”**

2026-06-21 AFL calibration note from St Kilda 61 vs Western Bulldogs 83:
- The high-total under was the cleanest signal and won comfortably, but the low-spread favourite cover failed. Do not let a better season percentage, recent home win, or defensive average push a favourite cover above an underdog cushion when the opponent has the stronger top-end midfield/clearance group and a recent H2H dominance profile. Low-spread favourite-cover alignment still needs a clear scoring-conversion and midfield-control edge; otherwise keep the underdog cushion near or above the favourite cover and let the total be the anchor.

2026-06-21 cricket live-moisture correction from Bangladesh 7/2 after 1.5 overs vs Australia:
- For T20 powerplay markets, actual just-before-start rain, covers-on timing, and live new-ball movement must outweigh generic "quick drying ground", "good batting pitch later", or "200 par after it dries" comments. If covers were on shortly before toss/start and there is evidence of recent rain, downgrade powerplay overs immediately unless the first over confirms clean carry and confident hitting. A pitch can dry into a good batting surface later while the first 2-4 overs still strongly favour seam/swing, tentative batting, and early wickets. In that state, powerplay under and full-innings under must be lifted above prior-series powerplay trends until live evidence proves the moisture has gone.

2026-06-21 WT20I Sri Lanka batting correction from Sri Lanka 98 all out vs West Indies:
- Do not let "batting-friendly pitch" and dry weather override a fragile top-order/wicket-risk profile at 150+ women's T20 innings lines. If the fielding side chooses to bowl, can open/control with a world-class all-round spinner, has extra spin/seam options, and the batting side depends heavily on one or two top-order players, the powerplay under and full-innings under can both be the cleanest rankings. A 150+ full-innings over needs both a strong powerplay and wickets in hand; early wickets such as 23/4 by 5.5 overs almost always kill the over path even if the surface itself is playable.

2026-06-22 WT20I phase/full split correction from India 158/7 vs South Africa:
- A powerplay over can be right while the full-innings over is wrong. India reached 59 in the first six but only 158/7 after South Africa kept taking wickets through overs 6-15 and prevented a death-overs surge. For 165+ women's T20 innings lines, require both a strong powerplay and a wickets-in-hand/death-hitting path. If the opponent has quality across phases, rank the powerplay over and full-innings under adjacent rather than stacking all overs together.

2026-06-22 MLB roof/lineup correction from Houston 2 vs Cleveland 1:
- Roof-closed, wind-neutral MLB games can stay far below a modest total even when one starter has ugly recent logs. If both starters have a credible six-inning stabilisation path, the favourite's top bats are concentrated rather than lineup-wide, and the underdog lineup has a thin lower third, do not rank the over above the narrow winner/cushion structure solely because of recent starter blowups. Re-check confirmed lineups, roof/weather, and bullpen leverage before making 9+ runs the cleaner path.

2026-06-23 GENERAL RULE UPDATE - STARTER/OPENING-PHASE QUALITY DOES NOT CONTROL THE FULL-GAME TAIL:
- Across sports, do not project a full-game under solely from strong starters or a slow opening-phase expectation. Explicitly test the later-phase failure path: relief units, bench quality, late fouling, overtime/extra innings, fatigue and score-state aggression. The lower the full-game threshold, the more heavily that tail must be weighted.
- When a full-game total is unusually low, write two separate projections before ranking: regulation/standard-duration scoring and the overtime/extra-inning tail. A close-game script may support the under early while increasing the chance that additional periods destroy it.

2026-06-23 BASEBALL / NPB RULE UPDATE - LOW TOTALS, BULLPENS AND EXTRA INNINGS:
- Rakuten's 8-7, 12-inning win over Seibu on June 22 invalidated the Lions ML and Under 5.5 anchors despite Kaima Taira and Takahisa Hayakawa entering with elite run-prevention profiles. The score was already 6-6 through nine, and the 11th/12th innings added three more runs.
- For NPB totals of 5.5 or lower, starter ERA/HQS evidence is necessary but not sufficient. Collect both bullpens' latest workload and leverage availability, then model the tied-after-nine probability under NPB's extra-inning/tie rules. Do not rank the under above a side/cushion unless both the starter phase and late-relief phase support it.
- A dome removes weather variance; it does not remove bullpen, home-run, defensive-error or extra-inning variance.

2026-06-23 BASKETBALL / ISRAEL WINNER LEAGUE PREGAME APPLICATION - GALIL ELYON VS NETANYA:
- In a lower-house season finale, separate motivation from lineup quality. A safe home team and a relegated visitor may play with freedom, but confirmed game-roster omissions still control the scoring ceiling. If a relegated team's leading scorer is absent from the official game roster, downgrade its side and full-game over before applying a generic dead-rubber pace boost.
- Direct matchup scoring remains useful when it is current and lineup-compatible: Galil won the three prior 2025-26 league meetings with totals of 163, 153 and 170. Use those games alongside current L5 phase splits; do not use H2H alone.
- For exact-complement basketball cards, rank the projected number first. Here the pregame projection was roughly 162-165 points and 80-83 first-half points, making Under 173.5 the structural anchor and 1H Under 87.5 a smaller edge. Keep the opposing overs explicitly labelled as forced complements rather than independent positive picks.

2026-06-23 GENERAL RULE UPDATE - DUPLICATED USER OPTIONS:
- If the same market and threshold are listed twice, treat them as one distinct outcome. Do not double-count the evidence, manufacture an unstated complement, or imply that two identical entries have independent probabilities.
- If the user also requires bottom-two slots, the duplicated entries may occupy both displayed bottom slots only when that shared outcome is genuinely the least likely. State explicitly that they are the same pick and that the card contains fewer distinct outcomes than numbered entries.

2026-06-23 BASKETBALL / ACB FINALS GAME 3 APPLICATION - BARCELONA VS VALENCIA:
- For a same-series Game 3, immediate Q1 and halftime evidence outranks season scoring averages when the threshold is phase-specific. Barcelona-Valencia produced 38 and 37 first-quarter points in Finals Games 1-2, and their May 31 Palau meeting produced 42. Three straight direct Q1 results below 43.5 make Q1 Over 43.5 a true fade even though both teams own elite full-game scoring ceilings.
- Do not infer a fast first quarter from a high full-game total. Game 1 reached 202 in regulation and 225 after overtime despite a 38-point Q1; late regulation shot-making and overtime were separate scoring mechanisms.
- Run the repeatability test after a blowout: Valencia's Game 2 102-75 win included 52.4% three-point shooting versus Barcelona's 19.1%, so some shooting regression is likely. However, Valencia's strong opening and Barcelona's slow start repeated across both Finals games and the latest Palau H2H. Regress the shooting percentage without erasing the repeatable early control pattern.
- Player return does not equal normal availability. Josep Puerto's four-minute Game 2 return after nearly six weeks out should be treated as a limited-depth addition, while Xabi Lopez-Arostegui and Nate Reuvers remain confirmed absences.

2026-06-23 GENERAL RULE UPDATE - TIMEZONE VERIFICATION FOR THINLY COVERED EVENTS:
- Never classify a minor or new-competition fixture as live from a local-time conversion alone. Confirm the published UTC kickoff against the official broadcaster/event page. Atletico Grau-Pirata FC was listed at 20:15 UTC, which is 06:15 AEST on June 23; an initial one-hour conversion error would have incorrectly triggered live-score modelling.
- When aggregators disagree, the official scheduled broadcast state controls whether the card is pregame or live. Record both the source time and converted user-zone time.

2026-06-23 BASKETBALL / ACB FINALS SETTLEMENT - BARCELONA 80, VALENCIA 88:
- Immediate same-series Q1 evidence repeated again: the first quarter total was 32 after the prior direct sequence of 38, 37 and 42. Keep direct phase evidence above season scoring averages for Q1 markets until a lineup or tactical change explains why the pattern should break.
- A low total does not require poor overall shooting. Barcelona made 50% from the field, but Valencia's 42-26 rebounding edge, controlled lead and both teams' modest three-point rates kept the game to 168. Model possession control, offensive-rebound ownership and clock state separately from raw field-goal percentage.
- The Valencia winner call was supported by the same matchup mechanisms that drove the under: guard creation led by Jean Montero and a decisive rebounding advantage. Side and under can correlate when the stronger matchup team controls second chances and game state without raising pace.

2026-06-23 SOCCER / PERU COPA DE LA LIGA APPLICATION - ATLETICO GRAU VS PIRATA FC:
- In a new regional cup with thin injury and lineup coverage, cap confidence and use competition-level adjustment explicitly. Pirata's strong Liga 2 scoring form is relevant, but it must be discounted when stepping up against a Liga 1 defence; Grau's poor Liga 1 attack remains relevant even against lower-tier opposition.
- Hot, dry afternoon conditions can suppress sustained pressing and favour a lower total, but temperature forecasts that disagree materially must be logged as a range rather than a precise input. Weather is a modifier, not the anchor.
- When the first-tier favourite has scored one or fewer in most recent matches and the lower-tier opponent arrives in strong form, prefer a narrow winner projection and total under over a confident handicap or blowout script.

2026-06-23 GENERAL RULE CORRECTION - THINLY COVERED CUP TOTALS:
- Atletico Grau 3-2 Pirata FC exposed the danger of using division gap and weather to stack 1H/full unders when lineups are unconfirmed. Grau scored in the 8th and 22nd minutes; Pirata then scored twice after 82 minutes.
- In new or regional cups, widen both tails for rotation, unfamiliar defensive partnerships, uneven motivation and late consolation scoring. If the lower-tier side has scored repeatedly in current form, discount its scoring rate for opponent strength but do not erase it.
- Without confirmed defensive lineups or a competition-specific low-tempo sample, no card should place both 1H Under 0.5 and full Under 2.5 in the top two solely from the favourite's league-season under profile.

2026-06-23 BASEBALL / MLB COORS FIELD APPLICATION - BOSTON AT COLORADO:
- Separate winner probability from run-line cushion probability. A road team can be the likely winner while the home +1.5 remains the safest listed side because Coors inflates comeback and one-run-game paths, especially against a contact-heavy rookie starter.
- At Coors totals of 11.5 or higher, do not make the over automatic from heat and altitude. Write the projected score first and require multiple independent 12+ mechanisms: vulnerable starters, taxed bullpens, full-strength lineups, meaningful wind out and weak defence. A light 3 mph breeze out is a modifier, not a primary over trigger.
- Starter surface stats must be paired with role/recovery context. Ryan Feltner's 5.05 ERA overstates his four-start post-IL improvement, while his recent workload and walks still create risk. Jake Bennett's 4.79 ERA understates Coors volatility because his low strikeout total leaves more balls in play.
- Mandatory defence check application: Boston's .987 fielding/35 errors versus Colorado's .983/47 errors strengthens Boston's winner path and Colorado multi-run-inning risk. Defensive quality should influence side and total independently.

2026-06-23 USER DIRECTIVE - MANDATORY STATMUSE L5/L10/L15/L20 FOR AMERICAN SPORTS:
- Before ranking any American-sports card, StatMuse is a mandatory statistical source for both teams and every decision-relevant player listed as available to play.
- Required windows are last 5, last 10, last 15 and last 20 games. Collect the sport-relevant team and player metrics that drive the proposed markets; do not substitute a season average for a missing rolling window without clearly marking that window MISSING.
- Validate every StatMuse answer by reading the restated query scope and checking that the newest table date matches the latest completed game. Reject outputs that drop the opponent, venue, home/away, phase, regular-season/playoff or season qualifier.
- StatMuse does not control injuries, active status, lineups, starters, game state, weather, venue, officials or final settlement. Those remain controlled by official league/team/game sources.
- If StatMuse is unavailable, stale, unsupported or misparsed, walk the documented fallback chain and print: STATMUSE STATUS, failed query/scope, newest returned date if applicable, and the replacement source used. Confidence must be capped when decision-driving L5 or L10 data remain unavailable.
- Do not claim comprehensive American-sports research unless the StatMuse L5/L10/L15/L20 team-and-available-player gate has been completed or the card explicitly documents why it could not be completed.

2026-06-23 GENERAL RULE APPLICATION - STATMUSE OPPONENT-PHASE MISPARSE:
- A StatMuse query for "opponent first-quarter points" or "opponent first-half points" can silently return the requested team's own scoring. Reject the result whenever the answer sentence repeats the team's own phase average or otherwise fails to name opponent points allowed.
- After rejection, calculate opponent Q1/1H scoring from official or reliable dated gamebooks. Record the newest included game date and keep the valid StatMuse own-team L5/L10/L15/L20 data rather than discarding the entire source.

2026-06-23 USER DIRECTIVE - CROSS-SPORT ROLLING VS BASELINE COMPARISON GATE:
- Extend the L5/L10/L15/L20 requirement to every sport and market where reliable rolling statistics are available. Team-level rolling windows are mandatory wherever a credible source provides them; player-level windows are required for decision-relevant available players when reliable participation-adjusted data exists.
- 2026-06-27 USER DIRECTIVE - EVERY-SPORT ROLLING-STATS ENFORCEMENT: for every serious card in every sport, when reliable stats are available, run and document L5/L10/L15/L20 comparisons for both teams and all available players who can materially affect the listed markets, not only the players named in the final picks. Compare each window with season average and historical/career or multi-season baseline where available. This is a required pre-ranking gate, not an optional enhancement. If all-player rolling windows are too large, blocked, stale, unsupported, or unavailable before the event cutoff, write the coverage status explicitly as COMPLETE / PARTIAL / MISSING, list the missing source or player group, cap confidence, and do not claim comprehensive player-level research. For market rankings, team-level windows plus the decision-relevant player/unit windows must be re-checked after adding this gate; if the ranking changes, update the log row rather than leaving the old card in place.
- 2026-06-27 USER DIRECTIVE - EVERY-SPORT PRESS-CONFERENCE / TEAM-REP PLAYSTYLE GATE: before ranking any serious card, search for current pre-match coach, captain, player, selector, manager, or official team-representative comments from official club/league sites, press-conference videos/transcripts, accredited media, and official social/video mirrors. Extract whether the comments imply a more attacking, defensive, conservative, aggressive, high-tempo, low-tempo, selection-experiment, youth-development, rest-management, chase/defend, press/transition, stoppage/territory, set-piece, bullpen/rotation, or phase-specific approach compared with previous games. Classify each comment as TACTICAL SIGNAL / AVAILABILITY SIGNAL / MOTIVATION SIGNAL / PR-NOISE / UNKNOWN, name the speaker and source, and state whether it supports or conflicts with the rolling-stat form anchor. If no current comments are found, write PRESS SIGNAL: UNKNOWN and cap confidence on totals, spreads, and game-script picks that depend on style. Post-match coach/player comments must be checked in retrospectives to explain whether the pregame style read was right, wrong, hidden, or contradicted by execution. Do not let L5/L10 trends carry a #1 total or spread unless either the broader L15/L20/season baselines agree or a current press/role/selection/tactical mechanism explains the short-window change.
- Never present L5/L10/L15/L20 in isolation. Compare each decision-driving rolling statistic with:
  (a) current season or current competition average;
  (b) current calendar-year average when materially different from the competition season;
  (c) historical team baseline at the same level, venue or role when available;
  (d) player career average and relevant current-role/season average when evaluating players.
- Print or log the comparison as: STAT | L5 | L10 | L15 | L20 | SEASON | YEAR | CAREER/HISTORICAL | d5 | d10 | FORM VERDICT.
- Calculate d5 and d10 against the most relevant baseline. State whether the evidence indicates acceleration, decline, stable form, regression risk, role change, opponent/schedule distortion or insufficient sample.
- Use participation-aware denominators. Player per-game trends must be checked against minutes, starts, innings, plate appearances, overs, snaps, possessions or other sport-relevant opportunity. Do not label a player "in form" from per-game output if the change is mainly caused by playing-time growth unless that role growth is itself expected to continue.
- Match the baseline to the market. Examples: quarter/half scoring against season quarter/half scoring; pitcher recent ERA/WHIP/K-BB against season and career starter/relief baselines; football goals/xG against season and historical level; cricket powerplay/death rates against season/year/career phase rates.
- If season, year or career/historical comparison is unavailable, mark it `MISSING` rather than silently substituting a different scope. Team-level season/year data should normally be obtainable and its absence must reduce confidence.
- The final ranking must identify which window is the FORM ANCHOR and why it deserves more weight than the other windows and baselines. Short windows cannot override the season/career baseline without a concrete mechanism such as availability, role, tactical, venue, schedule or skill change.
- Retrospectives must compare the realised result with both the short-window signal and the longer baseline, then identify whether the miss came from overreacting to recent form, underreacting to a real change, or using the wrong baseline.

2026-06-23 GENERAL SETTLEMENT RULE - HALF-POINT RESULT FRAGILITY:
- A pick that wins by only 0.5 at the supplied threshold is a correct settlement but weak calibration evidence. Log it as a win and separately tag the projection as fragile/near-line; do not convert it into a broad rule without supporting repeat evidence.
- When both a side and total win by 0.5 in the same game, review the realised phase path before claiming the model was strongly right. Galil 89-84 produced a five-point cover at -4.5 and a 173-point under at 173.5, but its 90-point first half contradicted the slow-start premise.

2026-06-23 SOCCER / WORLD CUP PHASE-FULL REPEAT - ARGENTINA 2, AUSTRIA 0:
- Argentina-Austria confirms that 1H Over 0.5 and full Under 2.5 can be the strongest paired outcomes when the favourite owns both early scoring routes and match-control/clean-sheet quality.
- Do not automatically stack full Over 2.5 behind an early-goal lean. If the opponent creates little on target and the favourite can protect possession/territory, the second goal may arrive late without producing a third.

2026-06-23 BASEBALL / MLB ROOKIE-SAMPLE AND LATE-BULLPEN CORRECTION - COLORADO 3, BOSTON 2:
- Jake Bennett entered with only 13 strikeouts in 20.2 MLB innings, then struck out nine over six scoreless innings at Coors. Four-start MLB samples are too small to hard-cap a young pitcher's strikeout ceiling. Compare minor-league/career pitch traits, swinging-strike indicators and opponent matchup before treating low MLB K rate as stable.
- Separate starter projection from exact-winner projection. Boston's starter and defence controlled the game for eight innings, but Aroldis Chapman allowed three runs without recording an out in the ninth. A strong starter/under read can coexist with a wrong favourite ML when the underdog +1.5 protects one-inning bullpen volatility.
- Coors does not require a high-scoring game: strong starter execution can suppress eight innings, while altitude/contact can still amplify one decisive late cluster. Model inning-cluster volatility separately from total-run expectation.

2026-06-23 BASKETBALL / WNBA ROLE-CONCENTRATION CORRECTION - DALLAS 112, SEATTLE 110 OT:
- A low first half does not validate a full-game under. Dallas-Seattle had 82 at halftime but reached 192 in regulation and 222 after overtime. Recalculate the full-game projection from halftime rotations, shooting quality, foul environment and available high-usage scorers; do not carry the pregame under forward mechanically.
- When both teams lose major defenders, net the absences symmetrically. Seattle missing Magbegor raised Dallas paint efficiency; Dallas missing Alanna Smith and Alysha Clark raised Seattle frontcourt, free-throw and three-point efficiency. Counting Seattle's defensive loss but Dallas's offensive losses created a one-sided availability verdict.
- Team L10/L15 averages can be stale after role concentration. Compare them with available-player L5/L10 deltas: Hiedeman and Malonga were already above longer baselines before producing 21 and 37, while Dallas retained Bueckers/Fudd/Shepard creation. If healthy players are absorbing vacated usage, lift the full-game ceiling even when team-level longer windows are low.
- Direct H2H must pass an availability/role compatibility test. The prior 79-56 Dallas win was not a sufficient anchor once the rematch removed key defenders and redistributed minutes and usage.
- Overtime was not the cause of the over; regulation total was already 192. Retrospectives must separate regulation model failure from OT tail amplification.

2026-06-23 BASKETBALL / WNBA PREGAME APPLICATION - DALLAS AT SEATTLE:
- When a direct current-season H2H is dramatically below every threshold (26 Q1, 61 halftime, 135 final), use it as a matchup anchor but stress-test current availability before treating it as deterministic.
- Missing rim protection can raise the opponent's scoring ceiling without automatically lifting the full game over. Seattle losing Ezi Magbegor materially improves Dallas interior efficiency, but Seattle's own depleted frontcourt/secondary creation and 73.6 L10 scoring average still support the high full-game under.
- On exact-complement phase cards, use separate phase projections. Dallas-Seattle's Q1 evidence was near 41.5 and therefore only a modest under, while the 170.5 full-game under had greater separation from the L10/L15 Seattle total environment. Do not assign equal confidence to Q1, half and full unders merely because they point in the same direction.
- Available-player rolling production must be netted by role: Dallas retained Bueckers, Fudd, Ogunbowale and Shepard despite four outs; Seattle's three outs removed its best rim protector plus wing/guard depth. Count the quality and function of the missing players, not the raw number of absences.

2026-06-24 CRICKET / WT20I SETTLEMENT SWEEP - IRELAND 130/5 VS SRI LANKA, AUSTRALIA 199/7 VS PAKISTAN:
- Ireland-Sri Lanka reinforced the wicket-gated under rule: Ireland were 30/3 after six and 130/5 after 20. When a batting side with limited lower-order acceleration loses three top-order wickets inside the powerplay, short square boundaries and one senior batter's recovery innings are not enough to treat 40+ powerplay or 134+ innings paths as likely.
- Australia-Pakistan exposed the opposite elite-ceiling problem. Australia lost Mooney first ball but still reached 64/1 in the powerplay and 199/7 because Perry/Voll rebuilt at boundary pace, the middle/death order kept hitting, and Pakistan leaked 21 extras. Do not assume one early wicket kills an Australia/India/England women innings over; require sustained dot pressure, two or more early wickets, or a confirmed difficult surface.

India followed 170/6 in the opener with only 134/6 and a 38-run powerplay after Nidhi Mahto moved to the bench and the scoring profile slowed. Direct same-series ceiling evidence is useful, but before ranking a full-innings over top, confirm the same batting core, pitch/venue average conflict, and powerplay intent; if the PP projection is only low-40s, keep the full-over confidence capped.
- At 190s WT20I lines for Australia women, do not rank both powerplay under and full-innings under above their complements when toss intent, batting-first venue profile, recent 200+ ceiling, tournament powerplay rate and deep middle/death batting all point to a plausible 195-205 path. If the actual pitch report is UNKNOWN, confidence should be capped, not automatically pushed toward the under.

2026-06-24 SOCCER / THIN LOWER-LEAGUE TOTALS - BUENOS AIRES CITY 1, CONTROL ORIENTADO 2:
- Tiny-sample home under profiles are fragile when confirmed lineups, injury news and chance quality are unavailable. Buenos Aires City-Control Orientado finished 1-2 after a 0-1 halftime despite the home side's prior low-scoring trend.
- If the away side has repeated 2-1 road states or a credible three-goal tail, keep full Over 2.5 adjacent to Under 2.5 rather than forcing it into the bottom slot. A 0-0 state after only a few live minutes does not materially settle a first-half under without reliable live chance data.

2026-06-24 SOCCER / WORLD CUP FAVOURITE REBOUND TAIL - PORTUGAL 5, UZBEKISTAN 0:
- A favourite's poor opener xG or shot count should be separated into chance-creation failure versus finishing/selection failure. Portugal's opener was sterile, but confirmed attacking quality plus urgency against a debutant defence created a rebound tail that produced 3-0 by halftime and 5-0 full time.
- When full Under 2.5 and Over 2.5 are near coinflip in a World Cup group mismatch, do not put the under above the over unless the under mechanism is clearly stronger than "favourite controls game after scoring." If the same favourite also has a strong first-half goal route, a multi-goal first-half can invalidate the full-under thesis very quickly.

2026-06-24 USER DIRECTIVE - ODDS/LINES ALLOWED AS SUPPORTING CONTEXT:
- The standing default is now: betting lines, odds and market movement may be checked and referenced as supporting context unless the user explicitly says not to use them for that query.
- Odds/lines are not the primary model. They must not distract from the sports-doc research sequence: game state, ruleset, lineups, injuries/availability, player and unit quality, form, venue, weather, pitch/surface, phase splits, model output, stress tests, settlement rules and prior retrospectives.
- Use market context mainly to sanity-check probabilities, identify consensus disagreement, detect stale assumptions, and decide when to re-research. Never copy a pick from odds alone, never let price replace evidence, and do not provide staking/P&L/CLV advice unless the user explicitly asks for execution tracking.
